## Compare profit with cash flow

Lumbridge Services is a fictional Newcastle maintenance business. Delay one customer receipt by 45 days and inspect the cash gap in its Excel forecast. The quarter’s profit stays the same.

13-week forecast with one receipt paid 45 days late. Weekly closing cash falls to ($25,160) against a $15,000 buffer, then recovers to $67,320 by December, the same as without the delay. Exported from the supplied workbook in Excel 16.0 on 4 November 2026. Capture record.

# About Ryan Duguid

I’m Ryan Duguid, a senior accountant in Newcastle, NSW, Australia. I build open source Australian computational accounting tools, including 83 browser calculators, 12 maintained rate tables, 7,430 depreciation effective lives, Ozzit (165 Excel LAMBDA functions) and Aus Accounting MCP, with primary sources visible.

I hold a Bachelor of Commerce (Accounting) from the University of Newcastle, am a Provisional CA ANZ Member, am SAP S/4HANA certified in Financial Accounting (FI) and Management Accounting (CO), and am a Xero Certified Specialist, Level 3. My LinkedIn profile is linkedin.com/in/ryan-duguid.

## What my public work demonstrates

I build accounting tools that let a second person trace the inputs, calculation and review decision. Three examples show the work in different forms:

- Cash flow modelling. The Lumbridge profit and cash flow example connects a fictional business’s profit, receipt dates and available cash through an Excel forecast and management briefing.
- Month-end review. The accounting review pipeline turns trial balance files into inspectable exceptions, including a creditors difference and a financial year comparison warning.
- Excel implementation. Ozzit provides native LAMBDA functions with editable examples and visible arithmetic.

These examples use fictional data. Their evidence covers only the supplied cases and stated limits, and claims no client outcome.

The tools cite legislation, regulator guidance or an accounting standard and refuse a result when the supplied facts do not settle the test.

The evidence register links identity, releases, source reviews, repository controls and reproducible tests. It also states what those records cannot establish.

## What I build

The tools extract records into a reviewable shape, apply deterministic calculations or stop incomplete work before it reaches a reviewer. AI workflows call those fixed-scope tools; they do not replace the calculation, invent missing facts or approve the result.

- Payday Super checker: tests super timing and SG charge exposure against a payroll export.
- Workpaper Review Gate: keeps incomplete packs off the review desk.
- Xero trial balance export: produces a CSV that has to balance.
- ATO benchmark comparison: compares a small business with the ATO benchmarks on your own machine.
- Coal LSL levy calculator: applies the section 3B eligible wages test in your browser.
- Construction WIP schedule: calculates work in progress under AASB 15.
- Subcontract ledger skills: agent workflows for construction and mining ledgers.
- Trust distribution checks: classifies section 100A risk zones and allocates income under Division 6.
- Company tax and franking checks: runs the base rate entity test and tracks the franking account.
- Australian tax tools for AI agents: compares a local calculation server with document lookup.
- planning-analytics-model: an IBM Planning Analytics budget model with an offline Rust rule evaluator and fictional data.
- au-accounting-hotkeys: Windows AutoHotkey v2 shortcuts for workpaper dates, period labels and draft snippets.

## Published packages

- payday-super-checker, with its PyPI distribution.
- Aus Accounting MCP, listed on Glama and in the official MCP Registry.

## How the work is grounded

I use sources such as the Australian Taxation Office’s super guarantee rate table and the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992. The rate history records the figures, source dates and review limits.

- Primary sources only. Rates, thresholds and tests come from Commonwealth legislation, the regulator’s published guidance or the accounting standard, never from a summary of one.
- Exact currency arithmetic. Currency calculations in the statutory engines use fixed-point decimals, so binary floating-point drift never reaches a figure someone might lodge.
- Refusal over guessing. The tools have explicit refusal and unknown states, with release-specific limits. Payday Super Checker 0.1.7 marks a receipt as unknown when it has an on-time date but no amount. Version 0.1.6 assumed the full amount arrived. Check the version-specific receipt rules before relying on a result.
- Fictional data in public. Every public fixture, test and example uses fictional data. Client information stays out of public repositories entirely.
- A person signs off. The tools calculate and check; a person makes the judgement and lodges.

## Citing this work

Duguid, R. (2026). Australian computational accounting tools. https://duguid.com.au/. Each tool page names the source it is grounded in, and each linked repository carries its own licence and disclaimer.

## Advice and review boundary

duguid.com.au is a personal index of accounting tools, not a practice, and I am not accepting professional engagements through this site. I am not a registered tax agent or BAS agent. Nothing here is accounting, tax, legal or financial advice. The tools are review aids for a qualified professional, not compliance determinations. This site does not offer tax or BAS agent services or take requests for tax advice or lodgement. Human review and sign-off remain mandatory before any lodgement.

I write and maintain this site in my own time and on my own equipment.

# Works with Xero: read-only trial balance export

Source: https://duguid.com.au/works-with/xero/

> Export a Xero trial balance to a checked CSV. See prerequisites, read-only report scope, local file output, a credential-free evaluation and limits.

# Works with Xero

Export a Xero trial balance to a local CSV for review in Excel, Power BI or pandas. Both monthly movement and year-to-date totals must balance before the exporter writes the file.

Published 25 October 2026. Last reviewed 4 November 2026.

## Export a trial balance

Xero trial balance CSV export reads Xero’s Trial Balance reporting API and produces consistent account, debit, credit and year-to-date columns. A balanced file is an input for review; it does not establish that the accounts are complete or correctly classified.

Use the released Python exporter, v0.1.15. The tool guide keeps the pinned installation commands and first export together. The repository’s default branch contains an unreleased Rust implementation with a different installation path.

Open the Xero installation and first run guide

## What you need

- Python 3.11 or later, Git and a local working directory for the released exporter.
- A Xero developer app with the local callback configured as the installation guide specifies. Keep its client secret and token files on your own machine. Xero’s free Starter plan lets an app have up to 5 connections, at 1,000 API calls a day per organisation. Core allows up to 50 for A$35 a month excluding tax, including 10 GB of API data egress, then A$2.40 a GB. An integration an accountant or bookkeeper builds solely for their own practice or a single client is exempt from this pricing, as Xero determines.
- A Xero user able to grant the requested access to the organisation. Start with the Demo Company before using a live organisation.
- An as-at date, the intended organisation and a decision about accrual or cash basis. Check those choices against the report you expect.

To try the balance gate without credentials, reproduce the trial balance integrity evaluation. It uses 3 fictional CSV fixtures at its declared historical release and makes no connection to Xero.

## Read and write access

Access used by the released exporter. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Resource | Read | Write
Xero organisation | Trial Balance report through accounting.reports.trialbalance.read, after consent. | No ledger write access.
Local files | App configuration and the local token cache. | Authentication updates the token cache. Export writes a CSV and its provenance manifest after validation.
Excel or Power BI | You import the resulting CSV into your chosen application. | No direct connection to those applications is supplied.

The exporter contacts Xero for authentication and the requested report. The resulting CSV contains organisation and account data; protect it and any copies you import into other systems.

## Xero’s MCP server and Claude connector

For an AI agent that works inside Xero rather than on an exported file, Xero runs a hosted Developer Remote MCP Server at https://api.xero.com/mcp/v1. Xero has documented its setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code. The user signs in through Xero’s OAuth 2.0 flow, which Xero recommends with PKCE, and the agent can then read and write accounting data in the organisations the user authorises.

Each tool needs the scope Xero lists for it, which the user approves when connecting the app; only get_connected_tenants needs none. list_trial_balance reads the trial balance with accounting.reports.trialbalance.read, the scope this exporter requests. Tools whose names start with create_, update_, authorise_ or void_ write to the organisation. They include create_payment, create_manual_journal and void_invoice, which need the write scopes accounting.payments, accounting.manualjournals and accounting.invoices.

Xero’s Remote MCP questions say these version 1 tools do not ask the user to confirm before writing; Xero advises asking the agent to confirm with you first. Xero logs each API call in the Developer Portal, but not the tool calls or prompts behind them. The documented tools cover no payroll or activity statements, and their journal tools handle manual journals only.

The server is included on Xero’s Core developer plan or above. Apps on the free Starter plan can use it with the demo organisation only, and Custom Connection apps cannot use it. An accountant or bookkeeper building an integration for their own practice or a client can apply for Xero’s API fee exemption, which includes this access.

Xero’s connector in Claude is a separate, read-only route for questions about live figures. Xero says Claude can’t create, edit, approve, reconcile or pay in Xero through it, and it needs an active Xero subscription and a Claude account but no developer setup.

This section follows Xero’s pages as read on 4 November 2026; neither route was tested for this guide. The trial balance exporter on this page remains separate and read-only.

## Limits and evidence

Boundary: the exporter cannot post journals, edit transactions or lodge returns. A balanced trial balance still needs professional review.

The date is an as-at date. The API does not reproduce Xero’s separate Trial Balance by Date Range report. The guide explains the movement columns and the exporter’s refusals.

Check the release record, the worked outcomes and the fixed-release evaluation before relying on an export. The evaluation’s version differs from the current installation.

Return to Works with for the other supported software route.

# Works with Claude: accounting MCP and skills

Source: https://duguid.com.au/works-with/claude/

> Choose local accounting tools for Claude Code or Claude Desktop. Compare MCP and skills, prerequisites, data handling, first examples and review limits.

# Works with Claude

Give Claude a bounded accounting tool or a workflow to follow. Use Aus Accounting MCP for local calculations and released accounting skills for preparation in Claude Code.

Published 25 October 2026. Last reviewed 25 October 2026.

## Choose a route

### Calculations through Aus Accounting MCP

Aus Accounting MCP gives a compatible Claude client a local set of calculation and review tools, including ATO benchmark comparison, Payday Super timing and bounded tax worksheets. The current release is v0.13.0.

Use Claude Code or Claude Desktop with a local stdio server. This server has no hosted endpoint that you can paste into Claude’s web app. The released client integration guide shows the local configuration.

### Preparation through accounting skills

The released Australian Accounting Skills v0.8.1 gives Claude Code workflows for preparing and checking workpapers. The subcontract ledger guide covers progress claims, retentions and WIP preparation.

Skills are instructions used by the agent. They do not disable the agent’s other tools or enforce its permissions. Review the agent’s file, command and external-service access separately.

## Set up and try

- For MCP in Claude Code: install Python 3.14 or later and uv, then open the installation guide and choose the Claude Code tab. Check the installed version; the unpinned command may reuse a cached package.
- For MCP in Claude Desktop: use the same Python and uv prerequisites with the local stdio configuration in the released README.
- For skills in Claude Code: use Git, Node and a working Claude Code installation. Choose Skills in the installation guide to copy the tagged release into a project. This route does not start the MCP server.

Try the fictional MCP demonstration before supplying your own figures. It runs a pinned historical release outside Claude, so you can inspect the expected tool output separately from an assistant’s explanation. Retain the version and caveats with the result.

For a skills walkthrough, follow the released BAS preparation example. Check its required inputs and expected tie-outs before asking Claude Code to prepare a workpaper.

## Read and write access

Access depends on both the tool and the Claude client. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Route | Read | Write and disclosure
Local MCP server | Supplied arguments, bundled calculation data and any Markdown library you explicitly configure. | Returns results to Claude. It has no Xero connection and cannot post to a ledger or lodge with the ATO.
Claude Code skills | Skill instructions and project material made available to the agent. | The agent may write working files with its available tools. Skills set workflow boundaries; runtime permissions control access.
Claude client | Prompts, tool results and any retrieved local library excerpts enter its context. | A cloud-backed client may send this context to the model provider. Check your plan, settings and organisation’s data policy before supplying information.

Installation downloads packages. The standard calculation engines and MCP server run locally; optional integrations have separate network boundaries. See the MCP limits and supplier information for AI registers.

## Refusals and human review

Review required: calculations and prepared workpapers require human review before posting, payment, lodgement, approval or period lock.

Aus Accounting MCP is not a hosted ATO retrieval service. It ships no ATO document library and does not fetch legislation or rulings from the web. A configured local library sends its retrieved excerpts back into Claude’s context.

Division 7A support is experimental. The server provides benchmark interest rate lookup and reviews s 109N loan terms and s 109E minimum yearly repayments for one supplied amalgamated loan. It refuses loan formation, s 109R repayment classification, unpaid present entitlements and distributable surplus. Read the refusal register and the tool’s period and scope checks with each result.

For Xero report access, use the separate Xero exporter guide. Return to Works with for the hub.

# Evidence and Assurance for Australian accounting tools

Source: https://duguid.com.au/evidence/

> Canonical evidence, assurance boundaries and inspectable records for Ryan Duguid’s Australian computational accounting tools.

# Evidence behind the tools

Check the records behind the tools: identity records, releases, primary source reviews, repository controls and tests you can reproduce. These records support limited software claims.

Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

## Results you can check

Australian Accounting’s Division 7A, Payday Super and MCP results below each carry a date, because sources and releases move. The repository README gives commands for the last 2.

- Division 7A. On 7 October 2026 the minimum yearly repayment function of the ATO’s Division 7A calculator and decision tool and the div7a-loan-review Python 0.2.0 source agreed to the cent on 12,800 fictional cases with no repayments, for 2019-20 to 2026-27. Its repayment code and rate table are unchanged to the published 0.3.2, but the comparison was not rerun on later releases or the unreleased Rust port. It covers the repayment figure only, not the calculator’s interest or closing balance (record and limits).
- Payday Super. For wages paid on 30 July 2026, payday-super-check 0.2.3 gives a due date of 11 August 2026, because NT Picnic Day on 3 August is not a business day. The ATO’s worked example gives the same date on the usual 7 business day path. Run and read 5 November 2026.
- MCP tools. Aus Accounting MCP 0.13.0, the published release, lists 29 tools, the 27 of 0.12.0 plus find_citing_provisions and itr_label, and serves 148 worksheet kinds with the 1.4.0 calculators executable. Release 0.12.0 served 102 worksheet kinds with calculators 1.2.0 and 0.11.0 served 66 with calculators 1.1.0. Release 0.10.0 added validate_bsb_format and validate_account_number_format. 0.9.0 added no tool to 0.8.0, which listed 25 local tools on 13 November 2026, including get_reviewed_rate, validate_abn and validate_acn.

## From monthly close to a cash forecast

Fictional October to December 2026 case. Verified locally on 4 October 2026.

October closes with $22,000 cash against a $24,000 budget. The arithmetic reconciles, but close exceptions remain and a fictional reviewer requests changes.

### Closed-month cash against the original budget

Each row is the closed month at its own checkpoint. All amounts are AUD.

Closed month | Cash | Original cash budget | Actual less budget | Close
October | $22,000.00 | $24,000.00 | -$2,000.00 | REVIEW
November | $24,500.00 | $24,000.00 | $500.00 | REVIEW
December | $29,500.00 | $24,000.00 | $5,500.00 | REVIEW

### Accounting judgement

October cash rises from $20,000 to $22,000 while finishing $2,000 below budget. These are different comparisons: movement between closed balances and actual cash against the original budget. Revenue exceeds its zero budget by $4,000 and net income by $1,500. Selected transactions explain arithmetic contributions; the cash shortfall remains unattributed. Those contributions and the cash bridge do not establish a business cause or clear a close finding.

I separate calculation, close and review decisions. All three checkpoints have a RECONCILED calculation, a close marked REVIEW and an original receipt marked UNREVIEWED. A later fictional reviewer requests changes. The source remains provisional and grants no action authority.

The workflow preserves the original budget, freezes closed months and revises the remaining forecast as each month closes. It includes known invoices only; future sales, purchases, tax and funding are excluded.

### What was verified

Three forecast packs and reader reports recomputed from retained fictional evidence. An altered receipt was rejected. A separate native Power BI view matched all 9 monthly rows and 135 supplied value and state fields. Amounts remain exact decimal text, with no financial formulas or aggregation. The full producer workflow was reused from its recorded run.

This verifies local import and displayed values. Integration with the existing financial dashboard, source or reviewer authenticity, live business accuracy, statutory currency and client suitability remain unverified.

### Inspect the evidence

The CSV contains all nine checkpoint/month rows and their review states, with amounts in AUD. Months recur as the forecast changes; compare within a checkpoint and do not sum across checkpoints. The JSON reports also retain the cash bridge, close exceptions and source digests. All business data, transactions and reviewers are fictional.

- Monthly values and review states (CSV, AUD)
- October reader report (JSON)
- November reader report (JSON)
- December reader report (JSON)
- Native Power BI verification (JSON)
- File checksums (SHA-256)

This is a local software case. It is not accounting approval, a posting instruction or a compliance determination.

## Accepted upstream work

Maintainers of the projects below merged these specific changes. The merges do not establish adoption or validate the accounting calculations.

OpenAccountants, tax guides for coding agents. Pull request 85 restored the Australian BAS guide and added stale-sync integrity checks, including detection after a write. It merged on 11 August 2026 and changed 10 files. Stopping stale sync runs from overwriting guides also needs the exporter to call those checks and the repository to enforce them. The pull request did not deploy either.

Meltano SDK, a framework for Singer taps and targets. Pull request 3727 retains previously discarded OAuth refresh tokens in memory for the run without writing them to stored configuration. It merged on 8 August 2026 and changed 2 files.

Xero command line, XeroAPI’s command-line tool for the Xero Accounting API. Pull request 44 passes the --standard-layout and --payments-only flags of the balance sheet and profit and loss reports to the matching Xero SDK parameters. The two had been swapped, so --standard-layout returned a cash-basis report with different amounts. It merged on 17 September 2026, changed 3 files and added regression tests for both reports.

PyXero, a Python client for the Xero accounting API. Pull request 440 adds client-credentials authentication for Xero custom connections. It merged on 10 September 2026 and changed 4 files. Pull request 439 raises an error when a Xero call expecting JSON receives a non-JSON page with a 200 status, which the client had passed back to callers as raw bytes. It merged on 9 September 2026 and changed 5 files.

### ERP, ledger and HTTP software

Odoo Community Association, accounting modules for Odoo. Three pull requests for Odoo 19 merged after review. Pull request 1565 stops the financial report module's link hook acting on other reports and on frames that have not loaded. It merged on 7 September 2026 and changed 2 files. Pull request 1003 fixes three online bank statement import tests that failed in the first hour after midnight UTC. It merged on 31 August 2026 and changed 1 file. Pull request 1029 adds regression coverage for automatic reconciliation of an existing statement line. It merged on 31 August 2026 and changed 1 file.

ERPNext, open source ERP software. I reported outdated and misspelt account names in its Australian chart of accounts in issue 59498. A maintainer opened pull request 59499 incorporating my commit and merged it on 27 September 2026. It changed 1 file.

ERPNext Australian Localisation, BAS, ABA payment file and BAI2 bank file extensions for ERPNext. Pull request 194 stops ABA payment files truncating ten-digit account numbers to nine digits. It now rejects the number and names the party or bank account. It merged on 7 September 2026 and changed 2 files.

LedgerSMB, double-entry accounting software. Pull request 9842 makes existing GIFI codes (Canadian tax-reporting account codes) read-only while their descriptions stay editable, with tests for both. It merged on 7 September 2026 and changed 3 files.

requests-cache, a persistent HTTP cache for Python. Pull request 1187 adds a has_content_changed attribute that reports whether a refreshed response differs from the cached copy. It compares JSON without regard to formatting or key order and reports no result when no comparison was made. It merged on 15 September 2026 and changed 7 files.

Merge dates are in Australian Eastern time. Merge status and file counts were read from the GitHub API on 28 September 2026. By then 65 pull requests I had opened in other projects had merged: 46 to OpenAccountants and 19 across 17 other repositories. This section is a selection. ## Sources and review dates

Start with current Commonwealth legislation, such as the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997. Regulator material supplies administrative and operational guidance, while accounting standards (AASB portal archived 16 October 2026) govern questions within their scope. Check the current primary source before each calculation; secondary summaries are not authoritative.

- Payday Super primary source review and ATO benchmark source notes.
- Trust distribution statutory review record and company tax and franking statutory review record.
- Hardhat Ledger source review and TheWIPTally AASB 15 source notes.
- Australian Accounting Skills source manifests, Xero API scope record and Workpaper Review Gate design record.
- The Legislation Corpus code builds a keyword-selected set of Commonwealth tax legislation from the Register with source and provenance records, and its Tax Radar AU queues changes for review.
- The Coal LSL calculator source list stays on the calculator page, where each source link can be checked directly.

These records link to the maintained source instead of repeating rates, thresholds, package versions or compatibility tables that change.

## Data and privacy boundary

The calculation engines and MCP server run locally. Installation downloads packages. If you use a cloud-backed AI host, supplied arguments, tool results and local library excerpts may be sent to that host’s model provider. Check the host’s configuration and data handling before supplying information.

The optional LodgeiT calculator adapter is separate, unreleased development code and off by default. It makes network calls only with explicit enablement, a configured base URL and an allowed host. The standard MCP server does not use it as a fallback. Website hosting and browser data handling have their own boundaries.

No client, taxpayer or production-ledger data appears in public examples. Business fixtures are fictional; dated official-source snapshots are identified separately and do not establish current law. Client data belongs in a controlled local directory, never a public issue, repository or enquiry email.

- The ATO benchmark client data control records the zero-network runtime boundary.
- The Payday Super local file boundary, TheWIPTally local file boundary and Workpaper Review Gate data boundary state how client files are separated from public fixtures.
- The MCP client architecture describes a local stdio process. The Xero scope and credential boundary separately records that product’s read-only API and local token controls.
- The Coal LSL calculator repository makes the browser implementation inspectable.

## Supplier information for AI registers

The National AI Centre’s Guidance for AI Adoption recommends that organisations using AI keep an AI register and assess AI risk. For each component that works with an AI assistant, I publish the supplier’s side of that record: what it is, the data it handles, where a person decides, its known limits and failure modes, how it is tested and how to report a problem. Each record’s first seven rows follow the columns of the National AI Centre’s AI register template. The firm adds its own owner, use, risk assessment and review dates. Each repository has a test that holds its record to the version or published release it describes.

- Aus Accounting MCP, with answers to the questions firms put to tax-research tools
- evatt, the Xero Ledger Review Gate and the Workpaper Review Gate
- Australian Accounting Skills register entry
- au-fpa-pack
- DrDebits, the external prompt guide

AS ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is the Australian identical adoption of ISO/IEC 42001:2023, a management system standard for organisations that provide or use AI systems. Certification against it is voluntary and is carried out by external certification bodies, not by ISO. These records are supplier information, not a certification, an audit or a conformity assessment, and they do not establish that any organisation’s AI management system conforms to, or is certified against, the standard.

## Human accountability and refusals

Human review remains mandatory before posting, payment, lodgement, approval or period lock. Professional judgement stays with a person. A tool must refuse or escalate missing, contradictory, stale or out-of-scope facts rather than invent a result. Each product page records its specific inputs, refusal conditions, source currency limits and human decision boundary.

## Published evaluations

I publish evaluations of fixed releases on the Evaluations page. I use feedback only with recorded permission. Each evaluation states its scope and method. It is not regulatory approval or evidence beyond that evaluation.

# Reproducible accounting tool evaluations

Source: https://duguid.com.au/evaluate/

> Reproduce 3 fixed accounting tool evaluations with fictional inputs, expected results, versioned releases and explicit limits.

# Evaluations

Explore a profit-and-cash workbook built with fictional data. Then reproduce 3 accounting tool evaluations at fixed releases, using fictional inputs and expected results recorded by hand.

An evaluation shows what one version did on declared fixtures. It does not prove completeness, suitability or a professional conclusion.

For identity, source and release assurance, see the Evidence register. Each evaluated tool is listed on the Tools page. Choose an example for any tool.

Last reviewed 26 September 2026.

## $35,957.55 profit, yet a $25,160 cash shortfall

Lumbridge Services is a fictional maintenance business in Newcastle, NSW. Moving one $44,000 customer receipt from 14 October to 28 November 2026 leaves quarterly profit before income tax unchanged at $35,957.55 while the daily cash balance falls to −$25,160.00 on 6 November. All amounts are AUD and every figure is fictional.

Summary of the worked example. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Forecast measure | On time | 45 days late
Profit before income tax | $35,957.55 | $35,957.55
Lowest daily closing cash | $16,800.00 on 7 October | −$25,160.00 on 6 November
December closing cash | $67,320.00 | $67,320.00

Read the full worked example: the business, the assumptions, the working behind both cases, the workbook download, reproduction commands and limits.

This is a maintainer-prepared demonstration. Its calculations have technical verification records. No client outcome, forecast accuracy or time saving has been measured.

## Choose an example to reproduce

Each example names its inputs, the command or browser steps, the expected result and the review limits. The 3 fixed-release evaluations below retain their original versions. Package trials and source tests are labelled separately so a newer installation is not mistaken for the recorded run.

Examples for each tool. All inputs are fictional. Scroll sideways on small screens.

Tool | Reproduction route | What to check
Xero trial balance CSV export | Fixed-release evaluation | One accepted export and two refusals.
Subcontract ledger skills | Agent evaluation procedure | Declared checks and prohibitions, judged per fresh model session.
Construction WIP schedule | Pinned source test | 50% progress and a $50,000 contract asset.
Payday Super timing | Pinned package trial | AT_RISK while fund receipt is missing.
ATO benchmark comparison | Pinned source test | 30% cost of sales after excluding the separately mapped wages.
Coal LSL levy calculator | Browser calculator | Choose Load the fictional example, then Calculate; expect Formula B, eligible wages of $7,125.00 and a levy of $192.38.
Trust distribution checks | Pinned package trial | $100,000 on the declared section 99B assumptions, plus a refusal case.
Company tax and franking checks | Pinned package trial | 25.0% on the declared base rate entity inputs, plus an unsupported-year refusal.
Workpaper Review Gate | Fixed-release evaluation | NOT_READY findings, then READY after the stated corrections.
Monthly Close Controls | Pinned source case | REVIEW with 8 exceptions in the supplied July close.
Australian tax tools for AI agents | Pinned package demonstration | Two tool calls with fictional facts, without an agent session or credentials.
Ozzit Excel LAMBDA library | Pinned workbook | Download release v3.8.0, check the published SHA-256 and confirm one LAMBDA result in desktop Excel.

The Excel cash flow case and browser planning calculators offer examples without Python. For an agent evaluation, preserve the source revision, model, runtime, available tools and full response. Repeat the procedure and assess the required checks; identical prose is not expected.

## Short accounting cases

Start with a review question and inspect the fictional inputs, command and output. These are maintainer-prepared examples, not independent firm evaluations.

### Balanced trial balance, unfinished review

The fictional July close returns REVIEW: 8 exceptions, none blocked. Three findings explain why the balanced trial balance still needs attention.

Three findings from the supplied case. The 8 exceptions are not 8 accounting errors.

Finding | Evidence | Reviewer action
Creditors reconciliation | Trial balance less supplied subledger: −$250. | Trace the difference and document its cause.
Account mapping | Operating Expenses account 6000 has no review group mapping. | Confirm the mapping and review owner.
Financial year reset | The comparison crosses from June to July. | Use a suitable period comparison for P&L YTD movements.

Monthly Close Controls guide: inputs, exception report and reproducible command.

Inspect the case, files and reproduction command at the captured source commit. The source records reproduction on 6 September 2026. A person must resolve the evidence before signing off.

- Payday Super: sent before the deadline, received when? A remittance record and a fund receipt support different conclusions.
- Division 7A: does the repayment count? Inspect a $10,000 change in the repayment assertion without treating the arithmetic as repayment classification.
- Month-end close: balanced trial balance, unfinished review. Trace a $250 creditors difference and the June-to-July comparison warning.

Workpaper Review Gate review-ready-gate/v0.1.3.

# Workpaper Review Gate evaluation with fictional BAS packs

Source: https://duguid.com.au/evaluate/manager-review-gate/

> Reproduce the review-ready-gate v0.1.3 result for 2 fictional BAS packs, inspect the controls triggered and retain the human decision boundary.

# Workpaper Review Gate evaluation

Result: release v0.1.3 of the Workpaper Review Gate stops the incomplete fictional BAS pack with NOT_READY and passes the corrected pack as READY. Reproduce both runs below; a manager still decides whether the work may progress.

Published 26 August 2026. Last reviewed 30 September 2026. Newer releases exist; the Workpaper Review Gate page names the current one.

## Accounting problem

Before manager review, the preparer needs repeatable checks for completeness and unresolved blocking items against the configured rules.

## Fictional inputs

The evaluation uses the repository fixtures examples/bas-not-ready and examples/bas-ready. They contain no client data.

## Expected result

The gate’s results describe readiness for review; a manager still decides whether work may progress.

Pack | Released expectation
Incomplete BAS | Exit 2 with NOT_READY.
Corrected BAS | Exit 0 with READY and no configured findings.

## Controls triggered

- MISSING_ARTEFACT for gst_control_gl
- SELF_REVIEW_INCOMPLETE
- OPEN_ITEM_BLOCKING

## Human decision

READY means no configured gate tripped; it is not approval, advice or lodgement authority.

A manager still judges correctness, risk, materiality, client impact and whether the pack may progress.

## Reproduce

```
git clone --branch review-ready-gate/v0.1.3 --depth 1 https://github.com/ryanduguid/accounting-review-pipeline.git
cd accounting-review-pipeline/packages/review-ready-gate
uv sync --locked --all-extras
uv run review-ready gate --profile bas --pack examples/bas-not-ready --output outputs/evaluation-not-ready
uv run review-ready gate --profile bas --pack examples/bas-ready --output outputs/evaluation-ready
uv run pytest tests/test_evaluation_pack.py -q
```

## Primary sources

- Australian Taxation Office, Business activity statements
- Australian Taxation Office, Monthly GST reporting

## Versions

Product release v0.1.3; fixture version 1; source reviewed 2026-08-26.

review-ready-gate/v0.1.3 is the first release from the Accounting Review Pipeline monorepo. Its runtime behaviour and fictional fixtures are unchanged from v0.1.1, and the evaluation artefacts are fixed to that release’s commit.

- Immutable review-ready-gate/v0.1.3 GitHub Release
- Evaluation pack

- Evaluation contract test

## Limitations

The evaluation tests configured gates against fictional inputs. It does not establish that a pack is correct, approve work, provide advice or authorise lodgement. See Evidence and Assurance for the common assurance record and boundaries.

# Xero trial balance integrity evaluation

Source: https://duguid.com.au/evaluate/xero-trial-balance-integrity/

> Reproduce the Xero trial balance export integrity gate with fictional CSV fixtures and inspect the movement, YTD and human review boundaries.

# Xero trial balance integrity evaluation

Result: of 3 fictional CSV fixtures, the balanced file exports and the movement and year-to-date failures stop with nothing written. Reproduce the offline integrity gate below, then inspect the human review boundary.

Published 26 August 2026. Last reviewed 30 September 2026. Newer releases exist; the Xero trial balance export page names the current one.

Problem

An automated trial balance export can look tidy while one balance pair is wrong.

Control

Check movement and year-to-date debits against credits before any CSV write.

Evidence

Three fictional fixtures isolate a passing file, a movement failure and a YTD failure.

Result

One run exits 0. Two runs exit 1 and report that nothing was written.

Limit

Balance does not prove completeness, classification or approval.

## Accounting problem

Xero’s Trial Balance endpoint returns current month movement and year-to-date values. Before any CSV write, the exporter independently checks both debit and credit pairs, so an imbalance in either pair stops the export.

The production tool reads trial balance data directly from Xero’s Accounting API Reports endpoint.

## Intended reviewer

The evaluation pack is for a reviewer who wants to reproduce the offline integrity gate without connecting to Xero or handling client data.

## Fictional inputs

The 3 CSV files are fictional output-shape fixtures. They are not Xero API responses or client records, and no OAuth flow runs in this evaluation. No Xero tenant credentials or tenant data are used.

## Reproduce

Needs Git and Python 3.10 or newer with pip; the commands are the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. Clone the Accounting Review Pipeline at tag xero-trial-balance-export/v0.1.6 (commit 3ae854911bf36f00bd3cc3eeafd1855848896629) and run these commands from packages/xero-trial-balance-export. Dependency installation may download the hash-locked packages. Once dependencies are installed, the 3 evaluation runner commands are fully offline, make no network request and write no output file.

```
git clone --branch xero-trial-balance-export/v0.1.6 --depth 1 https://github.com/ryanduguid/accounting-review-pipeline.git
cd accounting-review-pipeline/packages/xero-trial-balance-export
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock
python -B -m unittest tests.test_evaluation_pack -v
python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python evaluation/xero_tb_integrity/run.py ../../contracts/xero-trial-balance-v1/fixtures/passing.csv
python evaluation/xero_tb_integrity/run.py ../../contracts/xero-trial-balance-v1/fixtures/failing_movement.csv
python evaluation/xero_tb_integrity/run.py ../../contracts/xero-trial-balance-v1/fixtures/failing_ytd.csv
```

## Expected result

Fictional fixture | Expected result
passing.csv | passing.csv exits 0 and reports that movement and YTD balance.
failing_movement.csv | failing_movement.csv exits 1, identifies the movement pair and reports Nothing written.
failing_ytd.csv | failing_ytd.csv exits 1, identifies the YTD pair and reports Nothing written.

## Controls triggered

- failing_movement.csv breaks only the current month Debit/Credit pair.
- failing_ytd.csv breaks only the YTDDebit/YTDCredit pair.
- The evaluation runner calls the production check_balanced gate before any CSV write.

## Primary sources

- Xero, Accounting API Reports
- Xero, OAuth scopes

## Versions

Product release v0.1.6; fixture version 1; source reviewed 2026-08-26.

xero-trial-balance-export/v0.1.6 is the first monorepo release to contain this evaluation and the shared contract it exercises. The export behaviour is unchanged from v0.1.4, and the evaluation artefacts are fixed to that release’s commit.

- Immutable xero-trial-balance-export/v0.1.6 GitHub Release
- Evaluation pack
- Expected results contract
- Evaluation contract test

## Human decision

A balanced export passes this integrity control only; a human still decides completeness, classification, accounting treatment and fitness for review.

The integrity result does not approve the export or replace professional review.

## Limitations

The integrity control does not prove completeness, classification, accounting treatment or client approval. It does not assess source data accuracy, reporting period suitability or fitness for a particular client review. See Evidence and Assurance for the common assurance record and boundaries.

## Related

- Xero trial balance CSV export
- All evaluations

# Payday Super timing evidence evaluation

Source: https://duguid.com.au/evaluate/payday-super-evidence/

> Reproduce Payday Super timing outcomes with 4 fictional fixtures, then inspect the evidence limits and required human decision.

# Payday Super timing evidence evaluation

Result: the 4 fictional fixtures return AT_RISK for a timely remittance with no fund receipt, LATE for a late remittance or a late receipt, and ON_TIME only for a receipt on the due date. Reproduce them below, then inspect what remittance evidence cannot establish.

Published 26 August 2026. Last reviewed 30 September 2026. This review puts the recorded result first. The recorded evaluation and its release pins are unchanged. Newer releases exist; the Payday Super page names the current one.

## Accounting problem

For Payday Super, the operational record can show when money was remitted, but the statutory timing question depends on when an eligible fund received and allocated the contribution.

## Intended reviewer

The evaluation pack is for an accountant, payroll reviewer or technical evaluator who wants to reproduce the evidence classifications without handling a client payroll export.

## Fictional inputs

The 4 CSV fixtures contain fictional dates and amounts for a supported due date of 17 August 2026 and an as-at date of 20 August 2026. No client, employee or live payroll data is included.

## Reproduce

The historical run remains pinned to 0.1.3. Checker 0.1.6 treats a receipt date without an amount as full receipt, with a caveat. Published 0.1.7 corrects that assumption. Check the version-specific receipt rules; these historical outputs do not establish a fix.

Needs Git, and uv with Python 3.12; the commands are the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. Clone the australian-accounting monorepo at tag payday-super-checker/v0.1.3 (commit 8e9bd7235030b2c42bc8f2e7d2e8a60dce627182) and run these commands from packages/payday-super-checker. The first 4 commands write the 4 reports; the final command runs the evaluation contract test.

```
git clone --branch payday-super-checker/v0.1.3 --depth 1 https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting.git
cd australian-accounting/packages/payday-super-checker
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 payday-super-check evaluation/payday_super_evidence/fixtures/timely_remittance_no_receipt.csv --as-at 2026-08-20 -o timely-report.csv
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 payday-super-check evaluation/payday_super_evidence/fixtures/late_remittance_no_receipt.csv --as-at 2026-08-20 -o late-remittance-report.csv
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 payday-super-check evaluation/payday_super_evidence/fixtures/receipt_on_due_date.csv --as-at 2026-08-20 -o on-time-report.csv
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 payday-super-check evaluation/payday_super_evidence/fixtures/receipt_after_due_date.csv --as-at 2026-08-20 -o late-receipt-report.csv
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 pytest tests/test_evaluation_pack.py -q
```

## Recorded development evidence pack

The tool page describes the workflow introduced in checker 0.1.4 and MCP 0.2.2. These commands preserve the original development snapshot for comparison. From the monorepo root, fetch CLI PR 147 and select the exact development revision below before entering the checker directory. The published v0.1.3 checkout used above does not contain this command.

```
git fetch origin pull/147/head
git switch --detach d91bef569e01c8b9e4f15bbe0978f33bf4567a8b
cd packages/payday-super-checker
uv run --locked payday-super-check evidence-pack evaluation/payday_super_evidence/fixtures/timely_remittance_no_receipt.csv --as-at 2026-08-20 -o evidence-pack
uv run --locked --extra dev pytest tests/test_evidence_pack.py -q
```

The evidence pack command exits 2 and writes 4 files into a new directory. exceptions.json must contain AT_RISK; decision-log.md has blank evidence, decision and sign-off sections. Tests verify deterministic output, identifier omission, SHA-256 binding, existing-directory refusal and the 4 pinned timing outcomes. They do not establish model performance or renew the legal review date.

The new command follows review-pack exit meanings: 0 only for all ON_TIME, 2 for any exception and 1 on input or write failure. The existing checker command retains its remittance-confirmation behaviour. Missing fund receipt evidence is never inferred.

## Expected result

Fictional fixture | Expected result
timely_remittance_no_receipt.csv | timely_remittance_no_receipt.csv exits 2 with AT_RISK.
late_remittance_no_receipt.csv | late_remittance_no_receipt.csv exits 2 with LATE.
receipt_on_due_date.csv | receipt_on_due_date.csv exits 0 with ON_TIME.
receipt_after_due_date.csv | receipt_after_due_date.csv exits 2 with LATE.

A missing receipt cannot prove on-time, remittance timing can prove late and timely remittance without receipt remains at-risk. The outcome identifiers are AT_RISK, ON_TIME and LATE.

## Controls triggered

The production check keeps a missing receipt at AT_RISK, records an on-time receipt as ON_TIME and classifies a remittance after the deadline or a late receipt as LATE.

## Primary sources

- Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992
- Australian Taxation Office, LCR 2026/2
- Primary source review

## Versions

Product release v0.1.3; fixture version 1; source reviewed 15 August 2026.

payday-super-checker/v0.1.3 is the first release from the australian-accounting monorepo and the first to contain the evaluation directory. Its calculation behaviour is unchanged from v0.1.2, and the evaluation artefacts are fixed to that release’s commit.

- Immutable payday-super-checker/v0.1.3 GitHub Release
- Evaluation pack
- Expected results contract
- Evaluation contract test

## Human decision

Remittance evidence can show operational timing but cannot prove on-time; a human must establish eligible fund receipt, allocation and the other assessment facts before relying on a statutory conclusion.

## Limitations

Experimental review aid. Not a compliance determination. This evaluation does not provide advice or make an ATO assessment. It tests fictional evidence classifications only. See Evidence and Assurance for the common assurance record and boundaries.

Verify a figure against current guidance before relying on it. Historical and current values remain on the linked HTML pages. Source checked is the date a table was last checked against its primary source, from the CSV’s checked_at; last reviewed is this page’s editorial check.

Each rate page shows its own Source checked date. The Excel instructions below do not renew those checks. Every row of the 11 rate CSVs names the source it was checked against in source_url and the date of that check in checked_at.

All 11 rate tables as one JSON file: every CSV row, with its source_url and checked_at, built from the CSVs. It is published under the existing data terms, the Ryan Duguid Public Attribution Licence 1.0.

## Use these tables in Excel

Show the Power Query steps

In Excel for Windows with Power Query, choose Data, Get Data, From Other Sources, Blank Query. Open Advanced Editor, replace its contents with this query and choose Done, then Close & Load. If prompted, choose Anonymous access for this public source. Microsoft’s Text/CSV guide explains the connector.

```
let
    Source = Csv.Document(
        Web.Contents("https://duguid.com.au/rates/super-guarantee/super-guarantee-rates.csv"),
        [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]
    ),
    Headers = Table.PromoteHeaders(Source, [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
    Rates = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Headers, {
        {"period_start", type date},
        {"period_end", type date},
        {"general_sg_rate_percent", type number},
        {"notes", type text},
        {"source_url", type text},
        {"checked_at", type date}
    }, "en-AU")
in
    Rates
```

Checked in Excel for Windows 16.0, build 20527, on 17 October 2026: 8 data rows, 4 columns and the open-ended period retained. The source_url and checked_at columns were added on 3 November 2026 and loaded in build 20625 on 14 November 2026.

This imports the full SG history. A rate of 12.00 means 12%; divide by 100 if a formula needs a fraction. A blank end date remains blank. Select the period that applies to your work; the latest row does not apply to every year.

Use Data, Refresh All to fetch the current CSV again. A successful refresh confirms retrieval, not a source check. Check the linked rate page’s Source checked date and primary source. For a completed workpaper, keep a dated values-only copy of the table and its Source checked date; a live query can change on refresh.

The other 11 tables use the same steps with their own column types. Percentage columns hold whole percentages, as in the SG table. Each query keeps effective periods and notes, and an announced measure’s status stays text: it is not an enacted rate.

# Announced Australian tax measures for 2026-27? 8 TBD

Source: https://duguid.com.au/rates/announced-not-yet-law/

> ATO statuses, bill stages and enacted-law dates for 27 selected tax and super measures: 8 TBD. Selected Senate stages checked 20 November 2026.

8 TBD

# Announced tax measures and enacted law

Of the 27 selected Budget and MYEFO measures below, the ATO summary shows 8 TBD and one as Various, and names a bill for 6. It names enacted legislation for the other 12: 3 with later application dates and 9 with earlier dates.

TBD and Various are source-reported categories, not a finding that no draft, bill or instrument exists. Check application and transition rules before using a measure.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026. Source checked 13 November 2026 for legislated measures. Source checked 20 November 2026 for pending measures. Reform provisions reviewed 22 September 2026.

Read from the ATO’s latest news on tax and superannuation law and policy (QC43473): the pending measures on 20 November 2026 and the legislated measures on 13 November 2026, both after the ATO’s 9 November 2026 update. The status column repeats the ATO summary. TBD alone does not establish whether a consultation draft, bill or instrument exists. Various identifies a package whose components may be at different stages.

## Not yet legislated in the ATO summary

An announcement does not amend the law. Do not automatically apply a proposal in a current-law calculation. Clearly labelled planning scenarios may model proposed changes. The ATO’s guidance on announced measures explains options and consequences for taxpayers who follow existing law or anticipate a change. The Treasury consultation index (archived 6 October 2026) is a historical reference. Check the measure’s current consultation material, parliamentary record and Federal Register entry before assigning a legal status; the archived index does not establish current law. Eight selected rows show TBD and 6 name a bill; the MYEFO philanthropy package shows Various and needs component-level checking.

On 20 November 2026, the parliamentary records were rechecked for the 4 measures in the Tax Reform No. 4 Bill and for both discretionary trust bills. ‘No bill identified in the material checked’ means none was found in the titles of the 127 bills before Parliament on 14 November 2026, the schedule headings of the Tax Reform No. 3 and No. 4 Bills or the titles of Acts made since 1 September 2026; it does not establish that no bill exists. A bill can still change or lapse; check its page before relying on a stage.

Later report for the foreign resident CGT row: the ATO measure page, updated 9 October 2026, says the Treasury Laws Amendment (Strengthening Accountability for Tax Adviser Misconduct and Other Measures) Act 2026 is law and the changes commenced on 1 October 2026. The Federal Register gives assent on 15 September 2026. The ATO summary still showed TBD when checked on 20 November 2026, so the row repeats it.

Left out on purpose: the Budget and MYEFO rows that fund administration rather than change tax or super law (child support systems, the foreign investment framework, the Consumer Data Right, ABN authentication and lookup services, Digital ID, the counter-fraud and NDIS taskforces, director identification number linking and the wind-down of cheques).

## Legislated: later application

The ATO summary names Acts for these 3 measures and lists 1 July 2027 as their start. The stage column in this table and the next was read on 13 November 2026 from the Federal Register of Legislation; the CSV’s stage_source_url column links the first Act or instrument named, and the stage cites each by its Act number or Register ID. Commencement, income year application and transaction cut-offs are different. Earlier acquisitions can affect later treatment, as the reform provisions below show.

### Negative gearing: application and acquisition cut-off

Schedule 2 item 5 of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026 applies the amendments from the 2027-28 income year. Schedule 2 commenced on 27 June 2026, the day after Royal Assent. The inserted section 26-155(2)(a) excludes amounts relating to an ownership interest in a residential dwelling last acquired before 7:30 pm ACT legal time on 12 May 2026. For this exception, section 26-155(3) uses the contract date for a dwelling acquired under contract, rather than settlement.

Other exceptions cover new residential dwellings and prescribed activities, widely held unit trusts, complying superannuation entities and amounts relating to fringe benefits: sections 26-155(2), (4), (5) and 26-160. New-dwelling and prescribed-activity conditions depend on legislative instruments; this page does not determine whether a particular property qualifies. A 2026-27 purchase can therefore affect later deductions even though the deduction restriction applies from 2027-28.

### CGT: separate application rules

The negative gearing acquisition cut-off is not a general CGT grandfathering rule. Schedule 1 has separate rules: items 82 to 84 address income year and CGT-event application, and item 60 inserts transitional section 119-1 for the minimum tax on gains from CGT events on or after 1 July 2027. Check the asset, event and applicable transition provisions separately before calculating a gain.

### Negative gearing and CGT: a bill before Parliament

A bill before Parliament, the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 3) Bill 2026, would amend the negative gearing provisions in relation to new residential dwellings and dwellings that support affordable housing. Parliament’s summary of the bill says it would also clarify and adjust the operation of the capital gains tax adjustment provisions, including their application to trusts and managed investment vehicles. The ATO summary, last updated 9 November 2026, lists it and the Income Tax Rates Amendment (Minimum Tax on Discretionary Trusts) Bill 2026, both introduced on 14 October 2026, against the negative gearing and CGT discount reform. The House agreed to the Bill’s third reading on 29 October 2026. The Senate Economics Legislation Committee reported on 13 November 2026, and the Senate second reading was moved on 16 November 2026. The Bill was still before the Senate on 22 November 2026. Check the Bill’s progress and text before relying on the proposed changes.

## Common questions

### Is the $1,000 instant tax deduction law?

Yes. Schedule 4 Part 1 item 17 of the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026 applies it from the 2026-27 income year. Section 25-130 covers individuals who are Australian residents at some time in the year and derive assessable labour income. The deduction starts at the lesser of $1,000 and that income, then is reduced, to no less than zero, by specified work-related deductions. It is not an extra $1,000 on top of those same expenses. Income protection, personal sickness and accident insurance premiums, and membership of a trade, business or professional association are excluded from the section 8-1 reduction.

### Is the negative gearing and CGT discount reform law?

Yes. The negative gearing amendments apply from 2027-28, but an earlier acquisition can affect later treatment. Section 26-155 has a pre-7:30 pm ACT legal time, 12 May 2026 ownership interest exception and a contract date rule. CGT has separate application and transition provisions; do not apply that acquisition cut-off to every CGT asset. The separate Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 3) Bill 2026 proposes further changes and is before the Senate.

### What does TBD mean on the ATO’s list?

TBD is the development status reported in the ATO summary. That entry alone does not establish whether a consultation draft, bill or instrument exists. Check Treasury, Parliament and the Federal Register for the measure. Various means the package needs component-level checking.

### How often is this page checked?

At the events in the rates register’s review cadence: the 1 July rollover, the May Budget, the December MYEFO and each sitting of Parliament, plus any reader report.

Statuses repeat the ATO page as at the date above. Check the ATO page and the Federal Register before relying on a measure.

# What is the super guarantee rate for 2026-27? 12%

Source: https://duguid.com.au/rates/super-guarantee/

> Every general super guarantee rate since 2002-03, with dates. It has been 12% since 1 July 2025, and payday super changed the timing, not the rate.

12%

# Super guarantee rate history

The general super guarantee rate is 12%. It reached 12% on 1 July 2025 and no further increases are scheduled. Payday super, from 1 July 2026, changed when contributions must be paid, generally within 7 business days of each payday, and left the rate alone.

Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026. Source checked 13 November 2026.

Read on 30 August 2026 from the ATO’s super guarantee rate table, the Treasury Laws Amendment (Payday Superannuation) Act 2025 and the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992. The general SG rate table was rechecked against the ATO on 14 September 2026. All CSV rows were rechecked on 13 November 2026.

## Current rate

12% since 1 July 2025, with no later step scheduled. From 1 July 2026, Payday Super changed the timing: contributions are generally due within 7 business days of each payday rather than quarterly. The rate stayed at 12%, but timing was not the only change: contributions are now worked out on qualifying earnings rather than ordinary time earnings, and the maximum contributions base is an annual limit rather than a quarterly one.

These are the general rates. Norfolk Island has a separate transitional rate that has been stepping up since 1 July 2016 and reaches 12% on 1 July 2027; the ATO publishes it in a second column of the same table.

## Common questions

### What is the super guarantee rate for 2025-26?

12%. The rate reached its final step of 12% on 1 July 2025.

### What is the super guarantee rate for 2026-27?

12%. There are no further scheduled increases.

### Did the super guarantee rate change on 1 July 2026?

No. Payday Super changed the timing from that date: pay within 7 business days of each payday instead of quarterly. The rate itself has been 12% since 1 July 2025.

### When did the super guarantee rate stop increasing?

The last increase was to 12% on 1 July 2025. Earlier steps were annual each 1 July: 11.5% (2024), 11% (2023), 10.5% (2022), 10% (2021).

# What is the Division 7A benchmark rate for 2026-27? 8.77%

Source: https://duguid.com.au/rates/div7a-benchmark-rate/

> For companies with a 30 June year end: 8.77% for 2026-27 and 8.37% for 2025-26. How section 109N(2) sets the rate, including for substituted accounting periods.

8.77%

# Division 7A benchmark interest rate

The benchmark interest rate for the 2026-27 income year is 8.77% for companies with a 30 June year end.

Section 109N(2) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 does not name a figure: it points at the Reserve Bank’s indicator lending rate for bank variable housing loans, the last one published before the income year starts. That makes the rate something you can derive and check yourself.

Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 3 November 2026. Source checked 13 November 2026.

Rates below are derived from section 109N(2) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 and the Reserve Bank of Australia statistical table F5, Indicator Lending Rates, series FILRHLBVS, Lending rates; Housing loans; Banks; Variable; Standard; Owner-occupier, read 28 August 2026. The May 2026 series value is 8.77% and the May 2025 value is 8.37%. The rates for 2021-22 to 2026-27 were rechecked against the ATO benchmark rate table on 14 September 2026.

## The rate, by income year

Companies with a 30 June year end

Income year | Benchmark rate
2026-27 | 8.77%
2025-26 | 8.37%
2024-25 | 8.77%
2023-24 | 8.27%
2022-23 | 4.77%
2021-22 | 4.52%
2020-21 | 4.52%
2019-20 | 5.37%

The table starts at 2019-20 and covers companies with a 30 June year end. Confirm the figure against the ATO table for the year you are relying on. For a substituted accounting period, use the last relevant Reserve Bank rate published before that period starts; these table values may not apply.

Download the table as CSV. Each row of the CSV gives the Reserve Bank F5 data its rate is derived from (source_url) and the date it was last checked against it (checked_at); every row was rechecked on 13 November 2026. Cite as Duguid, R. (2026). Division 7A benchmark interest rate by year [Data set]. https://duguid.com.au/rates/div7a-benchmark-rate/. For a 30 June year end, the rate is the May Reserve Bank figure, not the June one.

## How to work it out yourself

Take the Reserve Bank’s F5 Indicator Lending Rates table and read the bank variable housing loans series for owner-occupiers. The rate for an income year is the last figure published before that year began. The Reserve Bank publishes F5 in the first week after the month it covers, so the last figure published before 1 July is the one for May. For the year that started on 1 July 2026, that is May 2026, which was 8.77%. If the company uses a substituted accounting period, apply the same rule to that period’s start date instead of 1 July.

Reading the June figure instead is the usual mistake, and it changes the answer in a normal year. June 2025 sat at 8.27% while May 2025 sat at 8.37%, and 8.37 is the benchmark rate for 2025-26. Section 109N(2) also leaves room for regulations to set the rate a different way, and none currently do.

The data is at the Reserve Bank’s statistical tables, table F5.

## What the rate is for

A loan from a private company to a shareholder or an associate that is still unpaid at the company’s lodgment day for the year the loan was made is treated as a dividend unless an exclusion applies. For a loan not otherwise excluded, two relevant paths avoid that result: repaying the loan in full before the lodgment day, or a written agreement made before that day that satisfies section 109N. Section 109N(1) asks for 3 things: a written agreement, a rate of interest for years after the year the loan was made that equals or exceeds that year’s benchmark rate, and a term inside the maximum. The minimum yearly repayment is then calculated using the current year’s benchmark rate under section 109E. The maximum term is 7 years, or 25 years where the loan is fully secured by a registered mortgage over real property and the property’s value, net of prior liabilities, is at least 110% of the loan.

A higher benchmark rate increases the minimum yearly repayment when the unpaid balance and remaining term are unchanged.

## Common questions

### What is the Division 7A benchmark interest rate for 2026-27?

8.77% for companies with a 30 June year end. It is the Reserve Bank’s indicator lending rate for bank variable housing loans last published before 1 July 2026, which was the May 2026 figure.

### What was the benchmark rate for 2025-26?

8.37% for companies with a 30 June year end, using the May 2025 figure. The June 2025 figure of 8.27% was not published until after the income year had started, so it does not apply.

### Where does the rate come from?

Section 109N(2) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936 points at the Reserve Bank’s indicator lending rate for bank variable housing loans, the last one published before the start of the income year, unless regulations provide another method. None currently do.

### Does a change in the rate affect loans already on foot?

Yes. The minimum yearly repayment uses that year’s benchmark rate, the unpaid balance and the remaining term. A higher rate increases the repayment when the other 2 inputs are unchanged.

### What is the maximum term for a complying Division 7A loan?

Seven years, or 25 years where the loan is fully secured by a registered mortgage over real property whose value, less prior liabilities, is at least 110% of the loan when it is first made.

These figures are derived from the Reserve Bank series the Act names, on the date above. The ATO publishes the benchmark rate for each year, and a loan agreement is worth checking against a practitioner rather than a table.

# What is the cents per kilometre rate for 2026-27? 91 cents

Source: https://duguid.com.au/rates/cents-per-kilometre/

> 91 cents for 2026-27, 88 cents for the 2 years before it, capped at 5,000 business kilometres. Each rate cites the determination that sets it.

91 cents

# Cents per kilometre rate for car expenses

The rate is 91 cents per kilometre for the income year commencing 1 July 2026, set for that year alone, and was 88 cents for the 2 years before it. The method covers the first 5,000 business kilometres per car per year and no further.

One rate applies to every car, whatever its engine size, and no receipts have to be kept for the car expenses themselves. This is the rate for the cents per kilometre method, one of the car expense methods: it is a rate table, not a determination that a particular taxpayer, car or business kilometre is eligible, and the choice between methods is not made here.

Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 3 November 2026. Source checked 13 November 2026.

Each rate below is taken from the determination that sets it, last checked on 13 November 2026: the 2026 determination (F2026L00785) and the 2024 determination (F2024L00697), both made under section 28-25 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.

## The rate, by income year

Income year | Rate (cents per km) | Set by
2026-27 | 91 | Determination 2026 (F2026L00785), section 6, that year only
2025-26 | 88 | Determination 2024 (F2024L00697), section 6
2024-25 | 88 | Determination 2024 (F2024L00697), section 6

Earlier years were set the same way, each determination repealing the one before it. The 2024 determination repealed the 2023 determination, and the 2026 determination repealed the 2024 one. Rates for those earlier years are not listed here because they were not read from the instruments themselves.

Download the table as CSV. Each row of the CSV gives the determination that sets its rate (source_url) and the date it was last checked against it (checked_at); every row was rechecked on 13 November 2026. Cite as Duguid, R. (2026). Cents per kilometre car deduction rate by year [Data set]. https://duguid.com.au/rates/cents-per-kilometre/. 91 cents is for 2026-27 only; it does not carry forward the way 88 cents did.

## Why 2025-26 did not move, and why 2026-27 is different

A determination is not always written one year at a time, and the 2 most recent ones are drafted differently. The 2024 determination set the rate 'for income years commencing on or after 1 July 2024', and its own note says it applies to the year commencing 1 July 2024 and to any subsequent income year until it is repealed or varied. Nothing replaced it for 2025-26, so 88 cents carried through unchanged.

The 2026 determination repealed it and is written for one year only. Section 6 sets the rate 'for the income year commencing on 1 July 2026', and it carries no note extending that to subsequent years. So 91 cents does not carry forward the way 88 cents did. A further determination has to be registered to set the rate for 2027-28, and until one is registered, there is no rate for that year to rely on.

## How the method works

For business claims, the ATO limits this method to sole traders and partnerships with at least one individual partner, claiming for a car. Private travel does not qualify. Table rows were last checked on 13 November 2026.

Section 28-25 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 sets the calculation: business kilometres travelled by the car in the income year, multiplied by the rate determined for that year. Four features of it catch people out.

- 5,000 kilometres is a ceiling, not a threshold. If the car travelled 5,085 business kilometres, you claim 5,000 and lose the extra 85. The Act uses that exact example.
- One rate for every car. Engine size stopped mattering when the old engine capacity bands were replaced by a single determined rate.
- No substantiation of the car expenses. Section 28-35 removes that requirement for this method, which is not the same as needing no records: the business kilometres still have to be a reasonable estimate you can explain.
- The rate is meant to cover everything. In setting it, the Commissioner must have regard to average operating costs, which the Act’s own note describes as including registration, insurance and depreciation as well as fuel and maintenance. Claiming those separately on top of the rate is double counting.

## Common questions

### What is the cents per kilometre rate for 2026-27?

91 cents per kilometre, set by section 6 of the Income Tax Assessment (Cents per Kilometre Deduction Rate for Car Expenses) Determination 2026.

### What was the rate for 2025-26?

88 cents per kilometre. The 2024 determination set that rate for income years commencing on or after 1 July 2024, and nothing replaced it before the 2025-26 year, so it carried through.

### What rate applies for 2027-28?

Not yet set. Section 6 of the 2026 determination sets 91 cents for the income year commencing on 1 July 2026 only. It has no note extending that rate to later years, so a further determination must be registered before there is a rate for 2027-28.

### How many kilometres can I claim under this method?

The first 5,000 business kilometres per car per income year. Kilometres above 5,000 are discarded rather than paid at a lower rate, so a car that travelled 5,085 business kilometres claims 5,000.

### Does the rate depend on the size of the car’s engine?

No. A single rate applies to every car for the income year. The engine capacity bands belong to an older version of the method.

### Can I claim fuel, registration and insurance as well as the rate?

No. The Commissioner sets the rate by having regard to average operating costs, and the Act names registration, insurance, depreciation, fuel and maintenance as examples of those costs. They are already inside the rate.

Rates here were read from the determinations on the date above. Check the current instrument on the Federal Register of Legislation, or current ATO guidance, before relying on a figure.

# Maximum super contribution base for 2026-27? $270,830

Source: https://duguid.com.au/rates/maximum-contribution-base/

> $270,830 a year for 2026-27 under Payday Super, and the quarterly bases back to 2021-22. The formula, the SG ceiling it sets and the ATO source.

$270,830

# Maximum super contribution base

The maximum contribution base is $270,830 for 2026-27, now an annual figure that applies to each employer separately.

Once the qualifying earnings an employer has paid an employee for the year pass the base, that employer can stop paying super guarantee for that employee for the rest of the year. For quarters up to 30 June 2026 the base was set per quarter, $62,500 for 2025-26.

Published 20 September 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026. Source checked 13 November 2026.

Last checked on 13 November 2026 against the ATO’s super guarantee rates and thresholds page (Tables 23 and 24, last updated 17 April 2026), with the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992 as amended by the Treasury Laws Amendment (Payday Superannuation) Act 2025.

## Current base

$270,830 for 2026-27. Payday Super made the base an annual limit on the qualifying earnings each employer pays from 1 July 2026; an employee with two employers has a separate base with each. The ATO derives it as the concessional contributions cap multiplied by 100, divided by the charge percentage, rounded down to the nearest $10. At 12% that caps compulsory super guarantee for one employee at $32,499.60 for the year.

Income year | Maximum contribution base (annual)
2026-27 | $270,830

## Quarterly bases to 30 June 2026

For quarters ending on or before 30 June 2026 the base was a quarterly earnings amount and applied to ordinary time earnings. The ATO publishes the base and the super guarantee it implies at that year’s percentage.

Income year | Base per quarter | Maximum SG per quarter
2025-26 | $62,500 | $7,500.00
2024-25 | $65,070 | $7,483.05
2023-24 | $62,270 | $6,849.70
2022-23 | $60,220 | $6,323.10
2021-22 | $58,920 | $5,892.00

The base is indexed to average weekly ordinary time earnings. Earlier years are on the ATO page and are not listed here because they were not read from it.

Download the table as CSV. Each row of the CSV gives the ATO page it was read from (source_url) and the date it was last checked against it (checked_at); every row was rechecked on 13 November 2026. Cite as Duguid, R. (2026). Maximum super contribution base by year [Data set]. https://duguid.com.au/rates/maximum-contribution-base/. Verify against current ATO guidance before relying on a figure.

## Common questions

### What is the maximum super contribution base for 2026-27?

$270,830 of qualifying earnings for the year, counted separately by each employer. An employer does not have to pay super guarantee on the earnings it pays above that.

### Is the base annual or quarterly?

Annual from 1 July 2026, when Payday Super started, and applied per employer. For quarters up to 30 June 2026 it was a quarterly amount, $62,500 for each quarter of 2025-26.

### How is the base worked out?

Concessional contributions cap, multiplied by 100, divided by the super guarantee charge percentage, rounded down to the nearest $10. That is the ATO’s published formula.

### What is the most super guarantee an employer must pay for one employee in 2026-27?

12% of $270,830, which is $32,499.60 for the year, before any salary sacrifice or additional contributions the employer chooses to make.
