# How does this business compare to ATO benchmarks?

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/ato-benchmarks/

> Current release ato-benchmark-compare v0.2.2. Compare a business’s profit and loss against ATO small business benchmark ranges and review differences locally.

# ATO small business benchmark comparison tool

The ATO small business benchmark comparison tool maps a profit and loss to the ATO’s own categories, applies its narrow definitions and shows whether each ratio falls inside the published range.

Current release ato-benchmark-compare v0.2.2, 20 October 2026, from the australian-accounting repository. Release licence: Apache License 2.0. Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Python

Needs

Python 3.14 or later

Boundary

A comparison is not an audit finding or compliance conclusion.

Install ato-benchmark-compare Read the worked example

## Cost of sales ratio excluding wages

```
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 pytest -q tests/test_ratios.py::test_cost_of_sales_ratio_excludes_wages_inside_cost_of_sales
```

30% cost of sales on $100,000 turnover

Wages of $10,000 stay in total expenses ($40,000) in v0.1.6. Read the fictional totals and setup steps.

The ATO publishes benchmark ranges for around 100 industries and uses them to pick which small businesses to examine. Sitting outside a range is not a finding that anything is wrong.

Checking a business against the benchmarks before lodgement is a useful review step, and it is usually done by hand: find the industry page, work out which turnover band applies, add up the right accounts and divide.

This tool does that on your own machine, with no network call in the runtime, and it records which account went into which figure so a second reviewer can check your working later. It applies the ATO’s own narrow definitions rather than a rough 'expenses over income': wages sitting inside cost of sales come out of that ratio, and payments to associated persons come out of total expenses before the division.

The workflow is 2 steps on purpose. First, the tool drafts a mapping from the profit and loss, suggesting a bucket for each account from its name alone. Then a person reviews and corrects that mapping, because no account name on its own tells you whether wages went to an associate.

## What this tool does

- Reads a profit and loss and maps each account to the ATO’s benchmark categories, with a person reviewing that mapping before anything is compared.
- Applies the ATO’s own narrow definitions of turnover, cost of sales and total expenses, for example excluding wages inside cost of sales from that ratio and deducting payments to associated persons from total expenses.
- Prints the figures behind each ratio and shows whether it sits inside or outside the ATO’s published range.

## Worked example: cost of sales excluding wages

The fictional example below comes from the ratio tests in ato-benchmark-compare v0.1.6. It starts with mapped totals:

- Turnover: $100,000.
- Cost of sales excluding wages: $30,000.
- Wages recorded within cost of sales, mapped separately: $10,000.

The cost of sales ratio is $30,000 ÷ $100,000 = 30%. The $10,000 of wages remains in reported total expenses, which are $40,000 in this example.

A person must review the mapping and select the relevant industry, year and turnover band before comparing that 30% with an ATO range. This example does not establish whether a business falls within a benchmark.

### Reproduce this exact example

This example uses v0.1.6 under the MIT License.

In a fresh folder, with Git and uv installed, run the test at the release used above:

```
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting.git
cd australian-accounting
git checkout ato-benchmark-compare/v0.1.6
cd packages/ato-benchmark-compare
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 pytest -q tests/test_ratios.py::test_cost_of_sales_ratio_excludes_wages_inside_cost_of_sales
```

Expected: one passing test and exit 0. The test asserts the figures above. The broader sample under Get it contains different inputs.

## Limits

Sitting outside a range is not a finding that anything is wrong. The ATO publishes ranges because businesses differ.

## Get it

Needs Python 3.14 or later. A command-line tool for whoever runs Python at your firm. These commands install v0.2.2 under the Apache License 2.0. This is the last Python release; the default branch now holds an unreleased Rust rewrite that pip does not install.

```

cd australian-accounting/packages/ato-benchmark-compare
pip install .
```

Source on GitHub · Primary source: the ATO’s small business benchmarks.

One known limitation is recorded against this tool. When a bucket a ratio needs is absent from the supplied totals, it reaches the command-line comparison as exactly the nil that a genuine zero produces, while the Python library marks it not_supplied. The two output paths differ in releases up to 0.1.7. Release 0.1.8 gates the command line on the same presence rules as the library, so a bucket no account was mapped to reads not_supplied on both. That is separate from a profit and loss account with no mapping entry, which stops the comparison with a mapping error before any ratio is produced. Check the required buckets, including income fields, before relying on a ratio. See Known limitations.

Software issue using fictional data? Open an issue or email with the tool named in the subject. If the email link does not open, the contact page spells the address out. Wrong rate, date or rule on this page? Report a correction.

## Common questions

### What are the ATO small business benchmarks?

Ranges the ATO publishes for around 100 industries, showing the usual relationship between figures such as cost of sales and turnover. The ATO uses them to decide which businesses to examine.

### Does being outside a benchmark range mean something is wrong?

No. Businesses differ, which is why the ATO publishes a range rather than a point. A ratio outside the range is a prompt to explain why.

### Does this tool send my client data anywhere?

No. It runs on your own machine with no network call in the runtime, and it records which account went into which figure so a colleague can check the comparison later.

### Why does a person have to review the account mapping?

Because no account name on its own tells you whether wages went to an associated person, and the ATO’s definitions turn on that. The tool drafts the mapping, a person corrects it, and only then is anything compared.

# Trust distribution worksheets for professional review

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/trust-distributions/

> Inspect section 100A, Division 6 and section 99B worksheets from supplied facts. Have a registered tax agent review the arrangement before relying on a result.

# Trust distribution worksheets for professional review

The software compares supplied flags with its implemented PCG 2022/2 zone criteria and calculates conditional Division 6 and section 99B amounts.

Current release solomons-sword v1.0.0, 25 November 2026, from the australian-accounting repository. Release licence: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Rust

Needs

Windows x86_64 or Linux x86_64. The executable runs without Python or Rust.

Boundary

Does not invent arrangements, intentions or beneficiary facts.

Install solomons-sword Read the worked example

## Check a section 99B receipt

```
uvx --from solomons-sword==0.1.9 solomons-sword s99b-check --beneficiary "Fabricated Beneficiary" --gross 150000 --corpus 50000 --resident-during-year
```

$100,000.00 assessable under s99B

Fictional $150,000 gross receipt less $50,000 corpus exemption in v0.1.9. See the full output and refusal check.

PCG 2022/2 sorts section 100A arrangements into white, green and red zones. There is no blue zone: that was proposed in the draft, PCG 2022/D1, and did not survive into the final guideline. The software does not establish the underlying facts or give tax clearance.

Section 100A can treat a trust distribution as a reimbursement agreement and tax it at the top rate instead of the beneficiary’s own rate. The ATO’s finalised guideline PCG 2022/2 says where the risk sits.

The white zone, for income years ending before 1 July 2014, is out of scope because the tool does not take an income year. Division 6 shares follow the High Court’s decision in Bamford.

Where the tool does not implement a rule, such as trust capital gains and franked dividends, streamed or not, under the Division 6E carve-out, it refuses the input rather than returning a number it cannot stand behind.

## What this tool does

- Classifies a trust distribution against the ATO’s section 100A green and red risk zones under PCG 2022/2, from facts you supply.
- Works out each beneficiary’s proportionate share of trust income under Division 6, following the Bamford case.
- Calculates the assessable amount on a foreign trust distribution under section 99B, after corpus and previously taxed income deductions.

## Get it

Needs Python 3.10 or later. The command installs v0.1.9 under the MIT License.

```
python -m pip install "solomons-sword==0.1.9"
```

Published package and release instructions.

The current release, solomons-sword/v1.0.0, published on 25 November 2026, replaces the Python package with an executable for Linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64, with provenance attestations, under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. It needs no Python. Run on 26 November 2026, it printed this page’s assessment figures and its refusal for this page’s inputs with the same message and exit code as the pinned release. The command above stays pinned to the Python release so the example stays reproducible.

## Fictional worked example

With uv installed, run this pinned package directly. No clone or input file is needed.

This section 99B example assumes a beneficiary who was resident during the income year, a gross receipt of $150,000 and $50,000 of qualifying corpus. It assumes no corpus attributable to notionally assessable income and no other exclusions. The name and amounts are fictional. The command states residency with --resident-during-year because release 0.1.9 refuses a run that states neither residency flag.

```

```


### Try a refusal


## Limits

The examples assume supplied facts, and nothing this engine produces is an assessment, a determination or confirmation of entitlement, liability or compliance. Outputs are review aids: confirm every allocation, zone and exemption against the current law, the trust deed and the entity’s facts before acting, have a registered tax agent verify the supplied facts and review their tax treatment, and leave lodgement decisions with a registered practitioner.

Source on GitHub · Primary sources: ATO PCG 2022/2 and the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936.

Software issue using fictional data? Open an issue or email with the tool named in the subject. If the email link does not open, the contact page spells the address out. Wrong rate, date or rule on this page? Report a correction.

## Common questions

### Is there a blue zone in PCG 2022/2?

No. The blue zone appeared only in the draft, PCG 2022/D1. The finalised PCG 2022/2 has white, green and red zones only.

### What is the white zone?

The white zone covers arrangements in income years ending before 1 July 2014. This tool does not take an income year, so the white zone is out of scope here.

### How is each beneficiary’s share of trust income worked out?

Proportionately, following the High Court’s decision in Bamford: a beneficiary’s share of trust income sets the proportion of the trust’s taxable income assessed to them.

### What will this tool refuse to calculate?

Anything it does not implement, including trust capital gains and franked dividends, streamed or not, under the Division 6E carve-out. It refuses the input rather than returning a number it cannot stand behind.

# Company tax and franking worksheets

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/company-tax-franking/

> Inspect company tax and franking worksheets from operator-established facts. Have a registered tax agent review the tax position before relying on a result.

# Company tax and franking worksheets

The company tax and franking worksheets run the base rate entity test, track the franking account and check the Division 203 benchmark rule.

Current release the-exchequer-tally v1.0.0, 25 November 2026, from the australian-accounting repository. Release licence: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Rust

Needs

Windows x86_64 or Linux x86_64. The executable runs without Python or Rust.

Boundary

Requires verified income composition, distributions and ledger inputs.

Install the-exchequer-tally Read the worked example

## Test base rate entity status

```
uvx --from the-exchequer-tally==0.1.7 the-exchequer-tally bre-test --fy 2025 --turnover 4500000 --assessable 800000 --passive 120000
```

25.0% applicable rate (15.00% passive income)

Fictional 2025 inputs in v0.1.7; exits 0 and does not set a franking rate. See the full output and refusal check.

A company gets the lower tax rate only if it is a base rate entity: aggregated turnover under the year’s threshold, and no more than 80% of assessable income being base rate entity passive income. Get that test wrong and the company pays the wrong income tax for the year. The rate used to frank a dividend is a separate imputation question that turns on prior-year facts, not this year’s test; this tool keeps the two apart and the worked example below does not determine a maximum franking rate.

The worksheets run the base rate entity test and track a franking account ledger covering PAYG instalments, company tax paid, dividends paid and received, and refunds. They work out franking deficit tax and check the 30% offset reduction for supported debit types. The debit types and applicable exceptions determine whether a reduction applies, as explained under Common questions. They also check distributions in a franking period against the Division 203 benchmark rule for over-franking tax and franking debit shortfalls.

The worksheets also build the statement fields a dividend distribution statement needs. That is a review helper for the statement, not a lodgement or a compliance certificate.

## What this tool does

- Tests whether a company is a base rate entity for a given financial year, against the aggregated turnover threshold and the 80% passive income test.
- Tracks a franking account ledger and checks franking deficit tax and any offset reduction for supported debit types, subject to the conditions under Common questions.
- Checks distributions in a franking period against the Division 203 benchmark rule, for over-franking tax and franking debit shortfalls.

## Limits

The examples assume supplied facts, and nothing this engine produces is an assessment, a determination or confirmation of entitlement, liability or compliance. Outputs are review aids: confirm every rate, threshold and consequence against the current law and the entity’s facts before acting, have a registered tax agent verify the supplied facts and review their tax treatment, and leave lodgement decisions with a registered practitioner.

## Get it

Needs Python 3.10 or later. The command installs v0.1.7 under the MIT License.

```

```

It needs no Python. Run on 26 November 2026, it printed this page’s rate test and its refusal for this page’s inputs with the same message and exit code as the pinned release. ## Common questions

### What makes a company a base rate entity?

Two tests, both of which must hold for the income year: aggregated turnover below that year’s threshold, and no more than 80% of assessable income being base rate entity passive income.

### What is franking deficit tax?

Tax payable where a franking account ends the year in deficit. Where the deficit exceeds 10% of the credits arising in the year, the offset may be reduced by 30%, but only for the part of the liability that relates to franking debits arising under the provisions listed in section 205-70(8). Check the debit types and any exceptions before applying the reduction.

### What is the benchmark rule?

Under Division 203, a company must frank all distributions in a franking period to the same extent. Departing from the benchmark franking percentage produces over-franking tax or a franking debit shortfall.

10 workflows in the 107-skill pack

Human-confirmed verdicts cover 95 of 235 validation cards in v0.7.0. Repeat the evaluation procedure.

The subcontract ledger workflows are Claude Code skills rather than a standalone calculator, so an AI coding agent has to be set up first.

Each skill encodes the workflow: the steps, the tie-outs and the exceptions to chase. Rates and thresholds go stale and differ by state, so the skill sends the agent to the primary source for them. Two things the skills will not do: decide whether a security of payment Act covers a contract, or conclude that a worker is a contractor rather than an employee. Both stay with a person.

For work in progress, the skills assemble the contract CSV. The arithmetic lives in TheWIPTally, which produces a deterministic AASB 15 schedule. Do not ask the agent to invent cost-to-cost progress, constrained variations or the contract-asset versus contract-liability split.

## What this tool does

- The contracting core: progress claim preparation, retention schedules, work in progress and overbilling and underbilling under AASB 15, and contract cost tracking.
- Mining services and earthmoving: fuel tax credit claims, the Coal LSL levy, payroll tax on contractors, and plant and equipment costing.
- Paying subcontractors: super guarantee under the extended definition, TPAR and a shared reference skill for the exports these workflows need.

## Limits

The skills prepare and check. They do not serve a payment claim, lodge a return or sign anything. Contract interpretation, eligibility conclusions and professional judgement stay with a person.

## Repeat the agent evaluation procedure

Use the evaluation method and its linked validation cards at the same revision. Install that revision, start a fresh session with the target skills loaded and supply the selected card unchanged. Keep the deliberately missing evidence unavailable.

Check the full response against the card’s required checks and prohibitions. Any missed prohibition fails the card. Record the exact model, runtime, source revision, available tools and result; retain the response with the working evidence.

This method measures adherence to visible instructions. It does not test independent error discovery or promise identical wording between runs. Model results require human confirmation before publication; static validation alone does not establish agent behaviour.

Needs an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, and Node.

# Construction WIP under AASB 15: over- or under-billed?

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/wip-schedule/

> AASB 15 construction WIP from a contract CSV: cost-to-cost progress, per-contract assets and liabilities, and profit fade. Review aid, not a determination.

# TheWIPTally construction WIP schedule

TheWIPTally reads one row per unit of account and produces a cost-to-cost work-in-progress schedule: earned revenue after AASB 15 para B19 exclusions, constrained unapproved variations, and a contract asset or contract liability per job.

Current release the-wip-tally v0.2.0, 19 October 2026, from the australian-accounting repository. Release licence: Apache License 2.0. Published 25 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Python

Needs

Python 3.14 or later

Boundary

Review aid under AASB 15, not an accounting determination.

Install the-wip-tally Read the worked example

## Cost-to-cost underbilling check

```
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 pytest -q tests/test_schedule.py::test_clean_cost_to_cost_underbilling
```

$50,000 contract asset at 50% complete

Revenue to date ($500,000) less $450,000 certified billings in v0.1.2. Read the fictional inputs and setup steps.

Assets and liabilities are never netted. Review aid, not a determination.

Construction month-end turns on the WIP schedule. The formula is easy. Applying it the same way every month is the work: strip waste from percentage complete without dropping it from margin, book uninstalled materials at cost, constrain unapproved claims and present each contract as an asset or a liability, never a portfolio net.

This tool does the arithmetic. Install the Python engine, point it at a contract CSV and keep the schedule beside the review pack. Recognition over time versus at a point in time, contract combination, claim enforceability and any onerous-contract provision stay with a person. The subcontractor ledger skills own that workflow: they assemble the file and name this engine rather than inventing the numbers.

## What this tool does

- Measures cost-to-cost progress after AASB 15 para B19 exclusions: waste does not accelerate percentage complete; uninstalled materials are recognised at cost with zero margin. Whether uninstalled materials qualify for that treatment depends on the applicable paragraph B19 conditions, so check them against the contract before relying on it; the fixed example below contains none.
- Constrains unapproved variation estimates by the include ratio you supply, flags the excluded slice and never treats an uncertified claim as billing or entitlement.
- Classifies each contract as a contract asset or a contract liability, flags profit fade of 1.00 percentage point or more, and flags a stale estimate to complete after material extra spend.

## Worked example: a $50,000 contract asset

The fictional example below comes from the cost-to-cost underbilling test in the-wip-tally v0.1.2. The test uses a reasonably measurable outcome, with no variations, waste or uninstalled materials. All amounts below exclude GST.

- Transaction price: $1,000,000.
- Costs incurred: $400,000. Estimated cost to complete: $400,000.
- Certified billings: $450,000.

Progress is $400,000 ÷ ($400,000 + $400,000) = 50%. Revenue to date is 50% × $1,000,000 = $500,000. Deducting $450,000 of certified billings leaves a $50,000 contract asset and no contract liability.

A person must confirm that the recognition basis, contract terms and estimates support this calculation. The test’s conditional retention does not change this revenue-minus-billings result; retention classification and final sign-off still need review.

### Reproduce this exact example

This example uses v0.1.2 under the MIT License.

In a fresh folder, with Git and uv installed, run the test at the release used above:

```
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting.git
cd australian-accounting
git checkout the-wip-tally/v0.1.2
cd packages/the-wip-tally
uv run --locked --extra dev --python 3.12 pytest -q tests/test_schedule.py::test_clean_cost_to_cost_underbilling
```

Expected: one passing test and exit 0. The test asserts the figures above. The broader sample under Get it contains different inputs. The test is pinned to the-wip-tally/v0.1.2 so its figures stay reproducible.

## Limits

Outputs are not an accounting opinion, an audit conclusion or an AASB 15 determination. Confirm the operative compilation at standards.aasb.gov.au before citing a paragraph number, and leave sign-off with a registered practitioner.


## Common questions

### What is a contract asset versus a contract liability?

Revenue to date less certified billings, per contract. A positive amount is a contract asset and a negative amount a contract liability. The engine never offsets one job against another.

### Does wasted cost accelerate percentage complete?

No. Para B19(a) amounts are stripped from the progress measure and kept in estimated cost at completion, so they hit margin instead of pulling revenue forward.

### Are unapproved variations booked in full?

No. Only the constrained slice (unapproved estimate multiplied by the include ratio) enters transaction price. A bare 25 is refused; use 0.25 or 25%.

### Is this an accounting determination?

No. It is a review aid. Recognition over time versus at a point in time, whether a claim is enforceable and any AASB 137 onerous provision stay with the engagement lead.

# Export a Xero trial balance to CSV that balances

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/xero-trial-balance/

> Export a trial balance from the Xero API to a CSV for Excel, Power BI or pandas. Check debit and credit totals before using the figures in a workpaper.

# Xero trial balance CSV export tool

The Xero trial balance export pulls the trial balance from Xero’s own reporting API and refuses to write the CSV unless both the month’s movement and the year-to-date figures balance.

Current release xero-trial-balance-export v0.1.15, 12 October 2026, from the accounting-review-pipeline repository. Release licence: MIT License. Published 24 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Python

Needs

Python 3.11 or later and a Xero developer app (free Starter plan: up to 5 connections, 1,000 API calls a day per organisation)

Boundary

Read-only Xero scope; no ledger writes.

Install the exporter Read the worked example

## Export a dated trial balance

```
python export_tb.py --date 2026-06-30
```

CSV written only when movement and YTD balance

Unbalanced YTD figures exit 1 and write no CSV file in v0.1.6 tests. Compare both fictional outcomes.

The export asks Xero for report reading scope only, so it cannot write anything back to a ledger.

The export reads the trial balance from Xero’s reporting API and writes consistent CSV columns for account codes, names, monthly movements and year-to-date balances.

Before anything is written to disk, it runs a balance check: both the current month’s movement and the year-to-date figures must balance, or no file is written. One limit: --date is an as-at date, not a range. Xero’s Trial Balance endpoint accepts only a date, so the Trial Balance by Date Range report, which exists in the Xero interface only, cannot be reproduced this way. The movement columns cover the usual reason for wanting a range: the current month.

## What this tool does

- Pulls a trial balance from Xero’s own reporting API into a tidy CSV that Power BI, Excel or pandas loads without clean-up.
- Refuses to write a file unless both the month’s movement and the year-to-date figures balance.

Related work: XeroAPI accepted my correction to its command-line report flags. It maps --standard-layout and --payments-only to the matching SDK parameters for balance sheet and profit and loss reports. That contribution concerns a separate tool; it does not validate this exporter. Read the accepted-work record.

## Limits

Read-only (accounting.reports.trialbalance.read); this tool cannot write to any ledger.

MIT-licensed utility code, no warranty; outputs feed professional review like any other workpaper input.

## Get it

The commands install v0.1.15 under the MIT License. Setup needs Python 3.11 or later and a Xero developer app, about 5 minutes of one-off setup. Xero’s free Starter plan lets an app have up to 5 connections, at 1,000 API calls a day per organisation; Works with Xero covers the paid plans and Xero’s exemption for an integration built solely for your own practice or a single client. It works with Xero’s free Demo Company, so nothing has to touch a live ledger. A command-line tool for whoever runs Python at your firm.

```
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/accounting-review-pipeline.git
git -C accounting-review-pipeline checkout xero-trial-balance-export/v0.1.15
cd accounting-review-pipeline/packages/xero-trial-balance-export
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock
# copy .env.example to .env and add the app's client ID and secret, then:
python auth.py
```

First success takes one command. After the one-off consent step above, export a dated trial balance:

```
python export_tb.py --date 2026-06-30
# writes a CSV such as demo-company-au-...-tb-2026-06-30-accrual.csv, only when both balance checks pass
```

## Fictional worked example

Reproduce the Xero trial balance integrity evaluation

The xero-trial-balance-export/v0.1.6 release tests use mocked Xero API behaviour and fictional account rows. They do not contain a live organisation’s data.

Outcome | Fictional facts | Test-backed result
Balanced, CSV written | Business Bank Account (090) has a $1,200.00 movement debit and $15,234.50 YTD debit. Trade Debtors (610) has equal credits. | Both pairs balance and the exact expected CSV bytes are written.
Unbalanced, CSV refused | Cash (090) has $100.00 movement and YTD debits. Equity (960) has a $100.00 movement credit but only a $90.00 YTD credit. | The movement balances, but the $10.00 YTD difference causes exit code 1 and no CSV file output.

The tagged balanced-output test pins the CSV bytes. The tagged unbalanced-YTD test pins the refusal and warning. Refused means no CSV file output; the diagnostic warning is still printed.

The tool remains read-only and cannot write to a ledger. Its output is a review aid, not a compliance result. It does not post entries, approve work, lodge returns or lock periods.

## Common questions

### Can it export a trial balance for a date range?

No. Xero’s Trial Balance endpoint accepts an as-at date, not a range, so the Trial Balance by Date Range report, which exists in the Xero interface only, cannot be reproduced this way. The movement columns cover the usual reason for wanting a range, which is the current month.

### Can this tool change my Xero data?

No. It requests the accounting.reports.trialbalance.read scope, which is read-only, so it cannot write to any ledger.

### What happens if the trial balance does not balance?

No file is written. The balance check runs before anything reaches disk, and both the month’s movement and the year-to-date figures have to balance for the export to proceed.

# Australian tax MCP server: Aus Accounting MCP

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/australian-tax-ai-agents/

> Aus Accounting MCP v0.13.0: a local MCP server for ATO benchmarks, Payday Super timing, GST review and 148 worksheets with the calculators executable.

# Aus Accounting MCP

Aus Accounting MCP is a local Model Context Protocol server for Australian accounting checks: ATO small business benchmarks, Payday Super timing, limited Division 7A review, GST coding and BAS reconciliation review, and 148 tax and super worksheet kinds with the calculators executable.

Current release aus-accounting-mcp v0.13.0, 25 November 2026, from the australian-accounting repository. Release licence: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Published 25 August 2026. Last reviewed 24 November 2026.

Delivery

MCP

Needs

Python 3.14 or later and uv

Boundary

Human review required. Optional local library excerpts enter the assistant’s context; Division 7A scope stays limited.

Adopt Aus Accounting MCP Try 2 tool calls

## Run the pinned MCP demo

```
uvx --from aus-accounting-mcp==0.2.8 aus-accounting-mcp-demo
```

Exit 0 JSON transcript of 2 local tool calls

Runs the pinned v0.2.8 demonstration with fictional facts and no credentials. Inspect the demo output and caveats.

The server runs on your machine and lodges nothing. Outputs need human review.

Choose the tool by the work it supports: a calculation on established facts, a source lookup or an accounting workflow. Ryan Duguid, a senior accountant in Newcastle, NSW, publishes the local engines and the MCP server that runs them. Aus Accounting MCP is a separate project from ato-mcp, the document-retrieval service compared below. The server ships no ATO document library and does not retrieve rulings from the web.

## The split, in one table

The comparisons and capability list below describe reference release v0.2.8, so the worked example’s figures stay reproducible. The current release serves 148 worksheet kinds with the published 1.4.0 calculators executable. Use the current README for its complete scope.

Job | What to install | Where it runs | What it will not do
Apply a statutory test to your own figures | Aus Accounting MCP | Local stdio MCP: Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Codex | No hosted ATO corpus, formation of Division 7A amalgamated loans or lodgement.
Look up ATO guidance, legislation and public rulings | A document-retrieval MCP such as ato-mcp | Typically a hosted remote MCP | Not a reviewed calculator for Payday Super timing or ATO benchmark ratios
Walk an agent through a public practice workflow | australian-accounting-skills | Claude Code / Codex plugin, or npx --yes skills@1.5.22 add | Does not treat recorded figures as current rates. Sends the agent to the applicable authoritative source for current figures.
Bounded GST, resident tax, CGT, FBT, depreciation, quarterly SG or PAYG withholding arithmetic | Aus Accounting MCP with australian-tax-calculators | Local MCP | No HELP before v0.2.11, Medicare, offsets, scale 4 or irregular-pay PAYG withholding, or full tax return preparation. Each worksheet requires established facts and a supported period.

Those other projects are named so an agent can tell them apart. This page does not review them, and it does not speak for their authors.

The table leaves out one job: researching a technical question across rulings, cases and legislation. For that, start from the ATO Legal Database and the Federal Register of Legislation. Treat an AI tool’s citations as leads and open each source before relying on it.

## What aus-accounting-mcp does

- Lists and searches the shipped ATO small business benchmark industries.
- Compares the profit and loss buckets you supply to the published ATO ranges. Omitted buckets stay not_supplied; they are not treated as zero.
- Reviews one Payday Super contribution or a related group for one employer, using payday-super-checker. Missing fund receipt evidence remains unresolved.
- Reviews s 109N loan terms and s 109E minimum yearly repayments for one supplied amalgamated loan. Division 7A review is experimental and requires human review.
- The pinned v0.2.8 example calculates 7 experimental tax worksheets through calculate_tax_worksheet, with explicit scope and period checks.
- Searches and reads a configured local Markdown library with file and line citations. This is optional; the package includes no library.
- Emits fictional SBR fixtures for agent tests, labelled synthetic: true.

Payday Super and ATO benchmarks are delegated to reviewed engines, payday-super-checker and ato-benchmark-compare. The MCP server does not reimplement the law.

The worksheet scope and periods are fixed by the worksheet engine pinned in reference release v0.2.8. Resident basic tax covers full-year resident ordinary income for 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27, before offsets and levies. GST, CGT, depreciation and quarterly SG cover bounded 2025-26 cases; FBT covers the year ended 31 March 2026. The quarterly SG worksheet does not calculate post-June 2026 Payday Super entitlements. PAYG withholding covers one regular weekly, fortnightly or monthly pay from 1 July 2026 on Schedule 1 scale 1, 2, 3, 5 or 6, before tax offsets and Medicare levy adjustments.

Read aus-accounting://scope before confirming worksheet inputs. Keep the exclusions returned with each result. The release instructions also explain optional local library setup. Any retrieved excerpts enter the calling assistant’s context.

## Primary sources

Payday Super timing draws on the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992 and Australian Taxation Office, LCR 2026/2. Benchmark comparisons use the ATO’s small business benchmarks. The limited Division 7A review applies sections 109N and 109E of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936.

Each engine’s source review and release record state what was checked. Verify current sources and the supplied facts before using an output.

## Try two tool calls

With uv installed, run the published demonstration without configuring an AI client:

```
uvx --from aus-accounting-mcp==0.2.8 aus-accounting-mcp-demo
```

Expected: exit 0 and a JSON transcript containing generate_synthetic_sbr_fixture and review_div7a_loan. The demonstration calls the local tools with fictional facts. It needs no credentials, performs no lodgement and does not evaluate an agent’s behaviour.

The transcript’s first line shows the source-checkout command, uv run --locked aus-accounting-mcp-demo. The command above runs the published v0.2.8 package under the MIT License. Its full output includes the engine’s caveats; retain those with any extracted result.

## Adopt

The current published release is aus-accounting-mcp/v0.13.0, published on 25 November 2026 and verified on GitHub, PyPI and the MCP registry on 26 November 2026. With calculator release 1.4.0, the server exposes 148 worksheet kinds. Read aus-accounting://scope for each worksheet’s periods, scope and required inputs. The v0.12.0 release served 102 worksheet kinds with calculators 1.2.0 and v0.11.0 served 66 with calculators 1.1.0; the v0.9.0 release history and v0.2.8 demonstration are preserved below.

Install the calculator separately for Claude Code or Codex. Put it on PATH or set AUS_TAX_CALCULATORS_BIN to its absolute path. The server verifies the executable’s SHA-256. It recognises the released x86-64 Linux and Windows digests. For a source build, set AUS_TAX_CALCULATORS_SHA256 to its verified digest. The server needs permission to run the verified copy from its temporary directory. The v0.13.0 Claude Desktop bundle includes the calculator on x86-64 Linux and Windows.

### Release v0.10.0

Release v0.10.0 added BSB and bank account number format tests against AusPayNet’s published formats. A valid format establishes no institution, account or payee. This release moved the 14 worksheets to a separately installed calculators executable and corrected the amount the contribution cap worksheet reports as carried forward.

### Release v0.9.0 and earlier

Release v0.9.0 requires Python 3.14 or later; v0.3.0 remains available for Python 3.11 to 3.13 and v0.2.12 for Python 3.10. Since v0.2.8 it has added contribution cap, account-based pension minimum, study and training support loan repayment, Schedule 8 study loan withholding, annual Medicare levy, low income tax offset and Division 293 worksheets, bringing the total to 14, and pins newer engine releases; v0.3.0 moves Division 7A review to 0.2.0, which finishes a review with an extremely large remaining term instead of hanging. It can also search and read ATO rulings from a point-in-time local copy you configure, and its benchmark comparison adds the labour, rent and motor vehicle ranges from the ATO’s industry pages, which never set the key ratio. Release v0.6.0 adds two GST review tools from the new gst-review engine: one gives each coded bank line a review state against the supplied GST registration dates, and the other compares lodged G1, G2, G3, G10, G11, 1A and 1B figures with the ledger for each period on the cash or accruals basis. Neither classifies a supply or prepares, revises or lodges a BAS. It also pins the Apache-2.0 releases of the Payday Super, benchmark and Division 7A engines, which change no check, comparison or review. The annual Medicare levy worksheet does not adjust payroll withholding. Release v0.7.0 adds lodgment due-date lookup and a bundled-data freshness report; missing facts or recorded periods remain UNKNOWN. Release v0.7.1 changes no tool output except engine_version. Release v0.8.0 moves to the Ryan Duguid Public Attribution Licence 1.0 and adds 3 tools, bringing the total to 25: a reviewed ATO rate or threshold for a date, quoted from its ATO page, and ABN and ACN check-digit tests that contact no register. Its searches now match whole words only, and the rate search leaves out superseded rows unless in_force_only is false. Its Payday Super tools refuse a contribution marked returned_by_fund, because the pinned checker cannot assess returns. They do not detect a return, so every ON_TIME verdict carries a caveat that returned contributions were not assessed. Those changes are outside this guide’s v0.2.8 worked example.

Release v0.9.0 pins payday-super-checker 0.2.3, ato-benchmark-compare 0.2.2 and australian-tax-calculators 0.2.0. The pinned v0.2.8 example ranks local legislation search results best first and reads long provisions in parts.

### Five ways to try it

Start with the Excel cash flow example or browser calculator. Firms using Claude Code or Codex can use the commands below. An MCP server gives an AI assistant access to a defined set of tools.

No install

Open the browser calculator with fictional figures. Nothing to install, and this site’s code does not send the figures you enter to a server.

Open the fictional Excel forecast in desktop Excel, or send a reproducible evaluation to whoever manages your systems.

Claude Code

Needs Python 3.14 or later and uv. Release v0.13.0 uses the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Check the version uvx installs.

```
# Australian Accounting & Tax MCP server for Claude Code
claude mcp add aus-accounting -- uvx aus-accounting-mcp
```

Codex

Needs Python 3.14 or later and uv. Release v0.13.0 uses the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Check the version uvx installs.

```
# Australian Accounting & Tax MCP server for Codex
codex mcp add aus-accounting -- uvx aus-accounting-mcp
```

Skills

Needs Git and Node. This installs the 65 workflows in v0.4.0 under the Apache License 2.0.

```
# Run from the project where you want the released skills
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting-skills.git accounting-skills-release
git -C accounting-skills-release checkout --detach v0.4.0
npx --yes skills@1.5.22 add ./accounting-skills-release --agent codex claude-code --skill '*' --yes --copy
```

This copies the released skills into the current project’s Codex and Claude Code directories. An agent runtime is still required.

Clone once per project. To repeat or retry from that directory, rerun only the checkout and install commands.

Development installation

This command installs the default branch, which can be ahead of the v0.4.0 release.

```
npx --yes skills@1.5.22 add ryanduguid/australian-accounting-skills
```

GitHub workflows

github-agent-skills gives Codex and Claude Code the GitHub maintenance workflows this portfolio uses, and keeps the fictional-data and human review boundaries.

Needs Git and rustup for validation. Development checkout: clones the default branch, not a tagged release.

```
# GitHub maintenance workflows for Codex and Claude Code: https://github.com/ryanduguid/github-agent-skills
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/github-agent-skills.git
cd github-agent-skills
rustup toolchain install
cargo run --manifest-path tools/github-skills/Cargo.toml --locked -- validate-skills --strict
```

A fresh clone includes both runtime copies and needs no synchronisation. For another project, copy .claude/skills/ for Claude Code or .agents/skills/ for Codex into that project’s matching directory.

### Pinned and unpinned installs

The MCP install commands above are unpinned. uvx may reuse a cached environment or an already installed tool, so an unpinned command does not guarantee the latest release on every run. Upgrade deliberately, and check which version you are running before you compare a result with anything. The pinned command under Try two tool calls reproduces release 0.2.8, and each evaluation keeps the release it was run against.

The Skills commands pin the installer to version 1.5.22. The primary Skills installation uses the Apache-licensed v0.4.0 tag. The current Skills release is v0.8.1, published on 25 November 2026, with 112 workflows under the Apache License 2.0. For development installs, check the licence in the checkout. The development Skills and GitHub workflow commands install the default branch, which can include work no tagged release carries. Individual tool pages name the release their worked example reproduces.

aus-accounting-mcp is published on PyPI and from its source repository. Source on GitHub, PyPI and registry record. payday-super-checker is already on PyPI. The official Model Context Protocol registry lists this server as io.github.ryanduguid/aus-accounting.

Software issue using fictional data? Open an issue or email with the tool named in the subject. If the email link does not open, the contact page spells the address out. Wrong rate, date or rule on this page? Report a correction.

## Limits

The calculation engines and MCP server run locally. Installation downloads packages. If you use a cloud-backed AI host, supplied arguments, tool results and local library excerpts may be sent to that host’s model provider. Check the host’s configuration and data handling before supplying information.

The optional LodgeiT calculator adapter is separate, unreleased development code and off by default. It makes network calls only with explicit enablement, a configured base URL and an allowed host. The standard MCP server does not use it as a fallback. Website hosting and browser data handling have their own boundaries.

Published MCP 0.2.8 pins Payday Super Checker 0.1.7. A timely receipt date without an amount remains UNKNOWN; a late receipt without an amount cannot reduce the shortfall. Older MCP 0.2.4 pins checker 0.1.6 and retains its full-receipt assumption. Review the version-specific receipt rules before interpreting a result.

The tools calculate and refuse. Professional judgement and lodgement stay human. Tool results and any local library excerpts enter the calling assistant’s context. Public fixtures use fictional data only.

## Common questions

### What is aus-accounting-mcp?

A local Model Context Protocol server for ATO benchmark comparison, Payday Super timing, limited Division 7A review and optional search of a configured Markdown library. The reference example uses v0.2.8 and its 7 worksheets. Published v0.13.0 serves 148 worksheet kinds with the 1.4.0 calculators executable, alongside GST coding and BAS reconciliation review. Outputs need human review.

### Is aus-accounting-mcp a hosted ATO document library?

No. Aus Accounting MCP is a separate project from ato-mcp. It ships no ATO document library and does not fetch rulings or legislation from the web. You can configure a local Markdown folder for search and reading with file and line citations. Retrieved excerpts enter the calling assistant’s context.

### Does it calculate Division 7A repayments?

Aus Accounting MCP reviews s 109E minimum yearly repayments for one supplied amalgamated loan. This is experimental and requires human review. It refuses loan formation, s 109R repayment classification, unpaid present entitlements and distributable surplus.

### Does it lodge with the ATO?

No. It does not lodge, declare or replace a registered agent. SBR payloads it can emit are fictional test fixtures.

### When is a Payday Super contribution on time?

Since 1 July 2026, the fund must receive it within 7 business days of payday, or 20 business days for a first contribution to a new fund. Sending money to a clearing house does not stop the clock.

### Who maintains these tools?

Ryan Duguid is an Australian senior accountant based in Newcastle, NSW. He is a Provisional CA ANZ Member. He is not the US software product executive of the same name.

### Where is aus-accounting-mcp available?

On PyPI and from its source repository. Install with the commands under Adopt; they name the repository and the executable.

### Is aus-accounting-mcp on the official MCP registry?

Yes. The listing name is io.github.ryanduguid/aus-accounting. The install commands under Adopt are the maintained path.

# Workpaper Review Gate for manager review packs

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/workpaper-review-gate/

> Current release review-ready-gate v1.1.0. Check BAS, month-end or year-end packs before manager review. Incomplete files return to the preparer.

# Workpaper Review Gate

The Workpaper Review Gate inspects a folder of workpapers and answers READY, NOT_READY or BLOCKED.

Current release review-ready-gate v1.1.0, 25 November 2026, from the accounting-review-pipeline repository. Release licence: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Published 25 August 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Rust

Needs

Windows, Linux or macOS on x86_64 or aarch64. The executable runs without Python or Rust.

Boundary

READY means ready for human review, not approved or signed off.

Get review-ready-gate Inspect the fictional BAS pack

## Gate a corrected BAS pack

```
review-ready gate --profile bas --pack examples/bas-ready --output ../../../review-ready-demo/bas-ready
```

Overall status: READY (0 findings)

Incomplete BAS fixture returns NOT_READY with 3 findings in v0.1.3. Inspect both fictional packs.

A missing GST control export, an unsigned self-review or a trial balance that does not balance never reaches the manager.

## Inspect a fictional BAS pack

Release review-ready-gate/v0.1.3 returns NOT_READY for its incomplete pack and READY with no findings for its corrected pack. Both runs were reproduced on 17 October 2026 using the unchanged fictional fixtures.

Three findings in the incomplete pack’s generated findings.csv.

Supplied evidence | Finding code | Status
gst_control_gl.csv is absent. | MISSING_ARTEFACT | NOT_READY
pack_complete, tie_outs_done and self_reviewed are false in self_review.json. | SELF_REVIEW_INCOMPLETE | NOT_READY
Item OI-002 is BLOCKING and OPEN, with no resolution in open_items.csv. | OPEN_ITEM_BLOCKING | NOT_READY

Download the generated findings.csv, including the reasons, repeat flag and reviewer actions. Inspect the incomplete input pack and corrected input pack at that release.

The corrected pack’s generated cover sheet records Overall status: READY and Findings: 0 total; 0 blocked; 0 not ready; 0 repeats. A human still decides whether the file is acceptable. The fixed-release evaluation gives both reproduction commands.

Preparation got cheaper and review did not. Offshore teams, juniors and AI agents can produce a file faster than a manager can reconstruct it, so managers spend their review time finding the missing tie-out, the open item still sitting in email and the same error as last period.

Point the CLI at a pack directory. It checks that the required artefacts are present, that the preparer has certified the pack, that blocking open items are cleared and that the trial balance balances. For a BAS pack, it also checks that 1A less 1B ties to the GST control movement. A READY pack may enter manager review. The tool still does not decide that the work is correct.

## What this tool does

- Gates BAS, month-end and year-end packs before they reach a reviewer.
- Writes a cover sheet, a findings CSV and a hashed JSON pack a manager can archive.
- Flags findings that were still OPEN on the prior pack as repeats.

## Limits

Local files only. No Xero connection, no lodgement, no LLM, no period lock. A READY result is not sign-off.

Release v1.1.0 is under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later; v1.0.0 and v1.0.1 are under the Ryan Duguid Public Attribution Licence 1.0, and earlier releases keep their own licences. No warranty.

## Get it

Download review-ready-gate/v1.1.0 for Windows, Linux or macOS on x86_64 or aarch64 under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. The review-ready executable runs without Python or Rust. The release guide shows how to verify the download and its signed provenance.

### Reproduce the v0.1.3 example

The evaluation of 2 fictional BAS packs uses v0.1.3 under the MIT License. To run its corrected pack with the commands below, install Git and Python 3.10 or later.

```
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/accounting-review-pipeline.git
git -C accounting-review-pipeline checkout review-ready-gate/v0.1.3
cd accounting-review-pipeline/packages/review-ready-gate
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
review-ready gate --profile bas --pack examples/bas-ready --output ../../../review-ready-demo/bas-ready
```

The output goes outside the clone on purpose. A readiness pack names a client’s file and its open findings, so it belongs outside version control rather than behind an ignore entry the next commit can waive. Releases v0.1.7 to v0.1.9 refuse an output inside a version control checkout. The path above leaves the clone, which is what you want when you run these commands from an ordinary directory. If you are already inside another checkout, point --output at a directory outside that one instead.

Source on GitHub

Software issue using fictional data? Open an issue or email with the tool named in the subject. If the email link does not open, the contact page spells the address out. Wrong rate, date or rule on this page? Report a correction.

## Common questions

### Is READY the same as approved?

No. READY means no configured gate tripped on the files that were present. A human still decides whether the file can be signed or lodged.

### Does this replace monthly close review?

No. Monthly Close Controls still produces the exception pack once a trial balance is allowed onto the desk. This tool sits upstream of that.

### Can it change a client’s ledger?

No. It reads local files and writes a readiness pack. It cannot post, pay, lodge or lock a period.

# Australian accounting tools and site changelog

Source: https://duguid.com.au/changelog/

> Trace changes to the calculators, rate tables and accounting tools by date, with links to tagged releases and the evidence for each change.

# Changelog

Follow this changelog as an Atom feed.

What changed and when, across this site and the tagged tool releases. Dates are Australian Eastern time.

## Site

Date | Change
27 November 2026 | The depreciation register distinguishes assets with the same name, shows the dates recorded against asset group headings and links directly to sections of long tables. The work expenses and rental property calculators now label telephone expenses as dollar amounts.
27 November 2026 | The Markdown editions of calculators now preserve the instructions shown when JavaScript is off, including the link to the depreciation register data file.
27 November 2026 | Reference tables now carry names for screen readers. Calculator fields and reference pages have more space between headings, instructions and tables. The depreciation register identifies the industry or asset group on links that share a name. Each indexed page also has a Markdown edition at index.md.
26 November 2026 | A new business calculator, sole trader against company, puts one business profit for 2021-22 to 2026-27 through both structures: as a sole trader, tax and the Medicare levy on the whole profit less the small business income tax offset under Subdivision 328-F; through a company, a salary with its super guarantee, company tax at 25% or 30%, a fully franked dividend for the rest of what the owner takes out with its top-up tax, the profit kept in the company and the tax on the super. It states each total and the difference and recommends no structure, and names what it leaves out: the personal services income rules, Division 7A, the small business CGT concessions, state taxes and the cost of running a company. Rates were read on 26 November 2026.
26 November 2026 | Added the 183-day residency day count: the days in Australia in an income year from 2020-21 to 2026-27, added up from arrival and departure days, against the 183-day test and its exception. It does not decide residency, and agrees with the australian-accounting residency-tests command on 667 test cases.
26 November 2026 | A new business calculator, casual and overtime pay, works one employee’s gross pay for a pay period from the base hourly rate, casual loading and penalty and overtime rates you enter, and the 12% super guarantee on ordinary time earnings, leaving overtime out and keeping the casual loading in, for paydays from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2027. It holds no award rates: the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides and Pay and Conditions Tool give them.

It also works out one employee’s super guarantee charge: the final shortfall, notional earnings at the GIC rate and the administrative uplift, reduced for a first offence and a voluntary disclosure, or, for a quarter to June 2026, the shortfall, 10% nominal interest and the $20 administration component.
18 November 2026 | The individual tax calculators go back to 2020-21 (take-home pay to 2021-22), with the low and middle income tax offset for 2020-21 and 2021-22. The income tax calculator adds the Medicare levy surcharge, for singles and families and the days without private hospital cover, any study loan repayment and a refund or amount owing from the tax you enter as withheld. The take-home pay calculator takes a salary for a year, month, fortnight or week and salary sacrificed to super, names concessional contributions above the cap and Division 293, and for a 2026-27 pay gives the PAYG withheld under the ATO’s Schedules 1 and 8, which match all 288 of the ATO’s sample amounts. Each new rate and threshold was read on 18 November 2026 in the Act or on the ATO’s page for that year.
17 November 2026 | A new business calculator works out one person’s Division 296 tax for 2026-27 from the total superannuation balance at 30 June 2027 and the year’s total superannuation earnings: 15% on the share of earnings above $3 million and a further 10% above $10 million, with the child recipient, structured settlement and death exceptions. Its thresholds, rates, rounding and definitions were read on 17 November 2026 in the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, compilation 268, the transitional provisions and the Imposition Act, and it agrees with examples 1.1 and 1.2 of the Explanatory Memorandum. It works out one year from supplied figures and projects nothing.

17 November 2026 | A new business calculator sets out a complying Division 7A loan year by year over its 7-year or 25-year term: each minimum yearly repayment at that year’s benchmark rate, the interest and principal, what a larger repayment does to later minimums and the shortfall subsection 109E(1) takes to be a dividend. Rates to 2026-27 are the ATO’s, each cited; later years use a rate you assume and are marked as a projection. It can show the dividend that would fund each repayment at a marginal rate you give, and it refuses loans made before 4 December 1997, refinanced loans, loans through an interposed entity and repayments before the lodgment day.

16 November 2026 | A new vehicle classifier works out from a manufacturer’s specification whether a vehicle is a car under section 995-1, so whether the car limit and the GST credit cap apply, whether luxury car tax can apply at the 2025-26 or 2026-27 threshold and whether an employer’s FBT exemption for an eligible vehicle can apply on the private use you state. It works MT 2024’s dual cab test, LCTD 2023/1’s ute method and TD 2006/40’s order of the credit and the car limit, and refuses a modified vehicle without its compliance plate figures, a payload that disagrees with the mass and kerb weight, and any other body it cannot weigh. It leaves the car limit undecided for a single cab ute or panel van, which no ATO source settles. The car limit table now says the limit reaches a car designed mainly for carrying passengers, rather than excluding only utes and vans over 1 tonne.

24 September 2026 | The cash flow chart on the homepage and the cash flow example was re-exported from the workbook with larger text, plus a narrower version for phones, so its axis labels and callouts are readable at the size the page shows them. The figures are unchanged.
24 September 2026 | Copy edit on Home, About, Tools and Evaluations: repeated disclaimers removed, homepage headings made parallel without full stops, and negative amounts and percentages written one way.
24 September 2026 | The homepage drops a worked example that repeated a task row, lines its section headings up with the main heading, and shortens the note under the hero. The Human and Machine view switch moved into the header, so it no longer covers text while scrolling.
24 September 2026 | The Australian tax tools for AI agents page now documents MCP release 0.2.7, which adds a Schedule 1 PAYG withholding worksheet for regular weekly, fortnightly and monthly pays from 1 July 2026, bringing the bounded tax worksheets to seven.
22 September 2026 | The car limit page now explains which GST credits reduce the cost. Division 7A figures are qualified for companies with a 30 June year end, with guidance for substituted accounting periods. Workpaper Review Gate describes its released output safeguard. The machine index, tool source dates, financial year labels and Newcastle spelling were corrected, and generated text copies were refreshed.
22 September 2026 | The homepage now leads with Open source tools for Australian accountants and gives clearer starting points for accounting tasks. Mobile links gained larger touch targets and layouts support enlarged text. Pure dark mode remains, with brighter homepage text, a smaller headline, sentence-case labels and simpler dividers. Unnecessary hyphens were removed across the site, stylesheet URLs were refreshed, and all five messaging preview cards were updated.
20 September 2026 | Actions from the 20 September GEO audit: Evaluations joined the primary navigation; the Privacy page states which AI crawlers may fetch and cite and which training crawlers are disallowed; llm-tax-guardrails is labelled an external GitHub guide, not a site tool, on the refusals page and in the machine-readable index; the index review date moved to 20 September and lists the Atom feed, which the homepage now advertises.
20 September 2026 | The 100 accounting questions moved to ten topic pages and the nine business calculators to one page each, with the old addresses kept as indexes. Three rates tables added: the maximum super contribution base, the car limit for depreciation, and the FBT rate and gross-up rates. The homepage scope strip and the Tools category links were removed, six page titles lost the site-name suffix, breadcrumbs reached every page, secondary text and form controls grew on small screens, and an Atom feed of this changelog was added.
20 September 2026 | Actions from the 19 September site audits: the Coal LSL calculator now takes a reporting month on every branch, refuses months before July 2023 and exports the exact wage basis and period in its CSV; the Payday and ATO benchmark pages carry their matching-quality and missing-bucket warnings beside the download steps; installation routes are labelled released, pinned or development; the evaluation email copy, franking introduction, cents-per-kilometre and WIP scope notes, privacy wording, machine index super summary, README tool count and changelog caption were corrected; Ozzit joined the evaluation chooser.
14 September 2026 | The six webfonts return to IBM’s unmodified Latin1 files, the response header notes separate the GitHub Pages origin from the Cloudflare edge, the cash forecast names the dates it accepts, and the Coal LSL page explains the incorporated base pay definition.
11 September 2026 | Updated MCP capabilities and current release references, added verified trust and company tax examples, and widened the refusal tables for mobile reading.
6 September 2026 | The Tools page gained a Related resources section holding the third-party libraries, official guidance, and primary sources from the separate index repository, which is now archived; the footer links there instead.
4 September 2026 | Every link to a repository archived after the September 2026 consolidation now points at its maintained home in the monorepos, the 3 evaluations were rerun against the namespaced monorepo releases, and the site checks fail on any link that resolves to an archived repository.
2 September 2026 | Copy edit across the tool, rate, and evaluation pages, About, Contact, and Evidence: duplicated paragraphs removed, stray adverbs and rhetorical contrasts cut, disclaimers and bylines put in the active voice, and the super guarantee page moved to the site’s per cent style.
2 September 2026 | Font preloads and a Content Security Policy on every page, entry headings on the Rates and Evaluations hubs, a no-script notice on the Coal LSL calculator, a security.txt contact file, and repository tooling removed from the published origin.
31 August 2026 | Engage parked. The site remains a personal open source tool index, not a practice, and is not accepting professional engagements through this site.
30 August 2026 | Navigation, adoption, and accessibility refinements across the register, with contact and changelog pages added.
30 August 2026 | Coal LSL calculator month validation and print recalculation fixes, and the split 2013-14 super guarantee history row.
29 August 2026 | Adoption-first homepage, the Tools, Rates, and Evaluations hubs, contextual share cards, and calculator print and CSV improvements.
28 August 2026 | True-black register redesign, self-hosted IBM Plex subsets, and the register-seal site icon.

# Monthly Close Controls: Xero close exception report

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/monthly-close-controls/

> Current release monthly-close-control-plane v1.2.0. Compare Xero trial balance CSVs locally and flag exceptions for human review.

# Monthly Close Controls

Monthly Close Controls compares current and prior Xero-shaped trial balance CSVs and writes an exception report for a human reviewer.

Current release monthly-close-control-plane v1.2.0, 25 November 2026, from the accounting-review-pipeline repository. Release licence: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Published 11 September 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026.

Delivery

Rust

Needs

Git and Rust 1.99.0

Boundary

PASS applies to the configured checks. A human approves the close.

Inspect the eight exceptions Run the example

Fictional July close: REVIEW, including a $250 creditors difference. Read it in your browser; reproducing it needs Git and Rust.

## Fictional July close output

```
close-control: REVIEW; 8 exception(s); 6 client query(ies) drafted
```

Exit 2 (REVIEW) with a $250 creditors difference

Compares 31 July 2026 with 30 June 2026 at $10,000 and 10% thresholds. Inspect the 8 exceptions and CSVs.

It flags material movements, missing mappings and supplied subledger differences. It runs on local files without connecting to Xero.

## Worked example: balanced trial balance, unfinished review

The worked example runs the Rust source, version 1.0.0, at commit 1ce98d5, before its release.

The fictional example compares 31 July 2026 with 30 June 2026. With thresholds of $10,000 and 10%, and a reconciliation tolerance of $0.01, the result is REVIEW: 8 exceptions, none blocked, and 6 draft client queries.

### From supplied balances to an exception

Selected values for account 200, Trade Creditors. Amounts are AUD; a credit balance is negative.

File | Field | Value
current_trial_balance.csv | YTDCredit | 65000.00
subledger_balances.csv | SubledgerBalance | -64750.00
exceptions.csv | difference | -250.00

The engine compares -65000.00 with -64750.00 and writes subledger_reconciliation,REVIEW. Download the generated exceptions.csv with all 8 exceptions, or inspect the complete fictional input files at the same commit. Reproduced on 3 November 2026.

Exception | Result | Reviewer action
Creditors reconciliation | Trial balance less supplied subledger: −$250. | Trace the reconciling items and document their cause.
Account mapping | Operating Expenses, account 6000, has no supplied mapping. | Confirm the account’s review group.
Financial year reset | The comparison crosses 1 July. | Resolve the reset before treating profit and loss YTD differences as ordinary monthly movements.

Five threshold movements make up the remaining exceptions. The 8 exceptions are not 8 accounting errors. The review acknowledgement leaves the result at REVIEW.

### From an exception to a draft client query

Download the generated client-queries.csv with all 6 draft queries from the same fictional run. A preparer must review them before sending anything. A client answer does not clear an exception or approve the close.

One generated query, traced to its control, fictional tenant and account.

Field | Generated value
Query ID | Q-368abd6aff22
Source finding | period_variance for Varrock Ventures Pty Ltd, account ID 100, code 1000, Operating Bank.
Question | What drove the year-to-date movement in this account against the prior period?
Evidence requested | The transactions or documents behind the movement, and confirmation that no part of it belongs to another period. This comparison crosses a 30 June year-to-date reset, so confirm the movement is real before putting this query to anyone: a profit-and-loss account restarts at nil on 1 July.

The captured manager case study explains the selected exceptions. The command below reproduces the 4-file output at that same commit. All inputs are fictional.

## Inputs

Start with canonical CSVs written by the Xero trial balance exporter. The example uses these inputs:

- Current and prior trial balances, required: one organisation and one report date in each file. Both must name the same organisation, with the prior date earlier than the current date.
- Account mapping, optional: a CSV assigning accounts to review groups. With a supplied file, missing mappings are flagged for review. Omit it and the mapping control is not run.
- Subledger balances, optional: supplied balances to compare with the trial balance. Omit them and subledger reconciliation is not run.
- Review note, optional: a human acknowledgement. It does not clear exceptions or approve the close.

Set the absolute and percentage materiality thresholds and reconciliation tolerance for the review. Choose an output directory outside version control. The pinned source documentation defines the accepted files and controls.

## Outputs and status

- close-summary.md: overall status, thresholds, source hashes and the exception table.
- exceptions.csv: account-level differences, reasons and suggested reviewer actions for Excel or Power BI.
- client-queries.csv: draft questions for exceptions a client can help resolve. A preparer must review them before sending anything.
- close-review-pack.json: structured results and evidence for the run, including any supplied review acknowledgement.

PASS means the configured checks passed on the supplied files. REVIEW or BLOCKED requires attention and returns exit code 2. Malformed inputs, invalid configuration or an output path the tool refuses return exit code 1. A human decides whether the close is acceptable.

## Run the example

The example uses revision 1ce98d5 under FSL-1.1-ALv2. It needs Git and Rust installed with rustup. The component pins Rust 1.99.0 in rust-toolchain.toml, which rustup uses in that directory. The first build downloads the crates locked in Cargo.lock. It needs no Xero account, API access or client files.

```
git clone https://github.com/ryanduguid/accounting-review-pipeline.git
cd accounting-review-pipeline
git checkout 1ce98d50f1c81d9f9873d47986a33a42f40f4e96
cd packages/monthly-close-control-plane
```

```
cargo run --locked --release --bin close-control -- review --current examples/current_trial_balance.csv --prior examples/prior_trial_balance.csv --mapping examples/account_mapping.csv --subledger examples/subledger_balances.csv --absolute-threshold 10000 --percentage-threshold 0.10 --reconciliation-tolerance 0.01 --review-note examples/review_note.json --output ../../../close-control-demo
```

After Cargo’s build messages, expect exit code 2 and close-control: REVIEW; 8 exception(s); 6 client query(ies) drafted, followed by the absolute path of each of the 4 pack files. The output directory is beside the checkout. Keep review packs outside version control; the command refuses an output directory inside a checkout.

The current release, monthly-close-control-plane/v1.2.0, published on 25 November 2026, ships close-control as an executable for Linux, macOS and Windows on x86_64 and aarch64, with signed provenance, that needs no Rust toolchain, under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later. Its release guide shows how to verify a download.

Source on GitHub

Software issue using fictional data? Open an issue. Wrong rate, date or rule on this page? Report a correction.

## Reproduce a refusal: output inside the checkout

From the same component directory at source commit 1ce98d5, repeat the fictional example with only --output changed to ./close-control-demo:

```
cargo run --locked --release --bin close-control -- review --current examples/current_trial_balance.csv --prior examples/prior_trial_balance.csv --mapping examples/account_mapping.csv --subledger examples/subledger_balances.csv --absolute-threshold 10000 --percentage-threshold 0.10 --reconciliation-tolerance 0.01 --review-note examples/review_note.json --output ./close-control-demo
```

Expect exit code 1 and an output error saying the directory is inside the version-control checkout and naming that checkout. The command creates no pack. This guard runs before reading the input files, because review packs can contain client accounts and balances.

Use a new access-controlled directory outside version control for an actual review. The example proves this output-path refusal; it does not test every malformed input or establish that a close is acceptable.

## Limits

A balanced trial balance can still contain omissions, misclassifications or unsupported transactions. These checks use the files, mappings and thresholds you supply. They do not establish that the source records are complete or that an accounting treatment is correct.

The tool cannot post journals, make payments, lodge returns, lock a period or approve a close. It does not send the draft client queries. A reviewer must investigate the exceptions and record the decision through the firm’s workpaper process.

## Common questions

### Does Monthly Close Controls connect to Xero?

No. It reads local CSV files in the canonical Xero trial balance export format. Use the Xero trial balance exporter separately to obtain those files.

### Can I open the exception report in Excel?

Yes. Import exceptions.csv to filter the account-level findings, differences and reviewer actions. The tool also writes a Markdown summary and a JSON evidence pack.

### Does PASS approve the month-end close?

No. PASS means the configured checks passed on the supplied inputs. A human still reviews completeness, accounting treatment and the evidence before approving a close.

# Business calculators

Sixty-three free calculators that run in your browser with the formula, assumptions and primary source beside the inputs. No sign-up; inputs stay on your device.

Published 11 September 2026. Last checked 27 November 2026, the newest of the calculators’ source checks.

## Pricing, planning and loans

- GST calculator Work out GST, the GST-exclusive amount and the GST-inclusive amount for a wholly taxable supply at 10%, rounded once to cents.
- GST margin scheme calculator Whether the margin scheme can apply to a sale of land, a stratum unit or a long-term lease, the margin and its GST, and the GST it saves.
- GST adjustments calculator The 6 GST adjustments and tests.
- Business use share calculator Apportion an eligible cost by a supported business use percentage. It does not decide deductibility, depreciation or record sufficiency.
- Margin and markup calculator Gross profit, margin and markup from sales and direct cost, on a consistent GST basis and matching period.
- Break-even sales calculator Whole units and sales required to cover fixed costs from price and variable cost per unit.
- Hourly pricing calculator Required hourly rate before GST from annual costs, target profit and billable hours.
- Fixed fee pricing calculator A fixed fee from estimated hours at a rate or a cost and margin, with GST, monthly instalments and the effective hourly rate.
- Budget variance calculator Actual minus budget, the percentage of absolute budget and whether the difference is favourable or unfavourable.
- Loan repayment schedule calculator Every payment of a loan, weekly to yearly, in arrears or in advance, with an optional balloon; works out the payment, the amount, the term or the rate, with CSV export.
- Hire purchase and chattel mortgage schedule The same schedule for a hire purchase agreement or chattel mortgage, with the interest by income year and a journal for each payment.
- AASB 16 lease calculator A lessee’s lease liability, right-of-use asset, interest and depreciation by income year, with the journals, beside hire purchase and buying outright after GST and tax.
- Borrowing expenses calculator Section 25-25 borrowing expenses by income year from 2017-18, spread by days, with the $100 rule, refinancing and an optional AASB 9 column.
- Depreciation pools and capital works calculator A low-value pool at 18.75% and 37.5%, a general small business pool at 15% and 30% with the low pool value write-off, or a capital works deduction at 2.5% or 4%, for 2020-21 to 2026-27.
- Rental property calculator One owner’s rental income and deductions for a year: expenses by days let, interest on a mixed-use loan, capital works and second-hand assets, the net rent and its effect on tax.

- FBT car calculator Taxable value and FBT on one car for the FBT year ending 31 March 2027, by the statutory formula or operating cost method.
- FBT car parking calculator Whether car parking fringe benefits arise against the $11.48 threshold, and their taxable value by any of the 5 methods, for the FBT year ending 31 March 2027.
- FBT expense payment calculator Taxable value of an expense payment fringe benefit, external with the otherwise deductible rule or in-house by the in-house rules, for the FBT year ending 31 March 2027.
- FBT loan calculator Taxable value of a loan fringe benefit at the 8.27% statutory interest rate, with the otherwise deductible rule, for the FBT year ending 31 March 2027.
- Meal entertainment calculator Taxable value of meal entertainment fringe benefits by the 50/50 split or 12-week register method, for the FBT year ending 31 March 2027.
- FBT property calculator Taxable value of a property fringe benefit by the in-house or external rules, with the otherwise deductible rule and the $1,000 in-house reduction, for the FBT year ending 31 March 2027.
- Vehicle classifier Whether a vehicle is a car, and what follows for the car limit, the GST credit, luxury car tax, FBT and records.

- PCG 2021/4 allocation Each recipient’s tax on a professional firm’s profit, the effective tax rate and the ATO’s risk zone.
- GIC payment plan calculator What a tax debt costs by equal instalments, against paying it now, with GIC compounding daily.

- Division 7A loan schedule calculator A complying Division 7A loan year by year over 7 or 25 years: each minimum repayment, the interest, extra repayments and any shortfall taken to be a dividend.
- Division 296 tax calculator One person’s Division 296 tax on superannuation earnings for 2026-27, above $3 million and above $10 million.
- PSI rules checker Whether the personal services income rules apply, step by step through Divisions 84 to 87.
