# Depreciation rates: ATO effective lives in LI 2025/20

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/depreciation-rates/

> Every effective life in LI 2025/20 (F2025L01097), the Commissioner’s current determination, with both rates and a year’s deduction worked out.

# Depreciation rates and effective lives

The Income Tax Assessment (Effective Life of Depreciating Assets) Determination 2025 (LI 2025/20, F2025L01097), registered on 15 September 2025 and unamended on 13 November 2026, sets the 7,430 effective lives this page searches, each with both rates and the date it was last set.

Published 14 November 2026. Last reviewed 23 November 2026. Sources checked 13 November 2026.

## Find an asset

JavaScript is required to search and to work out a deduction. Every row is in the data file and in the registered determination; the rules and sources remain below.

Asset Industry (Table A)All industries

For example laptop, forklift, carpet or solar. Every word you type must appear in the row, the headings above it or its industry.

Search

Type an asset to search both tables of the determination at once, or choose your industry to see its rows first. Table A lists assets by industry and Table B lists assets used across industries. Under section 6 of the determination, an asset used in an industry named in Table A takes that industry’s life where a row describes the asset or its function; Table B applies where Table A does not.

General information, not tax advice. The search and the calculator run in your browser. The figures you enter stay there unless you open a link to the calculation. A search is kept in the page address so that it can be linked. An address holding a search or a calculation reaches this site’s host when it is opened.

On this page: find an asset, browse the tables, work out a year’s deduction, which determination applies, how a life becomes a rate, capped lives, pools, write-offs and the car limit, capital works, common questions, source and licence, changes and corrections and limits.

## Browse the tables

Open an industry in Table A or a letter in Table B to read its rows in the determination’s order. A row with no life is a heading for the rows indented under it, or points to another row.

## A page for every life

Each of the 7,430 effective lives has its own page, linked from its industry in Table A or its asset in Table B.

## Work out a year’s deduction

Enter a cost, an effective life, the day the asset was first used or installed ready for use and its taxable use to see its decline in value and deduction for each income year.

Choosing ‘Use this life’ on a row above fills in the life.

Decline in value inputs

Cost (AUD) Effective life (years) First used or installed ready for use Income year ending 30 June Taxable use (%) MethodDiminishing value Prime cost Both, side by side

Whole years, a decimal or a fraction as the determination prints it, such as 10, 7.5 or 6 2/3.

The share of your use of the asset that is for a taxable purpose, from 0 to 100.

Work out the deduction

Enter the inputs and work out the deduction.

Income years end on 30 June. The working assumes you hold the asset for all of each later year, at the same taxable use each year, with no second element of cost. Each year’s amount rounds to the nearest cent, with exact half cents rounded up.

The decline in value is worked out in full, and the deduction is reduced by the part of it attributable to use for a purpose other than a taxable purpose (subsection 40-25(2)). The ATO’s Guide to depreciating assets 2026 works a $6,000 computer used 50% for a taxable purpose: it declines by $1,500, the deduction is $750 and its value at the year’s end is $4,500.

Choose ‘Both, side by side’ to compare the 2 methods; you still choose one for each asset (section 40-65). Once the schedule is drawn you can copy a citation line for a working paper or a link that restores the calculation, download the schedule as CSV or print it.

An asset you started to hold before 10 May 2006 is not covered, because its diminishing value rate is 150% and not 200%. The calculator checks only the day of first use, so do not use it for an asset you held before 10 May 2006 and first used later.

## Which determination applies to your asset

The Commissioner’s life for an asset is the one in force when you entered a contract to acquire it, otherwise acquired it or started to construct it, where its start time falls within 5 years of then. Otherwise the life in force at the start time applies (subsection 40-95(2) of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997). Plant acquired before 11.45 am on 21 September 1999, by legal time in the Australian Capital Territory, has its own rule in that subsection.

The 2025 determination commenced on 16 September 2025 and repealed the 2015 determination. Each row’s ‘last updated’ date is the date the Commissioner last reviewed and determined that life. Where a row’s ‘last updated’ date is later than the time that rule fixes for your asset, check the life in force at that time. Earlier lives were published in tables attached to taxation rulings, a practice that ended when TR 2022/1 was withdrawn, as the ATO says on its page Effective life determinations, rulings and law.

TR 2022/1 was withdrawn with effect from 31 October 2025 (TR 2022/1W), and the ATO’s legal database cites the 2025 determination as LI 2025/20.

You may instead work out an effective life yourself under section 40-105. You make the choice for the income year in which the asset’s start time occurs (subsection 40-95(3)).

## How a life becomes a rate

Prime cost spreads the cost evenly over the life: cost × (days held ÷ 365) × (100% ÷ effective life), and never more than the value left (section 40-75). Diminishing value works on the value left: base value × (days held ÷ 365) × (200% ÷ effective life), and never more than the base value, for an asset you started to hold on or after 10 May 2006 (section 40-72). An earlier asset uses 150% (section 40-70).

Days held can be 366 in a leap year and the divisor stays 365, as the ATO’s Guide to depreciating assets 2026 says. You choose one method for each asset (section 40-65) and cannot change it (section 40-130).

The rates shown beside each life are 100% and 200% divided by the life, rounded to 2 decimal places. The calculator works from the exact life, so the diminishing value rate for a life of 6 2/3 years is 30% and not 29.99%.

## Capped lives

A row marked ‘capped life available’ can take a shorter life set by section 40-102, where you use the Commissioner’s life and the cap that applies at the relevant time is shorter. Except for the vessel cap, a cap applies to an asset whose start time is on or after the date shown. The vessel cap applies to a vessel you hold on or after 1 July 2012; if you started to hold it before that day, the cap applies as if you started to hold it on that day.

The dates are set by the Acts that added each cap: the Taxation Laws Amendment Act (No. 4) 2002 (Schedule 4, item 15), the Tax Laws Amendment (2005 Measures No. 1) Act 2005 (Schedule 2, item 3), the Tax Laws Amendment (2006 Measures No. 7) Act 2007 (Schedule 5, item 2) and the Tax Laws Amendment (Shipping Reform) Act 2012 (Schedule 2, item 9).

## Pools, write-offs and the car limit

Four rules can replace or limit a deduction worked out from an effective life. Each is stated from the law in force on 1 October 2026, with the ATO’s figure where one is named. The depreciation pools calculator works out a low-value pool or a general small business pool for 2020-21 to 2026-27.

### Low-value pool

A low-cost asset costs less than $1,000 at the end of the income year you start to use it, and can go into a low-value pool (section 40-425). Each year the pool declines by 18.75% of the taxable use percentage of the cost of low-cost assets added that year, and by 37.5% of the pool’s closing balance for the year before together with the taxable use percentage of the opening adjustable value of low-value assets added that year (section 40-440). A low-value asset is one already depreciated by diminishing value whose opening adjustable value is under $1,000, and that is not a low-cost asset.

Once you pool one low-cost asset, each later one goes in too, and an asset stays in the pool (section 40-430). An asset deducted under the small business rules cannot be pooled this way. Nor, in assessments for 2026-27 and later income years, can an asset that, when you first used it or had it installed ready for use, you reasonably expected to use mainly to earn your assessable labour income (subsection 40-425(9)). An asset allocated to a pool for 2025-26 or an earlier income year is unaffected (item 17 of Schedule 4 to the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Act 2026).

### Small business pool and instant asset write-off

A small business entity, with aggregated turnover under $10 million, that chooses simplified depreciation deducts the taxable purpose proportion of an asset costing less than $20,000 in the year it is first used or installed ready for use (sections 328-110 and 328-180). It must be a small business entity, and have chosen simplified depreciation, both for that year and for the year it started to hold the asset. The $20,000 threshold is permanent for assets first used or installed ready for use on or after 1 July 2026, under the Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 2) Act 2026.

A temporary rule gives the same $20,000 for assets first acquired at or after the 2015 budget time and first used or installed ready for use from 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2026 (section 328-180 of the Income Tax (Transitional Provisions) Act 1997). Other assets go to the general small business pool, deducted at 15% in their first year and 30% of the opening balance after that (section 328-190). Where the pool’s balance before that year’s deduction is under $20,000, the whole balance is deducted (section 328-210).

### Assets costing $300 or less

The decline in value of an asset costing $300 or less that you start to hold in an income year is its cost where you use it mainly to earn assessable income that is not from carrying on a business (subsection 40-80(2)). The asset must not be part of a set, or one of several identical or substantially identical items, that you start to hold in that income year and that cost more than $300 in total. Use of the asset for a purpose other than a taxable purpose reduces the deduction (subsection 40-25(2)).

### Car limit

The cost of a car designed mainly for carrying passengers is reduced to the car limit for the financial year you started to hold it: $69,883 for 2026-27 and $69,674 for 2025-26 (section 40-230 and the ATO’s figures). The limit does not apply to a car fitted out for transporting disabled people in wheelchairs for profit, or to one that is over the limit only because of modifications that let a person with a disability use it for a taxable purpose (subsection 40-230(2)). Car limit for depreciation gives each year and its source.

## Capital works

Construction costs of capital works are deducted under Division 43 and not by effective life: 2.5% a year for works begun after 26 February 1992, or 4% for parts used in the ways Table 43-145 lists (section 43-25). Those uses include short-term traveller accommodation and industrial activities and, for works begun after 7:30 pm by legal time in the Australian Capital Territory on 9 May 2023, build to rent.

Works begun before 27 February 1992 and used as Table 43-140 describes take 4% if begun after 21 August 1984 and before 16 September 1987, and 2.5% in any other case (subsection 43-25(2)). The ATO’s Rental properties 2026 guide shows no deduction for construction started before 22 August 1979. No deduction is available for a period before construction is complete (section 43-30). The depreciation pools calculator works out a capital works deduction for works begun from 16 September 1987.

## Common questions

### Is TR 2022/1 still the ruling to use for effective lives?

No: the Commissioner withdrew TR 2022/1 with effect from 31 October 2025 (TR 2022/1W). The Commissioner makes effective life determinations by legislative instrument and, on the ATO’s page last updated 17 November 2025, names the 2025 determination (LI 2025/20, F2025L01097), which this page searches, as the current one.

### Which life applies to an asset acquired before the 2025 determination?

The life in force when you entered a contract to acquire the asset, otherwise acquired it or started to construct it, where its start time falls within 5 years of then; otherwise the life in force at the start time (subsection 40-95(2)). Where a row’s ‘last updated’ date is later than that time, check the life in force then.

### Must I use the Commissioner’s effective life?

No: you can instead work out an effective life yourself under section 40-105, choosing it for the income year in which the asset’s start time occurs (subsection 40-95(3)). Where you use the Commissioner’s life for a row marked ‘capped life available’, section 40-102 gives the capped life instead if it is shorter.

### How does private use change the deduction?

You work out the decline in value in full and reduce the deduction by the part of it attributable to use for a purpose other than a taxable purpose (subsection 40-25(2)). In the ATO’s guide, a $6,000 computer used 50% for a taxable purpose declines by $1,500, gives a deduction of $750 and is worth $4,500 at the year’s end.

## Source, licence and checks

Every row comes from Schedule 2 of the Income Tax Assessment (Effective Life of Depreciating Assets) Determination 2025 (LI 2025/20, F2025L01097), made on 2 September 2025 and registered on 15 September 2025. The data file holds all 9,311 rows, the source’s details and a count of every table row read.

A program builds the file from the Register’s EPUB and stops at any row it cannot read. On 13 November 2026 every row was compared with the Register’s Word version and with the text of its authorised PDF, with no difference in a description, life, mark or date.

Based on content from the Federal Register of Legislation at 13 November 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government legislation please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au.

The determination is reused under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence. Changes made here: Schedule 2 only, set out as data with each row’s nesting as a number, each life also in months and as 2 rates, dates in one form, plain spaces and hyphens, and 3 rows recorded one level shallower than the EPUB’s text sets them.

Ryan Duguid’s arrangement of the data file retains the Public Attribution 1.0 terms.

The rules beyond the tables were read on 13 November 2026 in the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 (Compilation No. 268, 1 October 2026), the Income Tax (Transitional Provisions) Act 1997 (Compilation No. 104) and in ATO guidance: the Guide to depreciating assets 2026, Rental properties 2026 and its pages on the 2 methods, the low-value pool and the car limit. The dates from which the capped lives and the labour income exclusion apply were read on 14 November 2026 in the amending Acts as made, as were the ATO’s legal database entries for LI 2025/20 and the withdrawal of TR 2022/1, and the guide’s example of an asset used partly for a taxable purpose. The ATO’s own depreciation and capital allowances tool works out deductions with more of an asset’s history.

## Limits

The page does not decide whether something is a depreciating asset, who holds it, what it cost or how far it is used for a taxable purpose. Check a life against the registered determination before relying on it.

The calculator leaves out balancing adjustments, second elements of cost, a taxable use that changes from year to year, pooling, the car limit, capped lives you have not entered and any rule that replaces these methods for a period. Diminishing value is not available for some assets, such as in-house software, intellectual property other than copyright in a film, and spectrum licences (subsection 40-72(2)). Section 40-27 can take away the deduction for a previously used asset in residential rental premises where the letting is not a business. A life the Commissioner has not listed can be worked out under section 40-105 or requested with the ATO’s effective life review application form.

# Tax returns

Practical steps, records and official guidance on tax returns.

10 of 10 answers checked between 27 September 2026 and 25 November 2026. Other guidance reviewed 11 September 2026. Page updated 25 November 2026.

1.

### What will my income tax bill be?

For 2026-27, a resident pays no tax on the first $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000 and 45% above that, plus the 2% Medicare levy. Start with taxable income for the correct income year, then account for levies, offsets, study loans and tax already withheld. A basic tax bracket result alone is incomplete.

- Gather income statements, investment statements, deductible expenses and PAYG credits.
- Use the ATO return estimate and reconcile each adjustment before treating it as a budget.

The linked experimental income tax worksheet excludes levies and offsets; check its supported years.

Your tax return · Tax rates for Australian residents · Experimental tax worksheets and supported years

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 1

2.

### Which expenses reduce my taxable income?

To claim a work-related expense, you must have paid it yourself without reimbursement, it must directly relate to earning your income, and you need a record to prove it, usually a receipt. From 2026-27, eligible taxpayers can claim a standard deduction of up to $1,000 for work-related expenses without records; it is reduced by any work-related expenses they claim that it covers. Most deductible expenses need a connection to earning assessable income and the evidence required for that type of claim; a few, such as gifts and donations, do not need that connection. Private spending and reimbursed amounts need separate treatment.

- List each expense, its purpose, date, amount and reimbursement.
- Record your work use calculation and check the ATO category before claiming.

A receipt proves spending, but does not by itself establish deductibility.

Deductions you can claim · Claiming deductions · Standard deduction for work-related expenses · Business use apportionment calculator

The bold answer was checked on 16 November 2026.

Link to question 2

3.

### What steps are involved in completing a return?

Most pre-fill data from employers, banks, health funds and government agencies is finalised by the end of July; check that it includes all your income before you lodge. If you lodge your own return, it is due by 31 October; to use a registered tax agent’s later dates, engage them before then. Collect the year’s records, reconcile them with pre-fill information, calculate supported claims, then review and lodge through an authorised channel.

- Check income statements are ready and account for income missing from pre-fill.
- Keep a copy of the reviewed return, declaration and lodgement receipt.

The checklist prepares your records; lodgement happens with the ATO or your registered agent.

Your tax return · Pre-fill availability · Preparing your tax return

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 3

4.

### Where can I obtain or recover my TFN?

Applying for a TFN is free, online or on paper depending on your residency and circumstances. If you have a TFN but can’t remember it, find it in ATO online services through myGov, or phone the ATO. Use the ATO’s TFN application or lost-TFN route. The right application process depends on residency and circumstances.

- If you already have a TFN, use the ATO recovery instructions before applying again.
- Complete any identity checks directly with the official service.

Do not put a TFN or identity documents into this website or a public issue.

Tax file number · Apply for a TFN · Lost or stolen TFN

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 4

5.

### What dates govern the annual tax cycle?

The income year runs from 1 July to 30 June. A return you lodge yourself is due by 31 October, quarterly BAS is due on 28 October, 28 February, 28 April and 28 July, and STP finalisation is due by 14 July. Build a calendar from the dates that apply to your return, activity statements, payroll and entity obligations.

- Record the period, lodgement date, payment date and responsible person for each obligation.
- Confirm the dates in your ATO account or with your registered agent; record any approved extension.

An agent’s program or a particular account can have different dates from a general calendar.

Your tax return · Preparing your tax return · Due dates for lodging and paying your BAS · Finalise your STP data by 14 July

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 5

6.

### Which methods can I use to settle my tax bill?

You can pay the ATO by BPAY, direct deposit, debit card, Government EasyPay, in person at Australia Post or through an international money remitter. Credit card payments are accepted until 30 June 2027. Use the ATO payment instructions for the relevant account and payment reference.

- Check the amount owing and available payment methods in the official service.
- Allow for processing time and keep the receipt; reconcile the payment when it appears.

This website does not collect payments or supply bank details.

Paying the ATO · How to pay

The bold answer was checked on 23 November 2026.

Link to question 6

7.

### Which earnings are taxable?

You must declare employment income, government payments and allowances, investment income such as interest, dividends, rent and capital gains, business, partnership and trust income, super pensions and annuities, and foreign income. Some compensation and insurance payments, scholarships, prizes and awards are also taxable. Check each source of income against the ATO’s categories. Amounts missing from pre-fill still need review.

- Reconcile employment, business, investment, government and foreign income records.
- List unusual receipts separately and record why they are included or excluded.

A bank deposit is not automatically taxable income, and taxable income is not limited to deposits.

ATO income, deductions and records · Income you must declare

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 7

8.

### How long will the tax return process take?

The ATO says most returns lodged online are processed within 10 business days. For a paper return, most refunds are issued within 50 business days. Separate your preparation time from the ATO’s processing time. Missing records, amendments and reviews can extend the overall process.

- Complete the record checklist before setting a preparation deadline.
- After lodgement, use the official progress service and respond to any information request.

No refund date or processing outcome is guaranteed here.

Your tax return · Check the progress of your tax return · How to lodge your tax return

The bold answer was checked on 25 November 2026.

Link to question 8

9.

### Where can I submit a completed return?

You can lodge online with myTax, through a registered tax agent or on paper by mail. Registered tax agents are the only people who can charge a fee to prepare and lodge your return. Individuals can use the lodgement options on the ATO’s tax return page, including myTax where eligible, a registered agent or paper.

- Choose the route for your circumstances and confirm the income year.
- Review the declaration and save the lodgement receipt after submission.

The site supplies preparation guidance and does not submit returns.

Your tax return · How to lodge your tax return

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 9

10.

### Which tax rules changed from 1 July 2026?

From 1 July 2026, the 16% personal tax rate fell to 15% and the cents per kilometre rate rose to 91 cents. From the same date, Payday Super generally requires contributions to reach the fund within 7 business days of payday, and the $20,000 instant asset write-off became permanent for small businesses. Most changes start on 1 July, so compare 2025-26 with 2026-27 rather than calendar years.

- Use the ATO 'Before you prepare your tax return' guidance for each year.
- Record each changed rate or rule, effective date, source and affected calculation in a change log.

An announcement is not evidence that a measure applied to your transaction. This is a review procedure, not an exhaustive legislative history.

Your tax return · Tax rates for Australian residents · Payment deadlines for Payday Super · $20,000 instant asset write-off, new legislation · Cents per kilometre rates on this site · Announced tax measures and enacted law

The bold answer was checked on 29 October 2026.

11.

### How do I calculate my working-from-home deduction?

Under the fixed rate method, you claim 70 cents for each hour you work from home in 2024-25 and 2025-26. The actual cost method is the alternative. Compare the eligible working-from-home methods for the income year using the required evidence for each.

- Record actual hours worked at home and the costs or rate that the chosen method covers.
- Keep separately claimed costs out of any category already included in the chosen method.

Eligibility, rates and record requirements must be checked for the year; this site does not select the method for you.

Deductions you can claim · Working from home fixed rate method · Business use apportionment calculator

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 11

12.

### What records do I need to support my working-from-home claim?

For the fixed rate method, keep a record of the actual hours you work from home for the whole year, such as a timesheet, roster or diary, because estimates are not accepted. Also keep at least one record, such as a bill, for each running expense the rate covers. Keep evidence of hours and costs that supports the particular working-from-home method you use.

- Record dates and hours throughout the required period and retain bills or receipts.
- Keep a note of the method, year, work use basis and costs excluded to prevent double claims.

A reconstructed estimate may not meet the ATO’s requirements for your method.

Deductions you can claim · Working from home fixed rate method

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 12

13.

### Should I use the cents-per-kilometre or logbook method for car expenses?

The cents per kilometre rate is 91 cents for 2026-27 (88 cents for 2024-25 and 2025-26), capped at 5,000 business kilometres per car. The logbook method has no kilometre cap but needs a valid logbook. Compare the methods you are eligible to use, using the same car and income year.

- For cents per kilometre, document eligible kilometres and check the year’s rate and cap.
- For the logbook method, gather a valid logbook, odometer readings and actual running costs.

Vehicle type, ownership and entity structure can change which methods are available.

Deductions you can claim · Cents per kilometre rates on this site · Logbook method · Cents-per-kilometre rate table and method

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 13

14.

### How do I keep a valid vehicle logbook?

A logbook must cover at least 12 continuous weeks and be broadly representative of your travel. It stays valid for 5 years, but you need a new 12-week logbook if your circumstances change. A useful logbook records each business trip and lets another person check the business use percentage.

- Record the required trip dates, odometer readings, distance and business purpose.
- Keep opening and closing odometer readings and review whether changed use requires a new logbook.

Check the ATO’s required recording period and validity conditions before relying on the logbook.

Deductions you can claim · Logbook method · Cents-per-kilometre rate table and method

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 14

15.

### How do I calculate the work-related share of phone and internet expenses?

Work out your work use percentage on a reasonable basis over a continuous 4-week period, using an itemised bill or your own record of work and private calls and internet use, then apply it to the whole income year. Apply a supported work use percentage to eligible phone and internet costs.

- Gather bills and a representative usage record that distinguishes private from work use.
- Use the business use calculator and retain the usage calculation with the result.

Do not separately claim costs already covered by your chosen working-from-home method.

Deductions you can claim · Mobile phone, mobile internet and other devices · Business use apportionment calculator

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 15

16.

### Can I deduct a laptop or tools immediately, or must I depreciate them?

An employee can deduct the work-related share of an item costing $300 or less straight away, unless it is part of a set costing more than $300; a dearer item is depreciated over its effective life. A small business with aggregated turnover under $10 million that uses the simplified depreciation rules can write off each eligible asset costing less than $20,000 that is first used or installed ready for use on or after 1 July 2023. Separate employee deductions from business asset rules, then identify whether immediate deduction or decline in value applies.

- Record cost, acquisition date, first use, work use share and whether the item forms part of a set.
- Check the applicable year’s asset rules and retain the calculation in an asset register.

The depreciation worksheet covers a bounded ordinary first-year method; it does not decide immediate-deduction eligibility.

Deductions you can claim · Assets costing $300 or less · Instant asset write-off · Experimental tax worksheets and supported years

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 16

17.

### Which work clothing, uniforms and laundry expenses can I claim?

You can claim clothing that is protective, a compulsory uniform, a registered non-compulsory uniform, or occupation-specific and not conventional. Laundry can be worked out at $1 a load of work clothing only, or 50 cents a load if mixed, and, for 2025-26 and earlier years, a laundry claim of $150 or less needs no written evidence; from 2026-27 that exception no longer applies. Work clothing claims depend on the type of clothing and its connection to your work. Wearing ordinary clothes at work does not establish a claim.

- Separate protective clothing, qualifying uniforms, occupation-specific clothing and ordinary items.
- Retain purchases and a supportable laundry calculation, with any reimbursement recorded.

Check the ATO category and evidence requirements before adding an amount to the return.

Deductions you can claim · Clothing, laundry and dry-cleaning expenses

The bold answer was checked on 2 November 2026.

Link to question 17

18.

### Can I claim course fees, professional memberships and self-education expenses?

Self-education is deductible when it maintains or improves the specific skills or knowledge you need for your current employment, or is likely to increase your income from it. Check how the course or membership relates to your current income-earning activities.

- Keep invoices, course details, the work connection and any employer reimbursement.
- Split private components and costs of gaining a new occupation from costs relevant to current work for review.

A professional label or employer recommendation alone does not settle the tax treatment.

Deductions you can claim · Self-education expenses

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 18

19.

### What can I claim if I have lost the receipt?

For 2025-26 and earlier years, if your total work-related expense claim is $300 or less, you can claim it without written evidence, but you must be able to show how you worked it out. From 2026-27 that exception no longer applies. Eligible taxpayers get a standard deduction of up to $1,000, or their labour income if less, without records. Work-related expenses claimed in the return generally need written evidence, although the travel and overtime meal allowance exceptions remain, and most of them reduce the standard deduction; union and professional association fees do not. Keep any written evidence for 5 years from your return's due date, or from the date you lodge it if that is later, and longer while a dispute with the ATO about the claim is unresolved. Try to replace missing evidence before deciding whether a claim can be supported.

- Request duplicate invoices or download supplier records and match them to payment evidence.
- Write down the expense, work purpose, missing record and the ATO evidence rule you relied on.

A bank statement or a general receipt exception does not automatically support every claim.

ATO income, deductions and records · Records you need to keep

The bold answer was checked on 2 November 2026.

Link to question 19

20.

### Does my business qualify for the instant asset write-off this financial year?

Yes, if your aggregated turnover is under $10 million and you use the simplified depreciation rules. You can deduct the full cost of each eligible asset costing less than $20,000 that is first used or installed ready for use in the year. The $20,000 limit applied in 2025-26 and is permanent from 1 July 2026. Test eligibility against the rules enacted for the asset’s relevant year and circumstances.

- Record aggregated turnover, asset cost, acquisition and first use dates, and business use share.
- Check the current ATO small business depreciation rules, including exclusions and any applicable election.

The ordinary depreciation worksheet does not determine instant asset write-off eligibility.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Instant asset write-off · $20,000 instant asset write-off, new legislation · Experimental tax worksheets and supported years

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

21.

### Do I need an ABN for freelance or contracting work?

You’re entitled to an ABN if you’re carrying on or starting an enterprise in Australia. You’re not entitled to one for work you do as an employee, even if you or your employer calls it contracting. ABN entitlement depends on carrying on or starting an enterprise. An invoice or a client’s request alone does not establish it.

- Record the work arrangement, independence, activity and evidence that the enterprise has started.
- Read the ABR entitlement guidance before applying.

An ABN does not decide whether a worker is an employee for tax, super or workplace law.

ABR ABN application and entitlement · ABN entitlement, ABR

Link to question 21

22.

### How do I apply for an ABN, and what information do I need?

Apply online through the ABR. Details such as your TFN help the ABR identify you and process the application faster; if it needs to check details, it aims to review the application within 20 business days. Apply through the official ABR route after checking entitlement.

- Gather the entity structure, business activity, start date and contact information required by the ABR.
- Enter identity information directly into the official application and save its confirmation.

This site neither applies for an ABN nor handles identity documents.

ABR ABN application and entitlement

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 22

23.

### Is my activity a hobby or a business for tax purposes?

Generally, a business involves continuous and repeated activities done to make a profit. The ATO asks whether you intend to and have a prospect of making a profit, whether the scale is enough to make one, and whether the activities are repeated and continuous; a hobby you don’t seek to profit from is not a business. Assess the pattern of activity, commercial purpose and how the activity is organised.

- Document your intention, pricing, repetition, scale, records and plan to make a profit.
- Keep the conclusion and supporting facts, and reassess when the activity changes.

There is no single revenue figure in this guide that classifies every activity.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Are you in business?

The bold answer was checked on 29 October 2026.

Link to question 23

24.

### Should I operate as a sole trader or a company?

A sole trader reports business income as their own and is personally liable for the business’s debts. A company is a separate legal entity with higher set-up and running costs and an annual ASIC review; it pays tax at 25% or 30%, and it pays directors wages or fees rather than drawings. Compare liability, ownership, administration, tax and how profits will reach the owners.

- Prepare the same forecast under each structure, including compliance costs and money taken out.
- Discuss asset protection, existing contracts and restructuring costs with the relevant advisers before choosing.

A lower company tax rate alone does not establish a lower total cost or a suitable structure.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Difference between a sole trader and a company, business.gov.au · Changes to company tax rates · 13-week cash forecast

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 24

25.

### How much should I set aside for income tax as a sole trader?

The ATO automatically enters an individual, including a sole trader, into PAYG instalments when their latest return shows instalment income of $4,000 or more, tax payable of $1,000 or more and estimated tax of $500 or more. You can also enter voluntarily. Reserve cash against an estimate of your annual personal tax position and instalments already paid.

- Forecast business profit alongside salary and other personal income, deductions and credits.
- Place expected instalments and the remaining tax payment into the cash forecast on their due dates.

A fixed percentage of sales can miss deductions, other income and tax already paid.

Your tax return · Starting PAYG instalments · 13-week cash forecast

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 25

26.

### Do I need a separate business bank account?

A sole trader doesn’t have to have a business bank account, although it’s a good idea. A partnership, company or trust must have a separate bank account for tax purposes. A separate account makes business transactions easier to trace. The requirements also depend on the entity.

- Record which accounts hold business money and reconcile each to its statement.
- For a company or trust, keep entity funds and private funds clearly identified and correctly recorded.

Check the account requirements for your structure before opening or changing banking arrangements.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Set up your business bank account, business.gov.au

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 26

27.

### How do I pay myself and record drawings as a sole trader?

What you draw doesn’t change what a sole trader reports: all your business income goes in your individual tax return, whatever amounts you transfer to your personal account. Sole-trader drawings transfer the owner’s money out of the business; they are recorded separately from operating expenses.

- Record the transfer against drawings or the owner’s equity account in your agreed chart.
- Keep drawings visible in the cash forecast so the business can meet upcoming obligations.

A sole trader’s drawings do not set the amount of taxable business profit.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Using business money and assets · 13-week cash forecast

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 27

28.

### Do the personal services income rules apply to my contracting income?

For income that is mainly a reward for your personal effort or skill, the PSI rules apply when 80% or more of it comes from one client and its associates, unless you pass the results test or hold a personal services business determination. Review whether the income is mainly a reward for personal effort or skill, then work through the applicable PSI tests.

- Keep contracts, invoices, working arrangements and evidence for any test relied on.
- Record the income streams separately and review personal-services-business conditions with your adviser.

An ABN or company structure does not by itself switch off the PSI rules.

Starting, registering or closing a business · The PSI 80% rule

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 28

29.

### How do I report income from a side hustle, delivery work or online sales?

Income from providing services or assets for a fee through a sharing economy platform, such as ride-sourcing, renting out a room or sharing assets, is taxable, and GST can apply. Platform operators report these transactions to the ATO. Reconcile gross platform activity to payouts before deciding how to report it.

- Export sales, fees, refunds and activity records for the income year.
- Document whether the activity is business, employment or another income category and check GST separately.

Net bank deposits can omit fees and gross receipts that need separate reporting.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Types of activities in the sharing economy

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 29

30.

### Can I offset a business loss against my salary or other income?

Only if you meet the non-commercial loss rules: your income for the income requirement must be under $250,000 and you must pass one of 4 tests, such as earning at least $20,000 of assessable income from the business. Otherwise the loss is deferred. A business loss needs a separate review before it can reduce other income.

- Keep the loss calculation, activity history and records relevant to the non-commercial loss tests.
- Record whether an exception, test or discretion applies, or whether the loss must be deferred.

A loss in the accounts does not automatically offset salary in the tax return.

Starting, registering or closing a business · Non-commercial losses

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

31.

### How do I add GST to a price or extract GST from an inclusive amount?

GST is 10% of the GST-exclusive price. To find the GST included in a GST-inclusive price, divide it by 11: $110 includes $10 of GST. The calculation applies to a wholly taxable sale; classify GST-free, input-taxed and mixed sales first.

- Choose whether your amount already includes GST, then calculate the components.
- Keep the source invoice and confirm that the whole amount is subject to GST.

The calculator does not classify GST-free, input-taxed or mixed supplies.

ATO GST guidance · How GST works · Calculating sales using the calculation worksheet · GST calculator

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 31

32.

### When must my business register for GST?

Register within 21 days once your GST turnover reaches $75,000 ($150,000 for a non-profit). Taxi and ride-sourcing drivers must register whatever their turnover. Check current and projected GST turnover and any compulsory-registration rule for your activity.

- Build a monthly turnover schedule and review what counts towards GST turnover.
- Use the ATO registration guidance to determine the trigger and registration date.

Taxi and ride-sourcing rules and other exceptions mean a general turnover threshold is not enough.

ATO GST guidance · Registering for GST

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 32

33.

### What is the difference between GST-free and input-taxed sales?

Neither includes GST in the price. You can claim GST credits for purchases you use to make GST-free sales, but not for purchases that relate to input-taxed sales, such as financial supplies and selling or renting out residential premises. Classify each sale before coding it, because the category decides whether GST credits on related purchases can be claimed.

- Classify each income stream using the ATO guidance and retain the basis for the classification.
- Review purchase credits and any apportionment separately for input-taxed activities.

Do not give both categories the same purchase-credit treatment just because no GST appears on the sale.

ATO GST guidance · GST-free sales · Input-taxed sales

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 33

34.

### Do I charge GST when selling to overseas customers?

Exported goods are GST-free if they are exported within 60 days of the earlier of receiving any payment or issuing an invoice for them. Some other supplies for consumption outside Australia, such as certain services, can also be GST-free. An overseas customer does not automatically make a sale GST-free.

- Record what you sold, where it is supplied or used, customer circumstances and any export evidence.
- Check the relevant goods or services rule before choosing the GST code.

Export conditions and evidence requirements differ between goods and services.

ATO GST guidance · GST-free sales

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 34

35.

### What information must appear on a valid tax invoice?

If a customer asks, you must issue a tax invoice within 28 days for any sale over $82.50 including GST. It must show that it is a tax invoice, your identity and ABN, the date, what was sold with quantity and price, the GST amount and how much of each sale is taxable. Sales of $1,000 or more must also show the buyer’s identity or ABN. Use an invoice checklist matched to the sale and the ATO’s tax invoice requirements.

- Check supplier identity and ABN, date, description, price and how the GST amount is shown.
- Check any buyer-identification requirement and clearly separate taxable and non-taxable items.

Requirements depend on the amount and nature of the sale; a heading alone does not make an invoice valid.

ATO GST guidance · Tax invoices

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 35

36.

### How do I prepare a BAS from my accounting records?

If your GST turnover is under $10 million, you generally report GST using Simpler BAS: total sales at G1, GST on sales at 1A and GST on purchases at 1B. Reconcile source records to each BAS label before approval.

- Check reporting period and GST basis, reconcile tax-coded transactions and investigate exceptions.
- Reconcile PAYG and other labels, retain the workpaper and obtain approval before lodgement.

Fictional worked example

For a fictional quarter, reconciled GST on sales at label 1A is $3,000 and eligible GST credits at label 1B are $1,800. The GST component payable is $1,200. Keep the sales and purchase reconciliations with the BAS workpaper, then reconcile other applicable BAS obligations separately. This example assumes the supplied GST amounts are already classified correctly.

The linked readiness gate checks a prepared pack. It does not prepare the BAS, decide tax treatment or authorise lodgement.

ATO business activity statements · GST reporting methods · Simpler BAS GST bookkeeping guide · BAS pack readiness checks

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 36

37.

### When is my BAS due, and when must I pay it?

Quarterly BAS is due on 28 October, 28 February, 28 April and 28 July. Monthly BAS is due on the 21st day of the following month. Payment is due by the same date. Use the period and due date shown for your BAS account.

- Record both lodgement and payment deadlines and any approved concession.
- Put the cash payment in the forecast and assign someone to retain the receipt.

General quarterly dates can differ from the dates that apply to your account.

ATO GST guidance · Due dates for lodging and paying your BAS · 13-week cash forecast

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 37

38.

### Should I account for GST on a cash or accrual basis?

A business with aggregated turnover under $10 million can choose either the cash or the accrual basis for GST. Compare the timing of receipts and payments under the methods your business is allowed to use.

- Check eligibility and the method currently recorded with the ATO.
- Model the effect on unpaid invoices and bills before changing method, and document transition adjustments.

Changing a report setting in Xero does not by itself change the ATO accounting method.

ATO GST guidance · Choosing an accounting method for GST

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 38

39.

### Why does my BAS GST figure differ from the GST balance in Xero?

On the cash basis, you account for GST on the BAS covering the period in which you receive or make payment for your sales and purchases. Bridge the BAS calculation to the GST control account at the same date and on the same basis.

- Separate opening balances, payments to the ATO, cash-basis timing and journals.
- List each reconciling item and clear unexplained differences before signing off.

A control account balance is not automatically the GST payable for one BAS period. The linked gate tests supplied tie-outs; it does not investigate reconciling items.

ATO GST guidance · Choosing an accounting method for GST · BAS pack readiness checks

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 39

40.

### How do I correct a mistake in a BAS I have already lodged?

You can generally correct a GST error on a later BAS lodged within the period of review for the period of the error, but not to claim GST credits after the 4-year time limit, and not more than once. Revising the earlier BAS instead can attract penalties or general interest charge. Work out whether the error can be corrected on a later BAS or requires a revision.

- Record the original period, error type, amount, discovery date and supporting transactions.
- Apply the ATO’s correction conditions and retain the approved amendment or later-period adjustment.

Do not choose a later-period correction without checking the period of review and the 4-year credit time limit.

ATO GST guidance · How to correct GST errors · GST errors that can’t be corrected on a later BAS

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

41.

### How much super must I pay, and which earnings count towards it?

The super guarantee rate is 12%, as it has been since 1 July 2025. From 1 July 2026 it is worked out on qualifying earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026-27. Identify the applicable super regime and eligible earnings for the pay date before calculating a contribution.

- From July 2026, use the ATO Payday Super guidance and map each pay component to the relevant earnings definition.
- Check worker eligibility, limits and payroll settings; retain the calculation and contribution evidence.

The old quarterly SG worksheet does not establish current Payday Super entitlement.

Payday Super for employers · Super guarantee rate history on this site · ATO maximum contribution base · Maximum super contribution base by year

Link to question 41

42.

### By what date must a super contribution reach the employee’s fund?

Since 1 July 2026, the fund must receive the contribution within 7 business days after payday, or within 20 business days for the first contribution for a new employee or to a new fund. Test receipt at the employee’s fund against the applicable deadline.

- Record payday, pathway, amount, remittance date and confirmed fund receipt date.
- Use the existing timing example to distinguish timely remittance from evidence of timely receipt.

The timing tool needs the contribution amount supplied and the correct pathway selected.

Payday Super for employers · Payment deadlines for Payday Super · Payday Super receipt evidence example

Link to question 42

43.

### What should I do if a super payment is late, rejected or missing?

Since 1 July 2026, super that is unpaid, late, short or paid to the wrong fund makes you liable to the super guarantee charge, which the ATO assesses. The charge includes notional earnings and may include an administrative uplift of up to 60%; paying the fund what you owe as soon as possible, even in part, reduces it. Investigate the payment trail and apply the current late-payment process.

- Reconcile payroll, clearing house status, rejections and fund receipt for each affected employee.
- Resolve the cause, record any replacement payment and review the ATO’s reporting and charge requirements.

Sending a replacement does not automatically remove a late-payment consequence.

Payday Super for employers · What to do if you miss a Payday Super contribution · Payment deadlines for Payday Super · Payday Super receipt evidence example

44.

### Do I have to pay super for a contractor who invoices through an ABN?

If you pay a contractor under a contract that is mainly for their labour, meaning more than half its dollar value, they are an employee for super guarantee purposes and you may need to pay super for them. An ABN makes no difference. Review the actual contract and working arrangement against the ATO’s super eligibility guidance.

- Record who performs the work, how they are paid and whether the contract is for their labour.
- Retain the eligibility conclusion separately from the supplier’s ABN and invoice.

An ABN is not proof that super is unnecessary.

Payday Super for employers · Super for independent contractors

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 44

45.

### How much PAYG tax should I withhold from an employee’s pay?

Use the ATO tax withheld calculator or tax tables for the pay period, whether weekly, fortnightly or monthly. The employee’s TFN declaration or withholding declaration tells you whether to withhold extra for a study or training support loan. Use the ATO withholding calculation for the payment type and pay period.

- Check the declaration, residency, tax-free threshold choice, study loan information and any variation.
- Apply the current schedule or calculator and reconcile payroll totals to the withholding liability.

A resident annual income tax worksheet is not a payroll withholding calculator.

PAYG withholding · Tax withheld calculator

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 45

46.

### How do I finalise Single Touch Payroll at year-end?

Make the STP finalisation declaration by 14 July each year. Reconcile payroll to the ledger and ATO reporting before making the STP finalisation declaration.

- Check year-to-date wages, withholding, super and adjustments by employee.
- Resolve discrepancies, confirm the applicable deadline and retain the finalisation evidence.

An ordinary payroll submission and a finalisation declaration are different steps.

Single Touch Payroll · Finalising your STP data · Finalise your STP data by 14 July · Monthly close review pack

The bold answer was checked on 29 October 2026.

Link to question 46

47.

### How do I calculate an employee’s final pay, including unused leave?

Final pay is the wages owing, including penalty rates and allowances, plus any unused annual leave with loading if it would have been paid during employment; it can also include accrued or pro rata long service leave. Sick and carer’s leave isn’t paid out, and most awards require final pay within 7 days after the last day of employment. Build final pay from the employee’s entitlements and the circumstances of departure.

- Gather the award or agreement, termination date, unpaid hours, leave balances and notice details.
- Check leave loading, redundancy and long service leave where applicable, then apply the relevant tax treatment.

The generic staff cost calculator cannot determine final pay entitlements.

Final pay - Fair Work Ombudsman

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 47

48.

### When does my business become liable for payroll tax in NSW?

For 2026-27, NSW payroll tax applies to taxable wages above $1,200,000 a year, at a rate of 5.45%. Review Australian taxable wages, NSW connection, grouping and the applicable threshold.

- Prepare a wages reconciliation that includes the categories Revenue NSW requires.
- Check the monthly registration trigger and annual reconciliation requirements for the relevant year.

Book payroll expense alone can omit taxable benefits, super or grouped wages.

Revenue NSW payroll tax · Payroll tax thresholds and rates, Revenue NSW

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 48

49.

### Do contractor payments count towards NSW payroll tax?

Payments to a contractor who provides the services of a worker under a relevant contract are liable for NSW payroll tax unless an exemption applies. Exemptions include some services provided for 90 days or less in a financial year and services the contractor provides to the public. Contractor payments need a separate payroll tax review under the NSW relevant-contract rules.

- Keep the contract, services, days worked and evidence for any exclusion claimed.
- Reconcile reviewed contractor amounts to the payroll tax workpaper.

An invoice, ABN or GST registration alone does not establish an exclusion.

Revenue NSW payroll tax · Contractors, Revenue NSW

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 49

50.

### What does an employee cost after super, leave, insurance and other on-costs?

Start with wages plus the 12% super guarantee, then add leave, workers compensation, any payroll tax and other on-costs. Add annual wages, super and the other costs you expect to pay, then consider productive capacity separately.

- Enter the annual super amount and other costs such as insurance, payroll tax, recruitment and equipment.
- Allow for paid leave when estimating productive hours, and add relief staff costs only where expected.

Do not add ordinary paid leave again if it is already included in the annual salary.

Final pay - Fair Work Ombudsman · Super guarantee rate history on this site · Staff cost calculator

51.

### Why does my Xero bank balance differ from my bank statement?

Reconcile the bank statement and Xero at the same date before posting a correction.

- Compare statement lines with ledger transactions, outstanding payments and deposits.
- Investigate missing feeds, duplicates, opening balances and items dated outside the period.

Do not post a balancing journal while the cause remains unknown.

Record keeping for business · Monthly close review pack

Link to question 51

52.

### How do I identify and fix duplicate bank transactions in Xero?

Identify whether the duplicate is a statement line, an accounting transaction or both.

- Match date, amount, bank reference and source document; distinguish repeated genuine payments.
- Use the appropriate Xero correction after review, then rerun the bank reconciliation.

Removing the wrong item can remove a real transaction; retain the correction trail.

Record keeping for business

Link to question 52

53.

### How do I correct a customer payment matched to the wrong invoice?

Trace the payment and both customer invoices before changing the match.

- Save the original allocation details and check whether the invoice or period is locked.
- Correct the allocation through Xero’s supported workflow and recheck both customer balances and the bank reconciliation.

A different bank receipt should not be created merely to fix an allocation.

Record keeping for business

Link to question 53

54.

### How do I record a personal purchase paid from the business account?

Code the private payment according to the entity and the person’s relationship to it.

- Keep the receipt, purpose and repayment evidence, and separate any business portion.
- For a sole trader, review drawings; for a company, review the director or shareholder account and tax consequences.

A company payment cannot automatically be treated as sole-trader drawings.

Record keeping for business · Division 7A review case and limitations

Link to question 54

55.

### Which business records should I keep, and for how long?

Keep most business records for 5 years. Keep records for depreciating assets and CGT assets until 5 years after you dispose of the asset. Keep records that let someone trace transactions, calculations and decisions for the required retention period.

- Create a register covering tax, payroll, assets, loans, contracts and entity records.
- Assign retention dates using the relevant ATO and other legal requirements, including longer periods for continuing assets or disputes.

Do not apply one blanket retention date to every document.

Record keeping for business · Overview of record-keeping rules for business · Records you need to keep for longer than five years

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.

Link to question 55

56.

### How should I organise my chart of accounts?

Use a chart of accounts that supports reporting and reconciliations at a manageable level of detail.

- Separate assets, liabilities, equity, revenue and expenses; keep control accounts identifiable.
- Use consistent account mappings and tracking categories for the dimensions you need to report.

Do not create a new account for every customer or supplier when the subledger already tracks them.

Record keeping for business · Monthly close review pack

Link to question 56

57.

### How do I split a loan repayment between principal and interest?

Split each repayment using the loan statement and the agreement. Interest is a finance cost; principal reduces the loan balance.

- Reconcile opening principal, advances, principal repayments and closing principal.
- Use the loan calculator to sense-check a fixed-rate monthly schedule, then compare with the lender’s statement.

Fees, daily interest, variable rates and balloons need the actual lender schedule.

Set up a cash flow statement · Monthly loan payment calculator

Link to question 57

58.

### Should a purchase be recorded as an asset or an expense?

Apply your accounting policy to the nature, use and expected benefit of the purchase, then assess tax separately.

- Record what was acquired, cost, useful life and when it became available for use.
- If capitalised, update the asset register and depreciation; document any tax difference.

An accounting asset policy and an immediate tax deduction rule can give different treatments.

Record keeping for business · Experimental tax worksheets and supported years

Link to question 58

59.

### Why do my aged receivables or payables differ from the general ledger?

Compare the aged report and ledger on the same date with the same filters.

- Trace journals to control accounts, prepayments, credits, foreign-currency adjustments and excluded contacts.
- Prepare a bridge to the ledger and resolve unexplained items before closing.

A matching total alone does not establish that individual balances are collectible or payable.

Record keeping for business · Monthly close review pack

Link to question 59

60.

### What should I reconcile and check before closing the month or financial year?

Close from reconciled balances and documented review decisions.

- Reconcile bank, receivables, payables, GST, payroll, super, loans, fixed assets and key accruals.
- Review cut-off, unusual journals and variances, then retain the pack and approval before locking the period.

Fictional worked example

At 30 September 2026, a fictional bank statement shows $12,000 and the ledger bank account shows $11,700. A $300 customer receipt is on the statement but missing from the ledger. After confirming the invoice and posting the missing receipt, both bank balances are $12,000. The aged receivables report still shows $9,500 against a $10,000 control account. Record that separate $500 exception, its owner and the evidence needed to resolve it before completing the close.

The existing close pack supports review; it does not automatically approve journals or finalise accounts.

Record keeping for business · Monthly close review pack

61.

### How do I build a 13-week cash flow forecast?

Forecast cash by the week it is expected to move through the bank.

- Start with the reconciled bank balance and schedule receipts, suppliers, wages, tax, debt and drawings across 13 weeks.
- Use the browser forecast for a short scenario, or the existing workbook for a detailed worked example.

Fictional worked example

Start a fictional forecast on 28 September 2026 with $200 opening cash and a $100 buffer. Enter $1,000 receipts and $300 payments in week 1, and zero in every later week. Closing cash is $900. Delay the full $1,000 receipt by two weeks: cash closes at minus $100 in weeks 1 and 2, then returns to $900 in week 3. The lowest balance is minus $100, so the funding gap to the buffer is $200. The eventual closing balance is unchanged.

Weekly closing balances can hide a shortage within the week; review daily timing where cash is tight.

Set up a cash flow statement · 13-week cash forecast

Link to question 61

62.

### Why is my business profitable but short of cash?

Profit and cash diverge because income and expenses can be recognised at different times from receipts and payments.

- Bridge profit to cash using receivables, payables, inventory, tax, capital spending, debt and drawings.
- Use the fictional Newcastle example to inspect a profitable business with a temporary cash shortage.

Loan proceeds and principal repayments affect cash without being ordinary trading revenue and expense.

Set up a cash flow statement · Fictional Newcastle cash flow workbook

Link to question 62

63.

### How much cash should I reserve for BAS, payroll and super payments?

Schedule the actual expected liabilities and payment dates, then choose a buffer.

- Reconcile GST, withholding and super liabilities to their supporting workpapers.
- Enter their payment weeks in the cash forecast, including other committed cash costs.

The forecast reserves supplied amounts; it does not calculate statutory liabilities from sales.

Set up a cash flow statement · 13-week cash forecast

Link to question 63

64.

### What happens to my cash balance if a major customer pays 30 or 60 days late?

Move the expected receipt to its revised date and compare the lowest cash balance.

- Use the weekly forecast’s delayed-receipt controls and retain both scenarios.
- For an exact 30- or 60-day delay, use the existing dated workbook and record any receipt outside its horizon.

The browser scenario accepts whole weeks, so it is not an exact day-based simulation.

Set up a cash flow statement · 13-week cash forecast

Link to question 64

65.

### Can my business afford another employee?

Compare the extra cash costs of hiring with conservative additional receipts and available cash.

- Calculate annual staff cost, then phase wages, super, setup costs and training into the forecast.
- Test slower sales, a delayed start and a minimum cash buffer before committing.

Annual profitability does not establish that each payroll payment will be affordable.

Set up a cash flow statement · Staff cost calculator

Link to question 65

66.

### What would buying equipment outright versus financing it do to my cash flow?

Compare the timing and total payments of outright purchase and finance.

- Put the purchase price into the relevant cash week for the outright option.
- For finance, schedule deposit, fees, repayments and any balloon; compare the cash minimum and total cost.

The loan calculator assumes fixed monthly payments with no fees or balloon. Tax and ownership effects require separate review.

Set up a cash flow statement · Monthly loan payment calculator

Link to question 66

67.

### How much working capital or overdraft capacity will I need next quarter?

Find the lowest forecast balance and compare it with the cash buffer you need.

- Include current bank cash, committed payments, realistic receipts and stressed collection dates.
- Use the forecast funding gap result as an initial amount to investigate, then review timing and facility terms.

A calculated gap is not a credit approval or proof that borrowing is suitable.

Set up a cash flow statement · 13-week cash forecast

Link to question 67

68.

### How can I reduce overdue customer balances and get paid sooner?

Prioritise overdue balances by amount, age, dispute and likelihood of collection.

- Reconcile the aged ledger, assign an owner and record the next action for each overdue account.
- Review invoice accuracy, payment terms and billing timing; update receipt dates using what customers confirm.

Changing a forecast date does not improve collection evidence.

Set up a cash flow statement

Link to question 68

69.

### How do I plan for seasonal cash shortages?

Plan from the seasonal payment and receipt pattern, including the costs incurred before sales arrive.

- Compare prior periods with current orders, staffing and supplier commitments.
- Stress-test the low season and put any agreed funding or cost changes into the forecast.

A straight average month can conceal the quarter’s lowest cash balance.

Set up a cash flow statement · 13-week cash forecast

Link to question 69

70.

### How do I update my forecast each month using actual results?

Replace completed periods with reconciled actuals and explain the difference before rolling the forecast forward.

- Save the previous forecast, match actual receipts and payments, and classify timing versus permanent changes.
- Refresh remaining assumptions and extend the horizon with a dated version and owner.

Do not overwrite the old forecast if you still need it to explain accuracy and decisions.

Set up a cash flow statement · Budget variance calculator

71.

### How much must I sell each month to break even?

Break-even sales cover fixed costs after variable costs. For one product, divide fixed costs by contribution per unit.

- Use the same period for fixed costs and the expected selling price and variable cost per unit.
- Round required units up and compare them with practical sales capacity.

The calculator assumes one product or a stable representative mix; it excludes tax and financing cash timing.

Choose a pricing strategy · Break-even calculator

Link to question 71

72.

### What is the difference between gross margin and markup?

Gross margin divides gross profit by revenue. Markup divides gross profit by cost.

- Use sales and the directly related cost for the same goods or period.
- Compare both percentages with the calculator and keep GST treatment consistent.

A zero denominator has no meaningful percentage; the calculator leaves that percentage undefined.

Choose a pricing strategy · Margin and markup calculator

Link to question 72

73.

### What hourly rate should I charge to cover costs and earn a target profit?

Divide annual costs plus target profit by realistic billable hours.

- Include the owner’s pay target in costs if it must be covered before the stated profit.
- Allow for leave, administration, marketing and unpaid time when estimating billable hours.

The calculated rate is a cost recovery target before GST; customers’ willingness to pay needs separate evidence.

Choose a pricing strategy · Hourly pricing calculator

Link to question 73

74.

### Which customers, jobs or service lines are making money?

Build contribution by customer, job or service line from consistent revenue and direct cost assignments.

- Allocate labour using recorded hours and identify material costs, discounts, rework and write-offs.
- Keep shared overhead allocation visible and compare results before and after that allocation.

An allocation method can change apparent profitability without changing total business profit.

Choose a pricing strategy · Margin and markup calculator

Link to question 74

75.

### Why are my actual results different from my budget?

Compare actual and budget figures for the same period and accounting basis, then explain the drivers.

- Calculate the amount and percentage difference for income or costs.
- Split the difference into price, volume, mix, timing, coding and one-off items, then quantify each supported explanation.

The variance calculator measures the difference; it cannot infer its cause from two numbers.

Set up a cash flow statement · Budget variance calculator

Link to question 75

76.

### Which financial reports should a small business owner review each month?

Review profit, financial position and cash together, with the balances that explain them.

- Prepare the P&L against budget, balance sheet, cash forecast, aged debtors and creditors, and key obligation reconciliations.
- Record exceptions, decisions, owners and dates for the next review.

Choose detail that changes a decision; a larger dashboard does not necessarily improve the review.

Set up a cash flow statement · Monthly close review pack

77.

### How do my business expenses compare with ATO small business benchmarks?

Choose the ATO industry and turnover range that match your business and reporting period.

- Map ledger accounts to the benchmark definitions and retain the mapping.
- Compare ratios with the relevant dataset and investigate differences in business model, year or coding.

The linked benchmark tool uses specified historical datasets; a difference is not proof of an error or non-compliance.

ATO benchmark comparison method

78.

### How do I value and report work in progress and unbilled work?

Separate the accounting basis for recognising revenue from the amount billed.

- Reconcile contract value, costs incurred, estimates to complete, billings and unbilled amounts.
- For a suitable construction contract, use the WIP schedule and review estimate changes and profit fade.

The existing tool covers construction cost-to-cost schedules; it does not classify every service contract.

Record keeping for business · Construction WIP schedule

79.

### Why has my gross margin fallen even though sales have increased?

Higher sales can coincide with a lower margin when prices, product mix or costs change.

- Compare revenue and direct costs by job or product; check discounts, labour efficiency, rework and cut-off.
- Use the margin and variance calculators, and review cost-to-complete estimates for construction work.

A total sales comparison alone cannot identify which driver reduced margin.

Choose a pricing strategy · Margin and markup calculator

### How do I turn Xero data into a useful Excel or Power BI management dashboard?

Start with reconciled exports and a small set of decisions the report needs to support.

- Define account mappings, periods and measures, then tie totals to Xero before adding charts.
- Use the existing trial balance export and close pack, and document refresh and review steps.

The export tool supplies data; this guide does not install a Power BI connector or grant Xero access.

81.

### Does my company qualify for the lower company tax rate?

The 25% rate applies to a base rate entity: a company with aggregated turnover under $50 million and no more than 80% of its assessable income from base rate entity passive income. Other companies pay 30%. Test the company’s income and aggregated turnover conditions for the relevant year.

- Reconcile taxable income, passive income categories and connected entity information.
- Use the existing company tax example only after the inputs and applicable conditions have been established.

The example does not determine eligibility merely from accounting profit.

Corporate tax measures and assurance · Changes to company tax rates · Company tax and franking example

82.

### How should I record money paid to a director as wages, dividends or a loan?

Wages and director’s fees are assessable income to you, and the company must withhold PAYG from them. A loan to a shareholder or their associate can be treated as a dividend under Division 7A unless it is repaid, or put under a complying written agreement, before the company’s lodgment day. Record a director payment according to its legal basis and supporting documents.

- Gather payroll records, dividend documents or loan terms and trace each payment.
- Review withholding, super, franking and Division 7A consequences before posting or reclassifying it.

Changing the ledger label does not change the underlying transaction.

Corporate tax measures and assurance · Using business money and assets · Types of payments to employees · Loans by private companies · Company tax and franking example

Link to question 82

83.

### Does taking money out of my company create a Division 7A problem?

A payment, loan or forgiven debt from a private company to a shareholder or their associate can be treated as a dividend under Division 7A, generally unfranked. A loan avoids this if it is fully repaid, or put under a complying written agreement, before the company’s lodgment day. Review company payments, loans and debt forgiveness involving shareholders or associates under Division 7A.

- Reconcile the person’s account and gather agreements, dates and repayment evidence.
- Use the existing review case to organise the evidence and identify unresolved legal questions.

The repayment worksheet does not decide whether a loan is complying or whether a deemed dividend arises.

Private company benefits - Division 7A dividends · Loans by private companies · Division 7A review case and limitations

Link to question 83

84.

### How do I calculate the minimum yearly repayment on a complying Division 7A loan?

The minimum yearly repayment uses the benchmark interest rate (8.77% for 2026-27 and 8.37% for 2025-26 for a 30 June year end), the unpaid balance and the remaining term. The maximum term is 7 years, or 25 years for a loan fully secured by a registered mortgage over real property. Use the minimum yearly repayment calculation for an established complying loan and the correct year.

- Gather the relevant opening balance, benchmark rate, remaining term and qualifying repayments.
- Reproduce the existing Division 7A case, then retain the inputs and compare required with actual qualifying repayments.

Eligibility, amalgamation and repayment classification must already have been reviewed.

Private company benefits - Division 7A dividends · Division 7A benchmark interest rate on this site · Division 7A review case and limitations

Link to question 84

85.

### Which payments count as repayments of a Division 7A loan?

A repayment may not count if you reborrow a similar or larger amount from the company afterwards, or use money borrowed from the company to make it. A dividend can be set off against a minimum yearly repayment only if both exist and the offset is agreed by the end of the income year, usually 30 June. Review the source, timing and surrounding arrangements for each proposed repayment.

- Trace the payment through bank and loan records and identify any reborrowing or circular movement.
- Document the section 109R review and qualifying amount before using the minimum repayment worksheet.

A credit to a director loan account is not automatically a qualifying Division 7A repayment.

Private company benefits - Division 7A dividends · Division 7A myths debunked · Division 7A review case and limitations

The bold answer was checked on 27 September 2026.
