### oz.CountDOWλ

oz.CountDOWλ(Starts, Ends, DayOfWeek)

Count instances of a specific day of the week between two dates.

Parameters:

Starts (required)

One of more start dates (text or numeric) in a row or column

Ends (required)

End dates (text or numeric) for each start date

DayOfWeek (required)

1=Sunday, 7=Saturday.

```
=oz.CountDOWλ("23/7/2026", "11/8/2026",  1)
```

The workbook help shows 3.

Previous name: nabla.d.CountDOWλ.

### oz.IsBetweenλ

oz.IsBetweenλ(Values, Low, High, [Inclusive])

Determine if a value is between a lower and upper limit

Determine if a value is between a lower and upper limit.

Parameters:

Values (required)

one or more values to compare.

Low (required)

The lower limit that the value(s) must be greater than

High (required)

The higher limit that the value(s) must be less than

Inclusive (optional)

TRUE: Value(s) can be equal to Low and/or High (default)

```
=oz.IsBetweenλ(1, 2, 4)
```

The workbook help shows FALSE.

```
=oz.IsBetweenλ(Today(), Today(), Today()+1)
```

The workbook help shows TRUE.

```
=oz.IsBetweenλ("B", "B", "D", FALSE)
```

The workbook help shows FALSE.

Previous name: nabla.d.IsBetweenλ.

### oz.IsOccurrenceDateλ

oz.IsOccurrenceDateλ(Dates, FirstOccurrence, [LastOccurrence], [Repeats])

Returns TRUE if Date passed is when something happens. This was developed for budgeting where we have expenses that start, and sometimes repeat at regular intervals.

Returns TRUE if a Date is when something happens. Developed for budgeting, where expenses start and sometimes repeat at regular intervals.

Note: A monthly, quarterly, semi-annual or annual item that starts on the 29th, 30th or 31st falls on the last day of any shorter month.

Parameters:

Dates (required)

Date to test. Normally this is horizontal timeline by day

FirstOccurrence (required)

When something that may repeat, happens for the first time.

LastOccurrence (optional)

When something that may repeat, happens for the last time. If omitted, it is assumed repeating items repeat forever.

Repeats (optional)

A code that conveys how often this thing repeats. Repeat codes are O=One time/never repeats (default) A=Annually S=Semi-Annually Q=Quarterly M=Monthly B=BiWeekly W=Weekly X=Every Workday (Monday to Friday) D=Daily

```
=SUM(N(oz.IsOccurrenceDateλ(SEQUENCE(,90,"1/7/2026"), "1/7/2026", "10/9/2026", "D")))
```

The workbook help shows 72.

```
=SUM(N(oz.IsOccurrenceDateλ(SEQUENCE(,90,"1/7/2026"), "1/7/2026", "10/9/2026", "O")))
```

The workbook help shows 01.

```
=SUM(N(oz.IsOccurrenceDateλ(SEQUENCE(,90,"1/7/2026"), "1/7/2026", "10/9/2026", "W")))
```

The workbook help shows 11.

Previous name: nabla.d.IsOccurrenceDateλ.

Return how many days overlap two period ranges.

Count days shared between two sets of periods.

Parameters:

Period1End (required)

First period's end date.

Period2Start (required)

Second period's start date.

Period2End (required)

Second period's end date.

The workbook help shows 5.

```

The workbook help shows 8.

```

The workbook help shows 2.

Previous name: nabla.d.OverLapDaysλ.

### oz.PeriodLabelλ

oz.PeriodLabelλ(Date, [Interval])

Creates a label for a date based on period interval

Parameters:

Date (required)

A single date or array of date(s) where the first date is the first date of a calendar year.

Interval (optional)

Must be one of:

- D=Daily
- W=Weekly
- I=Weekly (using ISO week number)
- M=Monthly
- Q=Quarterly
- S=Semi-Annually
- A or Y=Annually

```
=oz.PeriodLabelλ(DATEVALUE("26/8/2026"), "D")
```

The workbook help shows 2026-Aug-26.

```
=oz.PeriodLabelλ(DATEVALUE("26/8/2026"), "M")
```

The workbook help shows 2026-Aug.

```
=oz.PeriodLabelλ(DATEVALUE("26/8/2026"), "Q")
```

The workbook help shows 2026:Q3.

```
=oz.PeriodLabelλ(DATEVALUE("26/8/2026"), "Y")
```

The workbook help shows 2026.

Previous name: nabla.d.PeriodLabelλ.

### oz.Periodsλ

oz.Periodsλ(Starts, Ends, [Intervals])

Determine the number of periods from Starts to Date2 in Days, Weeks, Months, Quarters, or Years.

Determine the number of periods from Starts to Ends inclusive. Differences to Excel's DATEDIF are: * Interval includes Weeks & Quarters * Counts the period starts crossed, so a part period at the end counts * Returns negative values if Starts is after Ends

Parameters:

Starts (required)

First date (normally older). A single date or an array of dates.

Ends (required)

Second date (normally newer). A single date or an array the same shape as Starts. A single Starts or Ends is applied to every date in the other.

Intervals (optional)

Days, Weeks, Months (default), Quarters, or Years (D, W, M, Q, Y). One code, or an array of codes the same shape as the dates.

```
=oz.Periodsλ("31/7/2026", "15/9/2026")
```

The workbook help shows 2.

```
=oz.Periodsλ("15/9/2026", "31/7/2026")
```

The workbook help shows -2.

```
=oz.Periodsλ("15/7/2027", "16/7/2026")
```

The workbook help shows -12.

```
=oz.Periodsλ("15/7/2027", "16/7/2026", "W")
```

The workbook help shows -52.

Previous name: nabla.d.Periodsλ.

### oz.ScheduleRatesλ

oz.ScheduleRatesλ(PeriodEnds, RateStarts, Rates)

Schedule rates that persist until replaced in a timeline.

Schedules rates that persist until replaced in a timeline from a schedule in a table.

Note: If 2 rates are scheduled within the same period, only the last rate will be selected.

Parameters:

PeriodEnds (required)

A row of period end dates (timeline).

RateStarts (required)

A column or row of rate effective dates in any order.

Rates (required)

A column or row of rates associated with RateStarts.

```
=oz.ScheduleRatesλ(Timelineλ("1/7/2026",5,"W"),{46208; 46216; 46222}, {10; 20; 30})
```

The workbook help shows _,10,20,30,30.

Previous name: nabla.d.ScheduleRatesλ.

### oz.ScheduleRatesByItemsλ

oz.ScheduleRatesByItemsλ(PeriodEnds, ItemFilter, ItemList, EffectiveList, RateList)

Schedule rates that persist until replaced in a timeline for each item in a list.

Schedules each item's rates by period until another rate takes effect.

Note: If 2 rates are scheduled within the same period for the same item,. only the last rate will be selected.

Parameters:

PeriodEnds (required)

A row of period end dates (timeline).

ItemFilter (required)

A column of 1 or more items to filter a rate schedule by. A 'rate schedule' is a table/list where each row contains a unique item/effective date pair with a rate. An item with no rate in the schedule scores nought in every period.

ItemList (required)

Items in a rate schedule.

EffectiveList (required)

Effective dates in the rate schedule.

RateList (required)

Rates in a rate schedule for each item/effective date pair.

```
=oz.ScheduleRatesByItemsλ( oz.Timelineλ( "1/7/2026"), UNIQUE( tblRates[Unit]),
tblRates[Unit], tblRates[Effective], tblRates[Rent])
```

Previous name: nabla.d.ScheduleRatesByItemsλ.

### oz.ScheduleValuesλ

oz.ScheduleValuesλ(PeriodStarts, PeriodEnds, Values, EffectiveDates)

Schedules values in a timeline from a schedule in a table.

Place values from a table into a timeline's appropriate period.

Parameters:

PeriodStarts (required)

A row of period start dates (timeline).

PeriodEnds (required)

A row of period end dates (timeline).

Values (required)

A column or row of values to be scheduled.

EffectiveDates (required)

When each value is scheduled, in the same orientation as Values.

```
=oz.ScheduleValuesλ(Timelineλ("1/7/2026"), Timelineλ("1/7/2026",,,FALSE), {1;3}, {"1/7/2026"; "15/8/2026"})
```

Previous name: nabla.d.ScheduleValuesλ.

### oz.ScheduleValuesByItemsλ

oz.ScheduleValuesByItemsλ(PeriodStarts, PeriodEnds, ItemFilter, ItemList, EffectiveList, ValueList)

Schedule and sum values in a timeline for each item.

Parameters:

PeriodStarts (required)

A row of period start dates (timeline).

PeriodEnds (required)

A row of period end dates (timeline).

ItemFilter (required)

A column of 1 or more items to filter a value schedule by. A 'value schedule' is a table/list where each row contains a unique item/effective date pair with a value.

ItemList (required)

Items in a value schedule.

EffectiveList (required)

Effective dates in the value schedule.

ValueList (required)

Values in a value schedule for each item/effective date pair. An item with no rows in the schedule totals nought in every period.

```
=oz.ScheduleValuesByItemsλ( oz.Timelineλ( "1/7/2026"),  oz.Timelineλ( "1/7/2026",,,FALSE),
UNIQUE( tblExp[Items]), tblExp[Items], tblExp[Dates], tblExp[Amount])
```

Previous name: nabla.d.ScheduleValuesByItemsλ.

### oz.Timelineλ

oz.Timelineλ(StartDate, Periods, Interval, PeriodStarts?)

Create a horizontal list of period dates

Creates a horizontal list of period dates.

Parameters:

StartDate (required)

First period's start date. May be entered as text.

Periods (optional)

The number of period in the timeline. Defaults to 12.

Interval (optional)

Period interval: D, W, M, Q or Y (Day, Week, Month <default>, Quarter, or Year)

PeriodStarts? (optional)

TRUE=Display period start dates <default>. FALSE=Period end dates

```
=oz.Timelineλ(TODAY())
```

The workbook help shows 12 mo, starts.

```
=oz.Timelineλ(TODAY(), , "Q", FALSE)
```

The workbook help shows 12 qtr, ends.

Previous name: nabla.d.Timelineλ.

Labels dates with their Australian financial year, which starts on 1 July

Labels dates with their Australian financial year, which starts on 1 July.

Parameters:

One or more dates, numeric or text. A blank cell returns a blank.

StartMonth (optional, Default = 7)

Month the financial year starts. Blank cells and empty text use 7.

### oz.FinancialMonthλ

oz.FinancialMonthλ(Dates, [StartMonth])

Numbers each date's month within its financial year, so July is month 1 when the year starts on 1 July

Numbers each date's month within its financial year, from 1 to 12.

Note: With the default 1 July start, July is month 1 and June is month 12. Dates may be one date or a range, and the result takes their shape. FinancialYearλ() labels the year and FinancialQuarterλ() the quarter.

Parameters:

Dates (required)

One or more dates, numeric or text. A blank cell returns a blank.

StartMonth (optional, Default = 7)

Month the financial year starts, one whole number from 1 to 12. Blank cells and empty text use 7.

```
=oz.FinancialMonthλ(DATE(2026,8,15))
```

The workbook help shows 2.

### oz.FinancialQuarterλ

oz.FinancialQuarterλ(Dates, [StartMonth])

Numbers each date's quarter within its financial year, so July to September is quarter 1 when the year starts on 1 July

Numbers each date's quarter within its financial year, from 1 to 4.

Note: Each quarter is 3 months counted from StartMonth. With the default 1 July start, July to September is quarter 1 and April to June is quarter 4. Dates may be one date or a range, and the result takes their shape.

Parameters:

Dates (required)

One or more dates, numeric or text. A blank cell returns a blank.

StartMonth (optional, Default = 7)

Month the financial year starts, one whole number from 1 to 12. Blank cells and empty text use 7.

```
=oz.FinancialQuarterλ(DATE(2026,11,15))
```

The workbook help shows 2.

### oz.RateAtDateλ

oz.RateAtDateλ(EffectiveDates, Rates, Dates)

Returns the rate in effect on each date from a table of effective dates and rates, refusing gaps, unsorted or repeated dates

Returns the rate in effect on each date from your table of effective dates and rates.

Note: Each rate applies from its effective date until the next one. Dates may be one date or a row or column of them, and the result takes their shape. A date before the first effective date has no rate in effect and returns #N/A. The table must be complete and in order, so instead of a result it returns a message when EffectiveDates and Rates differ in length or hold a blank or text entry, when the dates are not in ascending order, or when a date repeats. A text or blank date in Dates returns #VALUE!. The library ships no rate table: supply your own, with its source and the date you checked it. ScheduleRatesλ() lays rates across a timeline without these checks.

Parameters:

EffectiveDates (required)

A row or column of dates from which each rate applies, in ascending order.

Rates (required)

The rate that applies from each effective date, the same length as EffectiveDates.

Dates (required)

The date, or a row or column of dates, to look up.

```
=oz.RateAtDateλ(DATE(2026, {1;7;10}, 1), {0.04;0.045;0.05}, DATE(2026, 8, 15))
```

The workbook help shows 0.045.

### oz.DateDifλ

oz.DateDifλ(StartDate, EndDate, [Unit])

Whole years, months or days between two dates, and the remainders DATEDIF gets wrong

Whole years, months or days between two dates, and the remainders.

Note: Excel documents DATEDIF as a legacy compatibility function and warns its MD unit can return a negative or wrong day count. This counts a month as complete when EDATE() of the start date has arrived, so a month after 31 January is the last day of February, and takes every remainder from there. A reversed range or an unknown unit returns #NUM!.

Parameters:

StartDate (required)

The earlier date, numeric or text.

EndDate (required)

The later date, numeric or text.

Unit (optional, Default = D)

Y whole years, M whole months, D days, YM months left after the whole years, YD days left after the whole years, MD days left after the whole months.

```
=oz.DateDifλ(DATE(2026,1,31), DATE(2026,3,1), "MD")
```

The workbook help shows 1.

### oz.LeaseLiabilityλ

oz.LeaseLiabilityλ(Payments, Rate, [InAdvance])

Present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date

Present value of the lease payments that are not paid at the commencement date.

Note: AASB 16 paragraph 26 measures the lease liability at the present value of the lease payments not paid at the commencement date, discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease where that rate can be readily determined and at the lessee's incremental borrowing rate where it cannot. When InAdvance is TRUE, the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date and excluded from the liability. Add a payment made at or before commencement to the right-of-use asset cost instead. Rate is per period. Convert an effective annual rate with PeriodRateλ(AnnualRate, PeriodsPerYear). Divide a nominal annual rate by PeriodsPerYear only when its compounding periods match the payments. Include an amount expected to be payable under a residual value guarantee, or the exercise price of a purchase option, in the final period where paragraph 27 brings it into the lease payments. IRRλ() over the same cash flows gives an implicit rate per year; convert it to the rate per period, (1 + annual) ^ (1 / 12) - 1 for months, before passing it here. Arithmetic only: this does not determine the lease term, decide what is a lease payment, or decide whether the arrangement contains a lease. AASB 16 compilation checked 24 August 2026.

Parameters:

Payments (required)

One row or one column of lease payments, one per period, entered positive. Include the measurement-date payment first when InAdvance is TRUE.

Rate (required)

Discount rate per period, not per year.

InAdvance (optional, Default = FALSE)

TRUE when the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date.

```
=oz.LeaseLiabilityλ({100,100,100}, 0.05)
```

The workbook help shows 272.32.

### oz.LeaseScheduleλ

oz.LeaseScheduleλ(Payments, Rate, [InAdvance])

Unwinds an AASB 16 lease liability: opening, payment, interest and closing for each period

Unwinds an AASB 16 lease liability over its term.

Note: Returns four rows: opening liability, payment, interest, closing liability. When InAdvance is TRUE, the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date and is excluded from both the opening liability and the payment row. Each remaining payment follows one period of interest, so closing is opening plus interest less payment and the last closing balance is nil. The result has one fewer column for payments in advance; a sole measurement-date payment returns one zero column. The opening balance is LeaseLiabilityλ() on the same arguments. Pair this with ROUScheduleλ() for the asset that sits opposite it: the two together give the front-loaded expense profile AASB 16 produces. Arithmetic only, on the payments and rate you supply.

Parameters:

Payments (required)

One row or one column of lease payments, one per period, entered positive. Include the measurement-date payment first when InAdvance is TRUE.

Rate (required)

Discount rate per period, not per year.

InAdvance (optional, Default = FALSE)

TRUE when the first supplied payment is paid at the measurement date.

```
=oz.LeaseScheduleλ({100,100,100}, 0.05)
```

The workbook help shows 272.32, 185.94, 95.24; 100.00, 100.00, 100.00; 13.62, 9.30, 4.76; 185.94, 95.24, 0.00.

### oz.LeaseRemeasureλ

oz.LeaseRemeasureλ(RevisedPayments, Rate, CarryingLiability, CarryingROU, [InAdvance])

Remeasures an AASB 16 lease liability for revised payments and adjusts the right-of-use asset

Remeasures a lease liability for revised payments and adjusts the asset.

Note: Returns four rows: revised lease liability, adjustment, revised right-of-use asset, amount recognised in profit or loss. AASB 16 paragraph 42(b) remeasures the liability where future payments change because an index or a rate used to determine them has changed, and only when the cash flows change. Paragraph 43 keeps the discount rate unchanged for that revision, and uses a revised rate only where the change arises from a floating interest rate, so pass the original rate unless it is the rate itself that moved. When InAdvance is TRUE, the first revised payment is paid at the remeasurement date and excluded from the revised liability. Paragraph 39 takes the remeasurement to the right-of-use asset, and where that asset is reduced to nil any further reduction goes to profit or loss: row four carries that remainder, negative, because it is a credit. Arithmetic only. AASB 16 compilation checked 24 August 2026.

RevisedPayments (required)

Rate (required)

CarryingROU (required)

Right-of-use asset carried immediately before the remeasurement.

### oz.YearToDateλ

oz.YearToDateλ(Values, Dates, AsAt, [StartMonth])

Totals each row of values from the start of the financial year to an as-at date

Totals each row of Values from the start of AsAt's financial year to AsAt.

Note: A column counts when its date is on or after the first day of the financial year that contains AsAt, and on or before AsAt; a time of day is ignored. Date each column by the first day of its period, or by its last day and an AsAt at a period end. A part period counts in full, not pro rata. Values must hold numbers or blank cells, which count as 0; text and TRUE or FALSE return a message, and an error in any column shows. The result is one total for each row of Values. A financial year starting before 1 January 1900 returns #NUM!.

Parameters:

Dates (required)

A row of dates, one for each column of Values.

AsAt (required)

The one date the total runs to, inclusive.

StartMonth (optional, Default = 7)

### oz.HPScheduleλ

Amount financed at the start, in whole cents: the price less any deposit or trade-in.

Effective annual interest rate.

Periods (required)

Number of payments, a whole number of at least 1.

PeriodsPerYear (optional, Default = 12)

Payments a year: 52 weekly, 26 fortnightly, 12 monthly, 4 quarterly.

InAdvance (optional, Default = FALSE)

TRUE or 1 when each payment falls at the start of its period.

Balloon (optional, Default = 0)

### oz.CorkscrewRateλ

oz.CorkscrewRateλ(Opening, Rates, Flow1, [Flow2], [Flow3], [Flow4])

Create a corkscrew whose interest is charged on the average of each period's opening and closing balances and added to the balance

Create a corkscrew whose interest is charged on the average balance and added to it.

Note: Each period's interest is its rate times the average of its opening and closing balances, and the closing balance includes that interest. Each period is solved in closed form, without iteration or a circular reference: closing = (opening * (2 + rate) + 2 * flows) / (2 - rate). The rows are the opening balance, the flows, the interest and the closing balance. Every rate must be a number above -1 and below 2, Opening a single number and every flow a number or blank; anything else returns a message.

Note: All flows are added. To subtract a flow make it negative.

Parameters:

Opening (required)

First periods opening balance.

Rates (required)

The interest rate per period: one rate for every period, or one row with a rate for each, such as DayCountRateλ().

Flow1 (required)

First row (or array of rows) of numbers to include in period totals.

Flow2 (optional)

Second row (or array of rows) of numbers to include in period totals.

Flow3 (optional)

Third row (or array of rows) of numbers to include in period totals.

Flow4 (optional)

Fourth row (or array of rows) of numbers to include in period totals.

```
=oz.CorkscrewRateλ(1000, 0.01, {100,100})
```

The workbook help shows 1000.00, 1110.55; 100.00, 100.00; 10.55, 11.66; 1110.55, 1222.22.

### oz.PeriodRateλ

oz.PeriodRateλ(AnnualRate, [PeriodsPerYear])

Converts an effective annual rate to the equivalent rate per period, the rate the lease functions take

Converts an effective annual rate to the equivalent rate per period.

Note: (1 + AnnualRate) ^ (1 / PeriodsPerYear) - 1, so compounding the result PeriodsPerYear times gives the annual rate back. This is the rate per period that LeaseLiabilityλ(), LeaseScheduleλ() and LeaseRemeasureλ() take. It is for an effective annual rate. A nominal annual percentage rate that compounds monthly is already APR / 12 per month, so do not pass it here; EFFECT() turns one into the effective rate this takes. AnnualRateλ() is the inverse.

Parameters:

AnnualRate (required)

Effective annual rate, or a row or column of them.

PeriodsPerYear (optional, Default = 12)

Periods in a year: 12 for months, 4 for quarters, 1 for years.

```
=oz.PeriodRateλ(0.05)
```

The workbook help shows 0.004074.

### oz.AnnualRateλ

oz.AnnualRateλ(PeriodRate, [PeriodsPerYear])

Converts a rate per period to the effective annual rate, the inverse of PeriodRateλ

Converts a rate per period to the effective annual rate.

Note: (1 + PeriodRate) ^ PeriodsPerYear - 1, the inverse of PeriodRateλ(). Use it to state a rate per period, such as a lease rate solved per month, as the annual figure a reader expects.

Parameters:

PeriodRate (required)

Rate per period, or a row or column of them.

PeriodsPerYear (optional, Default = 12)

Periods in a year: 12 for months, 4 for quarters, 1 for years.

```
=oz.AnnualRateλ(0.01)
```

The workbook help shows 0.126825.

### oz.DayCountRateλ

oz.DayCountRateλ(Timeline, APR, [Convention], [EndDates])

Interest rate for each period of a timeline under a day count convention: 30/360, Actual/360, Actual/365 or Actual/Actual

Interest rate for each period of a timeline under a day count convention.

Note: Returns a row with one rate per timeline period, whichever way the timeline runs: APR multiplied by the days in the period and divided by the days in the year, as the convention counts them. Pass the result to DebtSculptVariableλ() or DebtSculptVariableLRVλ() as PeriodRates in place of a flat twelfth of the APR. With start dates each period runs from its date to the day before the next, and the last period takes its length from the one before it; with end dates each runs from the day after the previous date to its own, and the first period is the one inferred. A gap of 28 days or more is read as whole calendar months, a shorter one as days. 30/360 counts every month as 30 days on the European rule. Under Actual/Actual each calendar year uses its own length as the denominator (the ISDA rule), including periods spanning several years.

Parameters:

Timeline (required)

A row or column of period dates, at least two, evenly spaced.

APR (required)

Annual percentage rate, one value or one per period.

Convention (optional, Default = 3)

1 = 30/360, 2 = Actual/360, 3 = Actual/365, 4 = Actual/Actual. Any other number is #VALUE!.

EndDates (optional, Default = FALSE)

TRUE, or a number other than 0, when the timeline shows period end dates rather than start dates.

```
=oz.DayCountRateλ(EDATE(DATE(2026,7,1), {0,1,2}), 0.073)
```

The workbook help shows 0.0062, 0.0062, 0.0060.

# Ozzit Ratios functions: Excel LAMBDA reference

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/ozzit/functions/ratios/

> Parameters and worked examples for 48 Ozzit Ratios Excel LAMBDA functions: liquidity, gearing, margin, return, market and working capital ratios.

# Ozzit Ratios functions

The 48 Ratios formulas cover liquidity, gearing, margin, return, market and working capital ratios. Each entry gives what the workbook’s own help supplies: the signature, parameters, notes and worked examples.

Release v3.8.0. Read from the released Ratios formula source, which the workbook compiles.

By Ryan Duguid. Published 20 October 2026. Last reviewed 20 October 2026.

## Using these functions

Each named formula is a native Excel LAMBDA in the free Ozzit workbook, or one of its 5 help tables. It needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 or later. Enter a call in a cell of the workbook, or copy the definition from its name manager into your own model. Leave room for any spilled result.

The text below is the help each function carries in the v3.8.0 workbook. The workbook remains the authority, and a calculation does not decide an accounting treatment. Download the workbook and check its hash.

### oz.ATOTurnoverλ

oz.ATOTurnoverλ(OtherSales, TotalBusinessIncome)

Turnover as the ATO small business benchmarks measure it: other sales unless under half of total business income

Turnover excluding GST, the denominator of every ATO tax return benchmark ratio.

Note: Returns OtherSales, unless it is zero, blank or less than half of TotalBusinessIncome, when it returns TotalBusinessIncome instead. That is the ATO's rule. OtherSales is the other sales of goods and services amount on the return. Where total business income is blank or incomplete, the ATO adds up the business income items it lists for the return type: pass that total as TotalBusinessIncome. Pass both amounts excluding GST. Text in either argument returns #VALUE!. Arithmetic only: the reviewer decides what belongs in each amount. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

Parameters:

OtherSales (required)

Other sales of goods and services, excluding GST.

TotalBusinessIncome (required)

Total business income, excluding GST.

```
=oz.ATOTurnoverλ(480000, 500000)
```

The workbook help shows 480000.

```
=oz.ATOTurnoverλ(200000, 500000)
```

The workbook help shows 500000.

### oz.ATOBenchmarkRatioλ

oz.ATOBenchmarkRatioλ(Amount, Turnover)

ATO tax return benchmark ratio: an amount divided by turnover, as for rent or motor vehicle expenses to turnover

ATO tax return benchmark ratio: Amount / Turnover.

Note: The ATO's basic formula for a tax return benchmark ratio, and the whole of its rent expenses to turnover and motor vehicle expenses to turnover ratios: pass the rent or motor vehicle expenses amount from the return. Returns a fraction; format it as a percentage, as the ATO's figure is the same quotient multiplied by 100. Take Turnover from ATOTurnoverλ(). Use ATOTotalExpensesRatioλ(), ATOCostOfSalesRatioλ() and ATOLabourRatioλ() for the 3 ratios whose amounts the ATO adjusts. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

Parameters:

Amount (required)

The expense amount, excluding GST.

Turnover (required)

Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

```
=oz.ATOBenchmarkRatioλ(24000, 480000)
```

The workbook help shows 5%.

### oz.ATOTotalExpensesRatioλ

oz.ATOTotalExpensesRatioλ(TotalExpenses, Turnover, [AssociatePayments])

ATO total expenses to turnover: total expenses less payments to associated persons, over turnover

ATO total expenses to turnover benchmark ratio.

Note: (TotalExpenses - AssociatePayments) / Turnover. The ATO deducts payments to associated persons from total expenses before dividing. Where total expenses is blank or incomplete, it adds up the expense items it lists for the return type: pass that total as TotalExpenses. OperatingRatioλ() gives the same quotient only when its expenses already exclude those payments and its net sales equal this Turnover. Returns a fraction, as ATOBenchmarkRatioλ() does. An omitted or blank AssociatePayments counts as 0. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

Parameters:

TotalExpenses (required)

Total expenses from the return, excluding GST.

Turnover (required)

Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

AssociatePayments (optional, Default = 0)

Payments to associated persons.

```
=oz.ATOTotalExpensesRatioλ(410000, 480000, 30000)
```

The workbook help shows 0.7917.

### oz.ATOCostOfSalesRatioλ

oz.ATOCostOfSalesRatioλ(CostOfSales, Turnover, [IncludedWages])

ATO cost of sales to turnover, excluding salary and wages included in cost of sales

ATO cost of sales to turnover benchmark ratio, excluding labour.

Note: (CostOfSales - IncludedWages) / Turnover. The ATO's cost of sales excludes salary and wages: where the return's total salary and wages code is C, meaning they are included in cost of sales, it deducts the total salary and wages expenses. Pass that total as IncludedWages only when the code is C, and leave it out otherwise. GrossMarginλ() is a different measure: it keeps wages in cost of sales. Returns a fraction, as ATOBenchmarkRatioλ() does. An omitted or blank IncludedWages counts as 0. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

Parameters:

CostOfSales (required)

Cost of sales from the return, excluding GST.

Turnover (required)

Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

IncludedWages (optional, Default = 0)

Total salary and wages expenses, only when the return's code is C.

```
=oz.ATOCostOfSalesRatioλ(260000, 480000, 60000)
```

The workbook help shows 0.4167.

### oz.ATOLabourRatioλ

oz.ATOLabourRatioλ(SalaryWages, Contractors, Turnover, [AssociatePayments], [W1])

ATO labour to turnover: salary and wages plus contractors less payments to associated persons, over turnover

ATO labour to turnover benchmark ratio.

Note: (Wages + Contractors - AssociatePayments) / Turnover, where Wages is SalaryWages, or W1 when W1 is greater. The ATO adds total salary and wages expenses to contractor, subcontractor and commission expenses and deducts payments to associated persons. Where the activity statements' label W1 (total salary, wages and other payments) for the year exceeds the return's salary and wages, it uses W1. Returns a fraction, as ATOBenchmarkRatioλ() does. An omitted or blank AssociatePayments or W1 counts as 0. Turnover of 0 returns #DIV/0!. Arithmetic only. ATO benchmark ratio calculations checked 19 October 2026.

Parameters:

SalaryWages (required)

Total salary and wages expenses from the return.

Contractors (required)

Contractor, subcontractor and commission expenses.

Turnover (required)

Turnover excluding GST, for example from ATOTurnoverλ().

AssociatePayments (optional, Default = 0)

Payments to associated persons.

W1 (optional, Default = 0)

The year's total at activity statement label W1.

```
=oz.ATOLabourRatioλ(90000, 20000, 480000, 10000, 95000)
```

The workbook help shows 0.21875.

### oz.ReceivableDaysλ

oz.ReceivableDaysλ(Receivables, Sales, [Days])

Receivable days, or days sales outstanding (DSO): Receivables / Sales x Days

Receivable days, or days sales outstanding (DSO): the days of sales not yet collected.

Note: Receivables / Sales * Days. Days is the number of days the Sales figure covers: 365 with a year's sales, 90 with the last three months' sales for a rolling figure, or a month's days with that month's sales. Pass closing receivables, or the average of opening and closing for an average-balance figure. Put the balance and the sales on the same basis: where one includes GST and the other does not, adjust the inputs first, because this function makes no GST adjustment. Sales of 0 returns #DIV/0!, and Days of 0 or less returns #NUM!.

Parameters:

Receivables (required)

Trade receivables: the closing balance, or the average of opening and closing.

Sales (required)

Credit sales over the same Days.

Days (optional, Default = 365)

Days the Sales figure covers.

```
=oz.ReceivableDaysλ(125000, 1200000)
```

The workbook help shows 38.0208.

```
=oz.ReceivableDaysλ(125000, 330000, 90)
```

The workbook help shows 34.0909.

### oz.PayableDaysλ

oz.PayableDaysλ(Payables, Purchases, [Days])

Payable days, or days payable outstanding (DPO): Payables / Purchases x Days

Payable days, or days payable outstanding (DPO): the days of purchases not yet paid.

Note: Payables / Purchases * Days. Days is the number of days the Purchases figure covers, as for ReceivableDaysλ(). Credit purchases are the matching flow; cost of sales is the common substitute where purchases are not reported. Pass closing payables, or the average of opening and closing. Put the balance and the purchases on the same basis: where one includes GST and the other does not, adjust the inputs first, because this function makes no GST adjustment. Purchases of 0 returns #DIV/0!, and Days of 0 or less returns #NUM!.

Parameters:

Payables (required)

Trade payables: the closing balance, or the average of opening and closing.

Purchases (required)

Credit purchases, or cost of sales, over the same Days.

Days (optional, Default = 365)

Days the Purchases figure covers.

```
=oz.PayableDaysλ(64000, 780000)
```

The workbook help shows 29.9487.

### oz.WIPDaysλ

oz.WIPDaysλ(WIP, RelatedFlow, [Days])

Work in progress days: WIP / RelatedFlow x Days, with both on one valuation basis

Work in progress days: the days of work done but not yet billed or completed.

Note: WIP / RelatedFlow * Days. WIP and RelatedFlow must use the same valuation basis: fee revenue with WIP at charge-out value, as a professional services firm records it, or cost of sales with WIP at cost. Days is the number of days the RelatedFlow figure covers. WIP days plus ReceivableDaysλ() gives the lock-up days a services firm tracks. RelatedFlow of 0 returns #DIV/0!, and Days of 0 or less returns #NUM!.

Parameters:

WIP (required)

Work in progress: the closing balance, or the average of opening and closing.

RelatedFlow (required)

Fee revenue or cost of sales over the same Days, on the valuation basis of WIP.

Days (optional, Default = 365)

Days the RelatedFlow figure covers.

```
=oz.WIPDaysλ(42000, 510000)
```

The workbook help shows 30.0588.

### oz.CashConversionCycleλ

oz.CashConversionCycleλ(InventoryDays, ReceivableDays, PayableDays, [WIPDays])

Cash conversion cycle in days: inventory days + WIP days + receivable days - payable days

Cash conversion cycle: the days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers.

Note: InventoryDays + WIPDays + ReceivableDays - PayableDays. Pass day counts, for example from DSIλ(), ReceivableDaysλ(), PayableDaysλ() and WIPDaysλ(), with every component on the same period basis. For a shorter window, pass that window's days as the Days argument of each component. A negative result means suppliers are paid after customers pay. An omitted or blank WIPDays counts as 0. Pass WIPDays only where WIP is not already in the inventory behind InventoryDays, or it is counted twice.

Parameters:

InventoryDays (required)

Inventory days, for example from DSIλ().

ReceivableDays (required)

Receivable days, for example from ReceivableDaysλ().

PayableDays (required)

Payable days, for example from PayableDaysλ().

WIPDays (optional, Default = 0)

Work in progress days, for example from WIPDaysλ().

```
=oz.CashConversionCycleλ(40.8949, 38.0208, 29.9487)
```

The workbook help shows 48.967.

# Ozzit Utilities functions: Excel LAMBDA reference

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/ozzit/functions/utilities/

> Parameters and worked examples for 17 Ozzit Utilities Excel LAMBDA functions: standalone copies of the Essentials functions, each with a U suffix.

# Ozzit Utilities functions

The 17 Utilities formulas cover standalone copies of the Essentials functions, each with a U suffix. Each entry gives what the workbook’s own help supplies: the signature, parameters, notes and worked examples.

Release v3.8.0. Read from the released Utilities formula source, which the workbook compiles.

By Ryan Duguid. Published 20 October 2026. Last reviewed 20 October 2026.

## Using these functions

Each named formula is a native Excel LAMBDA in the free Ozzit workbook, or one of its 5 help tables. It needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 or later. Enter a call in a cell of the workbook, or copy the definition from its name manager into your own model. Leave room for any spilled result.

The text below is the help each function carries in the v3.8.0 workbook. The workbook remains the authority, and a calculation does not decide an accounting treatment. Download the workbook and check its hash.

oz.CountCUλ( Text, Characters)

Count occurrences of character(s) in a string

Count how many of one or more characters are in a string.

Parameters:

Characters (required)

A single character, or CSV of characters to find in Text NOTE! Case sensitive. A single character is taken as itself, so a comma works

=oz.CountCUλ( "Mary had a little lamb", "a,b")
```

### oz.IsBetweenUλ

oz.IsBetweenUλ( Value, Low, Hi, [Inclusive])

Determine if a value is between a lower and upper limit

Determine if a value is between a lower and upper limit.

Parameters:

Value (required)

A value or array of values to compare.

Low (required)

The lower limit that the value must be greater than

Hi (required)

The higher limit that the value must be less than

Inclusive (optional)

If set to TRUE (default) the value can be equal to Low and/or Hi

```
=IsBetweenUλ(1, 2, 4)
```

The workbook help shows FALSE.

```
=IsBetweenUλ(2, 2, 4)
```

The workbook help shows TRUE.

```
=IsBetweenUλ(2, 2, 4, FALSE)
```

The workbook help shows FALSE.

Previous name: nabla.u.IsBetweenλ.

Determine if a value is one of a list of items.

Note: The comparison is exact and case-insensitive; * and? are ordinary characters.

Parameters:

A value or array of values to compare.

List (required)

A list of values to check: a row, a column or a grid.

```

The workbook help shows TRUE.

Previous name: nabla.u.IsInListλ.

# Ozzit Debt functions: Excel LAMBDA reference

Source: https://duguid.com.au/tools/ozzit/functions/debt/

> Parameters and worked examples for 5 Ozzit Debt Excel LAMBDA functions: debt amortisation and fixed or variable DSCR debt sculpting.

# Ozzit Debt functions

The 5 Debt formulas cover debt amortisation and fixed or variable DSCR debt sculpting. Each entry gives what the workbook’s own help supplies: the signature, parameters, notes and worked examples.

Release v3.8.0. Read from the released Debt formula source, which the workbook compiles.

By Ryan Duguid. Published 20 October 2026. Last reviewed 20 October 2026.

## Using these functions

Each named formula is a native Excel LAMBDA in the free Ozzit workbook, or one of its 5 help tables. It needs Microsoft 365 or Excel 2024 or later. Enter a call in a cell of the workbook, or copy the definition from its name manager into your own model. Leave room for any spilled result.

The text below is the help each function carries in the v3.8.0 workbook. The workbook remains the authority, and a calculation does not decide an accounting treatment. Download the workbook and check its hash.

## All 5 functions

- oz.AmortiseBλ
- oz.DebtSculptFixedλ
- oz.DebtSculptVariableLRVλ
- oz.DebtSculptVariableλ
- oz.InterestLRVλ

### oz.AmortiseBλ

oz.AmortiseBλ(Principal, APR, Term, ModelPeriods, [StartPeriod], [MonthsPerPeriod])

Creates an amortisation schedule for a debt/loan across a model's periods

Creates an amortisation schedule for a debt/loan across a model's periods.

Parameters:

Principal (required)

Principal opening balance.

APR (required)

Annual percentage rate.

Term (required)

Number of periods to pay off the debt.

ModelPeriods (required)

Number of model periods.

StartPeriod (optional)

Period when the debt is issued. Defaults to 1.

MonthsPerPeriod (optional)

Number of months in each period. Defaults to 1.

Row contents:

- Opening Balance
- Interest Portion
- Repayment
- Closing Balance
- Principal Portion

```
=oz.AmortiseBλ(10000, 3%, 48, 60)
```

The workbook help shows 5 rows, 60 cols.

Previous name: nabla.debt.Amortiseλ.

### oz.DebtSculptFixedλ

oz.DebtSculptFixedλ([OpeningBalance], Debt, CFADS, DSCR, APR, [MonthsPerPeriod])

Creates a debt sculpting schedule where APR and DSCR are fixed for all periods

Creates a Debt Sculpting schedule where APR and DSCR are fixed for all periods

Parameters:

OpeningBalance (optional)

Model's debt on opening. Defaults to 0

Debt (required)

One row of new debt, at least two periods. Every period input must have this same width

CFADS (required)

A row of Cash Flow Available for Debt Service in each period

DSCR (required)

Debt Service Coverage Ratio, one number for all periods

APR (required)

Interest's Annual Percentage Rate, one number for all periods

MonthsPerPeriod (optional)

Defaults to one month per period.

Suggested row IDs:

- Debt opening balance
- Interest on Principal Balance
- Debt service (interest and principal)
- Debt closing balance

```
=oz.DebtSculptFixedλ(, {1000,0,0}, {300,300,300}, 1.2, 6%, 12)
```

The workbook help shows 4 rows, 3 cols.

Previous name: nabla.debt.DebtSculptFixedλ.

### oz.DebtSculptVariableLRVλ

oz.DebtSculptVariableLRVλ([OpeningBalance], Debt, CFADS, DSCR, APR, [MonthsPerPeriod], [PeriodRates])

Creates a debt sculpting schedule where APR and DSCR are set for each period, with interest charged on the average balance

Creates a Debt Sculpting schedule where APR and DSCR are set for each period. Interest is charged on the average balance over the period, the method presented by Lance Rubin, and the principal repaid is what the cash available for debt service leaves after that interest.

Parameters:

OpeningBalance (optional)

Model's debt on opening. Defaults to 0

Debt (required)

One row of new debt, at least two periods. Every period input must have this same width

CFADS (required)

A row of numeric Cash Flow Available for Debt Service in each period. Blank cells, text and logical values are rejected. Negative values supply no cash for debt service; existing debt still capitalises unpaid interest

DSCR (required)

A row of Debt Service Coverage Ratios, one per period

APR

(Required unless PeriodRates is given) A row of Interest's Annual Percentage Rates, one per period. Each period charges APR / 12 * MonthsPerPeriod

MonthsPerPeriod (optional)

Defaults to one month per period. Ignored when PeriodRates is given

PeriodRates (optional)

A row of interest rates per period, one per period, such as DayCountRateλ() returns for a day count convention. When given, interest uses these rates and APR and MonthsPerPeriod are ignored. A blank cell or range counts as not given

Suggested row IDs:

- Debt opening balance
- Interest on Principal Balance
- Principal repayments
- Debt closing balance

```
=oz.DebtSculptVariableLRVλ(, {1000,0,0}, {300,300,300}, {1.2,1.2,1.2}, {0.06,0.06,0.06}, 12)
```

The workbook help shows 4 rows, 3 cols.

Previous name: nabla.debt.DebtSculptVariableLRVλ.

### oz.DebtSculptVariableλ

oz.DebtSculptVariableλ([OpeningBalance], Debt, CFADS, DSCR, APR, [MonthsPerPeriod], [PeriodRates])

Creates a debt sculpting schedule where APR and DSCR are set for each period

Creates a Debt Sculpting schedule where APR and DSCR are set for each period

Parameters:

OpeningBalance (optional)

Model's debt on opening. Defaults to 0

Debt (required)

One row of new debt, at least two periods. Every period input must have this same width

CFADS (required)

A row of Cash Flow Available for Debt Service in each period

DSCR (required)

A row of Debt Service Coverage Ratios, one per period

APR

(Required unless PeriodRates is given) A row of Interest's Annual Percentage Rates, one per period. Each period charges APR / 12 * MonthsPerPeriod

MonthsPerPeriod (optional)

Defaults to one month per period. Ignored when PeriodRates is given

PeriodRates (optional)

A row of interest rates per period, one per period, such as DayCountRateλ() returns for a day count convention. When given, interest uses these rates and APR and MonthsPerPeriod are ignored. A blank cell or range counts as not given

Suggested row IDs:

- Debt opening balance
- Interest on Principal Balance
- Debt service (interest and principal)
- Debt closing balance

```
=oz.DebtSculptVariableλ(, {1000,0,0}, {300,300,300}, {1.2,1.2,1.2}, {0.06,0.06,0.06}, 12)
```

The workbook help shows 4 rows, 3 cols.

Previous name: nabla.debt.DebtSculptVariableλ.

### oz.InterestLRVλ

oz.InterestLRVλ(CFADS, DSCR, Principal, InterestRate)

Calculates debt sculpting interest on the average balance over the period, the method presented by Lance Rubin

Calculates debt sculpting interest using the method presented by Lance Rubin. Interest is charged on the average balance over the period, with the principal repaid capped at the principal outstanding. The average balance depends on the interest and the interest on the average balance, which is solved in closed form rather than by iteration.

Parameters:

CFADS (required)

Cash Flow Available for Debt Service for this period

DSCR (required)

Debt Service Coverage Ratio for this period

Principal (required)

Principal balance for this period

InterestRate (required)

Interest rate for this period (eg. APR/Days in this year * Days in this period)

```
=oz.InterestLRVλ( 6666.37, 3.50, 90000, 3%/12)
```

The workbook help shows 222.90.

Previous name: nabla.debt.InterestLRVλ.
